title: Check ACB System Statistics (robot faults, system faults, cycle time, tipping station bag counts) on the ACB System Statistics screen
summary: Open the OptiSweep Tipper HMI/WebVisu “ACB System” screen, press “STATISTICS” to view the “ACB System Statistics” screen, and verify the displayed ACB metrics: number of robot faults, number of system faults, cycle time, and tipping station bag counts.
when_to_use: Use when you need a quick, on-screen view of current Automated Carton Buffer (ACB) statistics—robot faults, system faults, cycle time, and tipping station bag counts—on the live OptiSweep HMI.

steps.title: Open ACB System Statistics from the ACB System screen
steps.instruction: On the Tipper HMI/WebVisu/VISU, open the “ACB System” screen, then press the “STATISTICS” button to access the “ACB System Statistics” screen.
steps.purpose: Access the live ACB System Statistics screen that contains the required ACB metrics.
steps.expected_result: The “ACB System Statistics” screen opens successfully.
steps.healthy_condition: The “ACB System Statistics” screen is displayed (not an error page or blank/unresponsive screen).
steps.failure_condition: Pressing “STATISTICS” does not open the “ACB System Statistics” screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: STATISTICS button does not open the ACB System Statistics screen

actions.label: Press STATISTICS
actions.exact_action: Press STATISTICS on the "ACB System" screen to access this screen.

steps.title: Locate and record the four ACB metrics on the ACB System Statistics screen
steps.instruction: On the “ACB System Statistics” screen, locate the displayed values for: (1) number of robot faults, (2) number of system faults, (3) cycle time, and (4) tipping station bag counts.
steps.purpose: Capture the current values shown for the required ACB statistics.
steps.expected_result: All four metric areas are visible and you can read the displayed values for robot faults, system faults, cycle time, and tipping station bag counts.
steps.healthy_condition: Each of the four metrics is present on the screen with a readable numeric/statistical value.
steps.failure_condition: One or more of the four metrics are missing/blank when the screen is open.
stop_or_escalate_if: One or more of the four metrics (robot faults, system faults, cycle time, tipping station bag counts) are missing/blank

actions.label: Read metric values
actions.exact_action: Locate and record the displayed values for: number of robot faults, number of system faults, cycle time, and tipping station bag counts.

steps.title: Confirm the ACB System Statistics screen is populated with numeric/statistical values
steps.instruction: Verify that the “ACB System Statistics” screen shows numeric/statistical values (not blank/missing) for all four metrics: robot faults, system faults, cycle time, and tipping station bag counts.
steps.purpose: Ensure the screen is providing current statistical data rather than blank/missing fields.
steps.expected_result: The four metrics are populated with numeric/statistical values.
steps.healthy_condition: No metric field is blank/missing; all four values are displayed.
steps.failure_condition: Any of the four metrics are blank/missing.
stop_or_escalate_if: One or more of the four metrics are missing/blank when the screen is open

actions.label: Check for blanks
actions.exact_action: Confirm the screen is populated with numeric/statistical values (not blank/missing) for the four metrics.

title: Perform Daily Maintenance Checklist: Operator Station, Chute, Stacklights, Guards, and QR Codes
summary: Complete the daily inspection items to confirm the Operator Station controller/chute are intact and that stacklights, guards, and QR codes are in good condition.
when_to_use: Use this daily, on-site inspection checklist to verify the Operator Station controller, Operator Station chute, stacklights, guards/attaching hardware, and QR codes (floor and racks) are in acceptable condition before operation.

steps.title: Record inspection date, inspected by, and unit inspected
steps.instruction: On the Daily Maintenance Checklist form, record the Inspection Date, Inspected By, and Unit Inspected.
steps.purpose: Ensure the daily checklist is properly logged for traceability.
steps.expected_result: The form has entries for Inspection Date, Inspected By, and Unit Inspected.
steps.healthy_condition: All three fields are completed (no blanks).
steps.failure_condition: Any of the three fields are missing or left blank.

actions.label: Fill checklist header fields
actions.exact_action: Record Inspection Date, Inspected By, and Unit Inspected on the Daily Maintenance Checklist form.

steps.title: Inspect the Operator Station controller for damage
steps.instruction: Visually inspect the Operator Station controller for damage.
steps.purpose: Confirm the controller is intact and safe to use.
steps.expected_result: No damage is observed on the Operator Station controller.
steps.healthy_condition: Controller appears intact with no visible damage.
steps.failure_condition: Damage is observed on the Operator Station controller.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the controller shows damage, stop the checklist and escalate for corrective action.

actions.label: Visual inspection: controller
actions.exact_action: Inspect the Operator Station controller for damage.

steps.title: Ensure the Operator Station chute is free of debris
steps.instruction: Visually check the Operator Station chute area and ensure it is free of debris.
steps.purpose: Prevent obstruction or unsafe conditions caused by debris in the chute area.
steps.expected_result: No debris is present in the Operator Station chute.
steps.healthy_condition: Chute interior/entry area is clear of debris.
steps.failure_condition: Debris is present in the Operator Station chute.
stop_or_escalate_if: If debris is found, stop the checklist and escalate for corrective action.

actions.label: Visual inspection: chute
actions.exact_action: Ensure the Operator Station chute is free of debris.

steps.title: Verify stacklights are operational
steps.instruction: Verify the stacklights are operational.
steps.purpose: Confirm stacklight indication is functioning for safe/visible status signaling.
steps.expected_result: Stacklights are operational (as determined by your site’s operational check for stacklights).
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklights indicate normal/operational condition (no failure observed).
steps.failure_condition: Stacklights are not operational.
stop_or_escalate_if: If stacklights are not operational, stop the checklist and escalate for corrective action.

actions.label: Check stacklights
actions.exact_action: Verify stacklights are operational.

steps.title: Inspect guards and verify attaching hardware is secure
steps.instruction: Inspect the guards and verify the attaching hardware is secure.
steps.purpose: Ensure guards are properly installed and secured to prevent hazards.
steps.expected_result: Guards are intact and attaching hardware is secure.
steps.healthy_condition: No loose/incorrectly secured attaching hardware is observed.
steps.failure_condition: Attaching hardware is not secure or guards appear damaged/incorrectly secured.
stop_or_escalate_if: If guards or attaching hardware are damaged/not secure, stop the checklist and escalate for corrective action.

actions.label: Inspect guards & hardware
actions.exact_action: Inspect the guards and verify attaching hardware is secure.

steps.title: Inspect all QR codes on the floor for damage or peeling
steps.instruction: Inspect all QR codes on the floor for damage or peeling.
steps.purpose: Ensure floor QR codes are readable and not physically degraded.
steps.expected_result: All floor QR codes show no damage and no peeling.
steps.healthy_condition: QR code labels appear intact (no peeling/damage observed).
steps.failure_condition: Any floor QR code shows damage or peeling.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any floor QR code is damaged or peeling, stop the checklist and escalate for corrective action.

actions.label: Inspect floor QR codes
actions.exact_action: Inspect all QR codes on the floor for damage or peeling.

steps.title: Inspect all QR codes on the racks for damage or peeling
steps.instruction: Inspect all QR codes on the racks for damage or peeling.
steps.purpose: Ensure rack QR codes are readable and not physically degraded.
steps.expected_result: All rack QR codes show no damage and no peeling.
steps.healthy_condition: QR code labels appear intact (no peeling/damage observed).
steps.failure_condition: Any rack QR code shows damage or peeling.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any rack QR code is damaged or peeling, stop the checklist and escalate for corrective action.

actions.label: Inspect rack QR codes
actions.exact_action: Inspect all QR codes on the racks for damage or peeling.

title: Perform Daily Preventive Maintenance Inspection on OptiSweep Hospital Station(s)
summary: Perform a daily inspection of each OptiSweep hospital station to verify the barcode scanner is operational, the stacklight is operational, and the tabletop is free of debris.
when_to_use: Use this daily checklist to verify each hospital station is safe to operate by confirming (1) barcode scanner operational status, (2) stacklight operational status, and (3) tabletop is free of debris.

steps.title: Inspect the barcode scanner at each hospital station
steps.instruction: For each OptiSweep hospital station, visually inspect the hospital station barcode scanner and confirm it is operational.
steps.purpose: Confirm the hospital station barcode scanner is operational as required for safe operation.
steps.expected_result: For the station being inspected, the barcode scanner is operational.
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode scanner is operational (pass condition per daily PM checklist).
steps.failure_condition: Barcode scanner is not operational.
stop_or_escalate_if: Barcode scanner issue is observed

actions.label: Visual check barcode scanner operational
actions.exact_action: Inspect each hospital station for the following: The barcode scanner is operational.

steps.title: Inspect the hospital station stacklight
steps.instruction: For each OptiSweep hospital station, inspect the stacklight and confirm it is operational.
steps.purpose: Confirm the hospital station stacklight is operational as required for safe operation.
steps.expected_result: For the station being inspected, the stacklight is operational.
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight is operational (pass condition per daily PM checklist).
steps.failure_condition: Stacklight is not operational.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stacklight is not operational

actions.label: Visual check stacklight operational
actions.exact_action: Inspect each hospital station for the following: The stacklight is operational.

steps.title: Inspect the hospital station tabletop for debris
steps.instruction: For each OptiSweep hospital station, inspect the tabletop and remove/confirm absence of debris.
steps.purpose: Confirm the tabletop is free of debris to support safe operation.
steps.expected_result: For the station being inspected, the tabletop is free of debris.
steps.healthy_condition: No debris present on the tabletop.
steps.failure_condition: Debris is present on the tabletop.
stop_or_escalate_if: Debris is present on the tabletop

actions.label: Visual check tabletop debris
actions.exact_action: Inspect each hospital station for the following: The tabletop is free of debris.

steps.title: Stop inspection and escalate if any required item fails
steps.instruction: If any barcode scanner issue is observed, if the stacklight is not operational, or if debris is present on the tabletop, stop the inspection and escalate to maintenance support.
steps.purpose: Prevent unsafe operation by escalating when any daily PM checklist item fails.
steps.expected_result: Inspection is stopped for the failing condition and maintenance support is engaged.
steps.healthy_condition: No failures observed; inspection can continue to the next station.
steps.failure_condition: At least one of: barcode scanner not operational, stacklight not operational, debris present on tabletop.
stop_or_escalate_if: Barcode scanner issue is observed
Stacklight is not operational
Debris is present on the tabletop

actions.label: Escalate to maintenance support
actions.exact_action: If any barcode scanner issue is observed, if the stacklight is not operational, or if debris is present on the tabletop, stop the inspection and escalate to maintenance support.

title: Perform Daily Preventive Maintenance Inspection on OptiSweep Operator Station
summary: Perform a daily operator-station inspection to verify the OptiSweep operator station is safe to operate by checking (1) controller condition, (2) stacklight operation, and (3) that the chute is free of debris such as stuck labels.
when_to_use: Use this daily checklist to verify the operator station is safe to operate by confirming controller condition, stacklight operation, and that the chute is free of debris (e.g., stuck labels).

steps.title: Inspect the operator station controller area for damage
steps.instruction: Go to the OptiSweep operator station and visually inspect the controller area for damage.
steps.purpose: Confirm the operator station controller is not damaged before operation.
steps.expected_result: No damage to the controller is observed.
steps.healthy_condition: Controller area shows no visible damage.
steps.failure_condition: Damage to the controller is observed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Controller damage is observed.

actions.label: Visual inspection of controller area
actions.exact_action: Visually inspect the controller area for damage.

steps.title: Check that the operator station stacklights are operational
steps.instruction: Check that the operator station stacklights are operational by observing that the stacklights function.
steps.purpose: Confirm stacklights function so operators receive correct visual status indications.
steps.expected_result: Stacklights are operational.
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklights function when checked.
steps.failure_condition: Stacklights are not operational.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stacklights are not operational.

actions.label: Observe stacklight operation
actions.exact_action: Observe that the stacklights function.

steps.title: Inspect the chute area for debris (including stuck labels)
steps.instruction: Inspect the chute area for debris, specifically looking for stuck labels.
steps.purpose: Ensure the chute is clear so packages can move without obstruction.
steps.expected_result: Chute is free of debris, including no stuck labels.
steps.healthy_condition: No debris/stuck labels are present in the chute area.
steps.failure_condition: Debris/stuck labels are found in the chute.
stop_or_escalate_if: Debris/stuck labels are found in the chute.

actions.label: Visual inspection of chute for debris
actions.exact_action: Inspect the chute area for debris, specifically looking for stuck labels.

steps.title: Stop the inspection and escalate if any checklist item fails
steps.instruction: If any controller damage is observed, or if stacklights are not operational, or if debris/stuck labels are found in the chute, stop the daily inspection and escalate to maintenance support.
steps.purpose: Prevent unsafe operation when inspection criteria are not met.
steps.expected_result: Inspection is stopped and maintenance support is escalated when any failure condition is found.
steps.healthy_condition: All three inspection items pass (no controller damage, stacklights operational, chute free of debris/stuck labels).
steps.failure_condition: Any of the three inspection items fails and escalation is not performed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Controller damage is observed.
Stacklights are not operational.
Debris/stuck labels are found in the chute.

actions.label: Escalate to maintenance support
actions.exact_action: Stop the daily inspection and escalate to maintenance support.

title: Check Hospital HMI Alarms List and Timestamp for Active Alarms
summary: Use the Hospital HMI Alarms screen to identify active alarm entries and their timestamps. Then match the Alarm Text/ID to the manual’s Alarms and Corrective Actions table to determine the documented Cause and Corrective Action for the specific alarm.
when_to_use: When the system is showing an alarm/fault condition at the Hospital station and you need to identify the specific active alarm text/ID and its timestamp so the correct documented corrective action can be applied.

steps.title: Open the Hospital HMI Alarms screen
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, navigate to the Alarms screen (Hospital HMI Alarms Screen, Figure 4-42).
steps.purpose: Get to the screen that lists all alarms and their timestamps for the Hospital station.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI Alarms screen is displayed and shows a list of alarms along with a time stamp.
steps.healthy_condition: A visible alarms list is present and each alarm entry has an associated time stamp.
steps.failure_condition: The Alarms screen shows no alarm entries while an alarm/fault condition is expected.
stop_or_escalate_if: Alarm list is empty when an alarm condition is expected.

actions.label: Navigate to Alarms screen
actions.exact_action: Open the Hospital HMI and navigate to the Alarms screen (Figure 4-42: Hospital HMI Alarms Screen).

steps.title: Verify alarms list and timestamps are present
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI Alarms screen, verify that the alarms list rows are present and that each alarm entry includes a time stamp.
steps.purpose: Confirm the screen is populated so you can identify the active alarm(s) and their timestamps.
steps.expected_result: The screen shows active alarm entries and a time stamp for each entry.
steps.healthy_condition: Each visible alarm row includes a timestamp value.
steps.failure_condition: Alarm entries are missing or timestamps are not shown for entries.

actions.label: Check alarms list rows and timestamp column/field
actions.exact_action: Verify the screen shows a list of alarms and a time stamp for each alarm entry.

steps.title: Record the active alarm Alarm Text and ID
steps.instruction: For the alarm(s) currently relevant to the issue, record the Alarm Text and the associated ID from the alarms list entry.
steps.purpose: Capture the exact Alarm Text and associated ID so the correct row in Table 4-23 can be matched.
steps.expected_result: You have the Alarm Text and ID for the active alarm entry/entries that correspond to the observed system condition.
steps.healthy_condition: Alarm Text and ID are captured for each active alarm you intend to troubleshoot.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot determine the Alarm Text and/or ID from the alarms list entries.

actions.label: Record Alarm Text and ID
actions.exact_action: For the alarm(s) currently relevant to the issue, record the Alarm Text and the associated ID from the alarms list entry.

steps.title: Match Alarm Text/ID to Table 4-23 to determine Cause and Corrective Action
steps.instruction: Using Table 4-23 (Alarms and Corrective Actions), match the recorded Alarm Text/ID to the corresponding row to identify the documented Cause and Corrective Action.
steps.purpose: Use the manual’s alarm mapping table to select the documented corrective action for the specific alarm.
steps.expected_result: The recorded Alarm Text/ID matches a specific Table 4-23 entry that provides Cause and Corrective Action.
steps.healthy_condition: A single, clear Table 4-23 row is identified for the recorded Alarm Text/ID, and it includes Cause and Corrective Action fields.
steps.failure_condition: The alarm text/ID cannot be found in Table 4-23 entries.
stop_or_escalate_if: Alarm text/ID cannot be matched to Table 4-23 entries.

actions.label: Use Table 4-23 mapping
actions.exact_action: Use the alarm table in the manual (Table 4-23: Alarms and Corrective Actions) to match the recorded Alarm Text/ID to the documented Cause and Corrective Action.

title: Check Hospital HMI Default Screen for software version, station IP, and login/logout access
summary: Use the Hospital HMI 2.4 “Default” screen to confirm the currently installed software version, the Hospital Station IP address, and that login/logout controls are available.
when_to_use: When you need to verify the Hospital Station HMI is running the expected software version, that the displayed Hospital Station IP address is correct, and that the user can access login/logout controls from the Hospital HMI “Default” screen.

steps.title: Open Hospital HMI and navigate to the “Default” screen (Hospital HMI 2.4)
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, navigate to the “Default” screen (Hospital HMI 2.4).
steps.purpose: Reach the screen that displays the software version, Hospital Station IP address, and login/logout controls.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI “Default” screen is displayed.
steps.healthy_condition: The “Default” screen is visible and shows the expected sections for software currently installed and Hospital Station IP address, along with login/logout controls.
steps.failure_condition: The “Default” screen does not load, or the expected on-screen sections (software/IP/login/logout) are not present.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the “Default” screen cannot be reached or does not display the expected information, escalate to support/maintenance.

actions.label: Navigate to Default screen
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the “Default” screen (Hospital HMI 2.4).

steps.title: Verify software currently installed and Hospital Station IP address
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI “Default” screen, locate the displayed “software currently installed” information and the Hospital Station IP address, and verify they are present and correct.
steps.purpose: Confirm the HMI is running the expected software and that the Hospital Station IP address shown on the HMI is correct.
steps.expected_result: The “software currently installed” information and the Hospital Station IP address are displayed on the “Default” screen.
steps.healthy_condition: Both the software version and Hospital Station IP address fields are populated with values that are not blank and not obviously incorrect.
steps.failure_condition: The software version or Hospital Station IP address fields are blank, missing, or obviously incorrect.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the software version or IP address fields are blank, missing, or obviously incorrect, escalate to support/maintenance for further investigation.

actions.label: Check software version and IP
actions.exact_action: Locate the displayed “software currently installed” information and record/verify the Hospital Station IP address.

steps.title: Verify login and logout controls are available
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI “Default” screen, verify that login and logout controls are present and usable (e.g., visible Login/Logout buttons or equivalent controls).
steps.purpose: Ensure the user can access login/logout from the Hospital HMI “Default” screen.
steps.expected_result: Login and logout controls are present on the “Default” screen.
steps.healthy_condition: Login/logout controls are visible and respond as expected for user access management.
steps.failure_condition: Login/logout controls are not present or do not respond.
stop_or_escalate_if: If login/logout controls are not present or do not respond, escalate to support/maintenance.

actions.label: Check login/logout controls
actions.exact_action: Verify the screen provides user login and log out controls (e.g., visible Login/Logout buttons or equivalent controls).

steps.title: Confirm “REBOOT TO SETUP” is reserved for maintenance personnel
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI “Default” screen, identify the “REBOOT TO SETUP” button and do not use it unless you are maintenance personnel.
steps.purpose: Prevent unintended maintenance-only actions from the operator check.
steps.expected_result: The “REBOOT TO SETUP” button is visible, and you do not press it as part of this check.
steps.healthy_condition: The button is present but remains unpressed by operator during this verification.
steps.failure_condition: The button is pressed by non-maintenance personnel or the operator attempts to use it during this check.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the “REBOOT TO SETUP” button was pressed by non-maintenance personnel, escalate to support/maintenance.

actions.label: Locate REBOOT TO SETUP
actions.exact_action: Do not use the “REBOOT TO SETUP” button unless you are maintenance personnel.

title: Use Hospital HMI IO Diagnostics screen to verify station switch input states and HMI temperature/voltage readings
summary: Use the Hospital HMI 2.2 “IO Diagnostics” screen to confirm which station switch inputs are ON vs OFF and to review the HMI’s own temperature and voltage readings for basic hardware health visibility.
when_to_use: When you need to verify station switch input states (ON/OFF) and check the Hospital HMI’s temperature and voltage readings shown on the Hospital HMI 2.2 “IO Diagnostics” screen.

steps.title: Open Hospital HMI 2.2 IO Diagnostics screen
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI, navigate to the “IO Diagnostics” screen (Hospital HMI 2.2).
steps.purpose: Get to the screen that displays station switch input states and the HMI’s temperature/voltage readings.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI “IO Diagnostics” screen is displayed, showing (a) station switch input on/off indicators and (b) temperature readings and voltage readings for the HMI itself.
steps.healthy_condition: The “IO Diagnostics” screen is visible and contains the switch input on/off indicators plus temperature and voltage reading fields.
steps.failure_condition: The “IO Diagnostics” screen cannot be reached/displayed, or the expected on-screen sections (switch input indicators and temperature/voltage readings) are not present.

actions.label: Navigate to IO Diagnostics
actions.exact_action: Open the Hospital HMI and navigate to the “IO Diagnostics” screen (Hospital HMI 2.2).

steps.title: Verify station switch input indicators (ON vs OFF)
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI “IO Diagnostics” screen, identify the on/off indicators for the station switch inputs and determine which inputs are currently ON and which are OFF.
steps.purpose: Confirm the current station switch input states as shown by the HMI.
steps.expected_result: You can clearly distinguish which station switch input indicators are ON vs OFF on the “IO Diagnostics” screen.
steps.healthy_condition: Switch input indicators show a consistent ON/OFF state set on the screen (i.e., the indicators are not ambiguous/missing).
steps.failure_condition: The switch input states shown on the screen do not match the expected physical switch positions (or the indicators are missing/unclear).
stop_or_escalate_if: If switch input states do not match expected physical switch positions, escalate to support/maintenance for further investigation.

actions.label: Check switch input on/off indicators
actions.exact_action: Identify the on/off indicators for the station switch inputs and verify which inputs are currently ON and which are OFF.

steps.title: Record HMI temperature readings
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI “IO Diagnostics” screen, locate the temperature readings and note the displayed values.
steps.purpose: Capture the HMI temperature values displayed for basic hardware health visibility.
steps.expected_result: Temperature reading fields on the “IO Diagnostics” screen show values that you can read and record.
steps.healthy_condition: Temperature readings are present and populated on the screen.
steps.failure_condition: Temperature readings are missing/blank or appear abnormal.
stop_or_escalate_if: If temperature readings are missing/blank or appear abnormal, escalate to support/maintenance.

actions.label: Check temperature readings
actions.exact_action: Locate the temperature readings on the screen and note the displayed values.

steps.title: Record HMI voltage readings
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI “IO Diagnostics” screen, locate the voltage readings and note the displayed values.
steps.purpose: Capture the HMI voltage values displayed for basic hardware health visibility.
steps.expected_result: Voltage reading fields on the “IO Diagnostics” screen show values that you can read and record.
steps.healthy_condition: Voltage readings are present and populated on the screen.
steps.failure_condition: Voltage readings are missing/blank or appear abnormal.
stop_or_escalate_if: If voltage readings are missing/blank or appear abnormal, escalate to support/maintenance.

actions.label: Check voltage readings
actions.exact_action: Locate the voltage readings on the screen and note the displayed values.

title: Navigate Hospital HMI Main Menu to Operator, Maintenance, Setup, and Alarms
summary: On the Hospital HMI Main Menu screen, use the right-hand function buttons (F1/F2/F3/F4/F5/F6) to navigate to the Operator Menu, Maintenance Menu, Setup menu, and Alarms for totes directed to the Hospital Station. Use F3 (Previous screen) to return one screen.
when_to_use: Use when you are on the Hospital Station Hospital HMI Main Menu screen and need to reach the Operator Menu, Maintenance Menu, Setup menu, or Alarms using the Hospital HMI function keys.

steps.title: Open Hospital HMI Main Menu for the Hospital Station
steps.instruction: Open the Hospital HMI / lane UI for the Hospital Station and display the Hospital HMI Main Menu screen.
steps.purpose: Get to the correct starting screen so the function keys route to the intended menus.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI Main Menu screen is displayed with the right-hand function buttons available.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the Hospital HMI Main Menu with the function buttons labeled for navigation (F1/F2/F3/F4/F5/F6).
steps.failure_condition: The Hospital HMI Main Menu screen is not displayed (function buttons are not present or you are on a different screen).

actions.label: Display Hospital HMI Main Menu
actions.exact_action: Open the Hospital HMI / lane UI for the Hospital Station and display the Hospital HMI Main Menu screen.

steps.title: Confirm you are on the Main menu using F5
steps.instruction: On the right-hand side of the Main Menu screen, press F5.
steps.purpose: Verify the current screen is the Hospital HMI Main Menu before navigating to other menus.
steps.expected_result: The screen confirms you are on the Main menu (F5 routes to the Main menu).
steps.healthy_condition: Pressing F5 keeps/returns you to the Main menu screen.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing F5 does not route you to the Main menu screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: If pressing a function key does not change screens to the expected menu, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for assistance.

actions.label: Press F5 (Main menu)
actions.exact_action: press F5 to confirm you are on the Main menu.

steps.title: Open Operator menu using F1
steps.instruction: Press F1 on the right-hand side of the Main Menu screen.
steps.purpose: Reach the Operator Menu from the Hospital HMI Main Menu.
steps.expected_result: The Operator menu screen opens (F1 routes to Operator menu).
steps.healthy_condition: You are taken to the Operator menu screen.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing F1 does not open the Operator menu screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: If pressing a function key does not change screens to the expected menu, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for assistance.

actions.label: Press F1 (Operator menu)
actions.exact_action: Press F1 to open the Operator menu.

steps.title: Open Maintenance menu using F2
steps.instruction: Press F2 on the right-hand side of the Main Menu screen.
steps.purpose: Reach the Maintenance Menu from the Hospital HMI Main Menu.
steps.expected_result: The Maintenance menu screen opens (F2 routes to Maintenance menu).
steps.healthy_condition: You are taken to the Maintenance menu screen.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing F2 does not open the Maintenance menu screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: If pressing a function key does not change screens to the expected menu, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for assistance.

actions.label: Press F2 (Maintenance menu)
actions.exact_action: Press F2 to open the Maintenance menu.

steps.title: Open Setup menu using F4
steps.instruction: Press F4 on the right-hand side of the Main Menu screen.
steps.purpose: Reach the Setup menu from the Hospital HMI Main Menu.
steps.expected_result: The Setup menu screen opens (F4 routes to Setup menu).
steps.healthy_condition: You are taken to the Setup menu screen.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing F4 does not open the Setup menu screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: If pressing a function key does not change screens to the expected menu, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for assistance.
Do not attempt configuration changes from the Setup menu unless instructed by FORTNA support.

actions.label: Press F4 (Setup menu)
actions.exact_action: Press F4 to open the Setup menu.

steps.title: Open Alarms using F6
steps.instruction: Press F6 on the right-hand side of the Main Menu screen.
steps.purpose: Reach the Alarms screen from the Hospital HMI Main Menu.
steps.expected_result: The Alarms screen opens (F6 routes to Alarms).
steps.healthy_condition: You are taken to the Alarms screen.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing F6 does not open the Alarms screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: If pressing a function key does not change screens to the expected menu, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for assistance.

actions.label: Press F6 (Alarms)
actions.exact_action: Press F6 to open Alarms.

steps.title: Return to previous screen using F3
steps.instruction: If you need to return, press F3 (Previous screen).
steps.purpose: Navigate back one screen when you need to return from a menu.
steps.expected_result: The HMI returns to the previous screen (F3 routes to Previous screen).
steps.healthy_condition: After pressing F3, the prior screen you came from is displayed.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing F3 does not return to the previous screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: If pressing a function key does not change screens to the expected menu, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for assistance.

actions.label: Press F3 (Previous screen)
actions.exact_action: press F3 (Previous screen) to go back one screen.

title: Check Hospital HMI Operations Screen Induct/Extract Position Read-Only Data and WCS Status Messages
summary: Use the Hospital HMI / lane UI Operations Menu screen to read the WCS-fed induct and extract position fields (AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, Status). Confirm the Status messages explain why the tote is there and what station operator menu/action to use.
when_to_use: When a tote arrives at the hospital station and you need to determine what tote/AGV is at the induct and extract positions and what the WCS status message requires the station operator to do next.

steps.title: Open Hospital HMI Operations Menu and locate Induct Position / Extract Position sections
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, navigate to the Operations Menu screen that contains the "Induct Position" and "Extract Position" sections.
steps.purpose: Get to the screen that displays the WCS-fed, read-only induct and extract position information for the hospital station.
steps.expected_result: The screen shows both "Induct Position" and "Extract Position" sections.
steps.healthy_condition: "Induct Position" and "Extract Position" sections are visible on the Operations Menu screen.
steps.failure_condition: The Operations Menu screen is not showing the "Induct Position" and/or "Extract Position" sections.

actions.label: Navigate to Operations Menu
actions.exact_action: Open the Hospital HMI and navigate to the Operations Menu screen that contains the "Induct Position" and "Extract Position" sections.

steps.title: Read Induct Position read-only fields (AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, Status)
steps.instruction: In the "Induct Position" section, read the four read-only fields: AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and Status.
steps.purpose: Capture the WCS-fed induct position identity and the WCS Status message that guides the station operator action/menu.
steps.expected_result: The "Induct Position" section displays values for AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and a Status message.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and Status are present in the "Induct Position" section as read-only WCS data.
steps.failure_condition: The "Induct Position" Status field is blank/missing or does not provide a WCS status message explaining why the tote is there and what menu/action the station operator needs.
stop_or_escalate_if: Induct Position Status is missing/blank.
Induct Position Status does not provide explanation/action guidance (why the tote is there and what menu/action to use).

actions.label: Read Induct Position fields
actions.exact_action: In the "Induct Position" section, read the four read-only fields: AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and Status.

steps.title: Read Extract Position read-only fields (AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, Status)
steps.instruction: In the "Extract Position" section, read the four read-only fields: AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and Status.
steps.purpose: Capture the WCS-fed extract position identity and the WCS Status message that guides the station operator action/menu.
steps.expected_result: The "Extract Position" section displays values for AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and a Status message.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and Status are present in the "Extract Position" section as read-only WCS data.
steps.failure_condition: The "Extract Position" Status field is blank/missing or does not provide a WCS status message explaining why the tote is there and what menu/action the station operator needs.
stop_or_escalate_if: Extract Position Status is missing/blank.
Extract Position Status does not provide explanation/action guidance (why the tote is there and what menu/action to use).

actions.label: Read Extract Position fields
actions.exact_action: In the "Extract Position" section, read the four read-only fields: AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and Status.

steps.title: Confirm both Status messages are present and provide WCS explanation/action guidance
steps.instruction: Verify that the "Induct Position" Status and "Extract Position" Status messages are present and written as messages received from the WCS that explain why the tote is there and what menu/action the station operator needs to use.
steps.purpose: Ensure the WCS Status messages on both induct and extract positions are usable for station operator decision-making.
steps.expected_result: Both Status fields contain non-blank WCS messages that provide explanation and action/menu guidance.
steps.healthy_condition: Induct Position Status and Extract Position Status each provide a clear WCS message describing why the tote is there and what menu/action to perform.
steps.failure_condition: Either Status field is blank/missing or does not provide explanation/action guidance.
stop_or_escalate_if: Induct Position Status is missing/blank or lacks explanation/action guidance.
Extract Position Status is missing/blank or lacks explanation/action guidance.

actions.label: Validate Status message content
actions.exact_action: Confirm the "Induct Position" and "Extract Position" Status messages are present and are written as messages received from the WCS (i.e., they explain why the tote is there and what menu/action the station operator needs).

title: Inspect Hospital Station Daily Preventive Maintenance (Barcode Scanner, Stacklight, Tabletop Debris)
summary: Perform a daily preventive maintenance inspection on each hospital station by verifying the barcode scanner is operational, the stacklight is operational, and the tabletop is free of debris (e.g., stuck labels).
when_to_use: Use this procedure for daily preventive maintenance on each hospital station to confirm the station’s barcode scanner and stacklight are operational and that the tabletop is clear of debris.

steps.title: Inspect each hospital station barcode scanner for operational condition
steps.instruction: For each hospital station, visually inspect the barcode scanner to confirm it is operational (e.g., not visibly damaged/obstructed).
steps.purpose: Confirm the barcode scanner at each hospital station is operational as required for station operation.
steps.expected_result: The barcode scanner at the station is operational (no visible damage/obstruction preventing normal use).
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode scanner appears intact and unobstructed at the hospital station.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode scanner appears damaged and/or obstructed such that it is not operational.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop inspection for this station if the barcode scanner is not operational.

actions.label: Visual check scanner
actions.exact_action: Visually inspect the barcode scanner to confirm it is operational (e.g., not visibly damaged/obstructed).

steps.title: Inspect each hospital station stacklight for operational condition
steps.instruction: For each hospital station, visually inspect the stacklight to confirm it is operational (e.g., not visibly damaged/obstructed).
steps.purpose: Confirm the stacklight at each hospital station is operational as required for station status indication.
steps.expected_result: The stacklight at the station is operational (no visible damage/obstruction preventing normal use).
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight assembly appears intact and unobstructed at the hospital station.
steps.failure_condition: Stacklight appears damaged and/or obstructed such that it is not operational.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop inspection for this station if the stacklight is not operational.

actions.label: Visual check stacklight
actions.exact_action: Visually inspect the stacklight to confirm it is operational (e.g., not visibly damaged/obstructed).

steps.title: Inspect tabletop and clear debris (e.g., stuck labels)
steps.instruction: For each hospital station, inspect the tabletop and remove/clear any debris such as stuck labels.
steps.purpose: Ensure the tabletop at each hospital station is free of debris that could interfere with tote handling.
steps.expected_result: The tabletop is free of debris (no stuck labels) at the station.
steps.healthy_condition: Tabletop surface is clear of debris/stuck labels.
steps.failure_condition: Debris (e.g., stuck labels) remains on the tabletop after attempted clearing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop inspection for this station if debris cannot be cleared.

actions.label: Check tabletop
actions.exact_action: Inspect the tabletop and remove/clear any debris such as stuck labels.

steps.title: Stop inspection and escalate when scanner/stacklight/debris issue is found
steps.instruction: If a hospital station barcode scanner or stacklight is not operational, or if debris cannot be cleared, stop the inspection for that station and escalate to the appropriate maintenance contact.
steps.purpose: Prevent continued operation with an impaired station and route the issue to maintenance support.
steps.expected_result: Inspection is stopped for the affected station and maintenance escalation is initiated.
steps.healthy_condition: All stations inspected successfully with no unresolved scanner/stacklight/debris issues.
steps.failure_condition: Continuing inspection/operation despite an unresolved scanner/stacklight issue or remaining tabletop debris.
stop_or_escalate_if: Barcode scanner not operational.
Stacklight not operational.
Debris cannot be cleared.

actions.label: Escalate maintenance
actions.exact_action: Stop the inspection for any station where the barcode scanner or stacklight is not operational or where debris cannot be cleared, and escalate to the appropriate maintenance contact.

title: Perform Hospital Station Daily Preventive Maintenance Checks (Barcode Scanner, Stacklight, Tabletop Debris)
summary: Perform a daily physical inspection of each Hospital Station to verify the barcode scanner is operational, the stacklight is operational, and the tabletop is free of debris.
when_to_use: Use this procedure at the start of each day (daily preventive maintenance) to confirm each Hospital Station is safe/ready for operation by checking: (1) barcode scanner operational status, (2) stacklight operational status, and (3) tabletop debris-free condition.

steps.title: Inspect each Hospital Station barcode scanner and confirm it is operational
steps.instruction: For each Hospital Station, visually inspect the barcode scanner and confirm it is operational.
steps.purpose: Ensure the Hospital Station barcode scanner is ready to read tote barcodes for station operations.
steps.expected_result: For the station being inspected, the barcode scanner is operational.
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode scanner is operational at the Hospital Station.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode scanner is not operational at the Hospital Station.
stop_or_escalate_if: Barcode scanner issue is observed

actions.label: Visual check scanner operational status
actions.exact_action: Inspect each hospital station for the following: The barcode scanner is operational.

steps.title: Inspect each Hospital Station stacklight and confirm it is operational
steps.instruction: For each Hospital Station, visually inspect the stacklight and confirm it is operational.
steps.purpose: Ensure the Hospital Station stacklight is ready to provide operational status indication.
steps.expected_result: For the station being inspected, the stacklight is operational.
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight is operational at the Hospital Station.
steps.failure_condition: Stacklight is not operational at the Hospital Station.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stacklight is not operational

actions.label: Visual check stacklight operational status
actions.exact_action: Inspect each hospital station for the following: The stacklight is operational.

steps.title: Inspect each Hospital Station tabletop and confirm it is free of debris
steps.instruction: For each Hospital Station, visually inspect the tabletop area and confirm it is free of debris.
steps.purpose: Ensure the tabletop area is clear so totes and station operations are not obstructed by debris.
steps.expected_result: For the station being inspected, the tabletop is free of debris.
steps.healthy_condition: Tabletop is free of debris at the Hospital Station.
steps.failure_condition: Debris is present on the tabletop at the Hospital Station.
stop_or_escalate_if: Debris is found on the tabletop

actions.label: Visual check tabletop debris-free condition
actions.exact_action: Inspect each hospital station for the following: The tabletop is free of debris.

steps.title: Stop inspection and escalate if any required condition fails
steps.instruction: If any barcode scanner issue is observed, if the stacklight is not operational, or if debris is present on the tabletop, stop the inspection and escalate to maintenance/support as required by site practice.
steps.purpose: Prevent operation with an unsafe/incorrectly functioning station.
steps.expected_result: Inspection is stopped for the day/sequence and escalation is initiated when any required condition fails.
steps.healthy_condition: No escalation is required because all three conditions (scanner operational, stacklight operational, tabletop debris-free) are met for the station(s) inspected.
steps.failure_condition: At least one required condition fails (scanner not operational, stacklight not operational, or debris present), and inspection continues without escalation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Barcode scanner issue is observed
Stacklight is not operational
Debris is present on the tabletop

actions.label: Stop and escalate
actions.exact_action: If any barcode scanner issue is observed, if the stacklight is not operational, or if debris is present on the tabletop, stop the inspection and escalate to maintenance/support as required by site practice.

title: Extract an Arriving Tote at the Hospital Station Using Hospital HMI and Green Scanner
summary: When an AGV brings a tote to the Hospital Station, use the Hospital HMI to open the correct tote-extraction screen based on the status fields, scan the tote barcode with the green scanner to populate the Tote ID field, and then perform the task indicated by the status fields. If the tote is being returned into the system, place it on the induct side (left) and ensure it is flush against the end stops.
when_to_use: Use this procedure when an AGV arrives at the Hospital Station with a tote and you need to extract the tote using the Hospital HMI workflow (screen selection driven by status fields), scan the tote barcode with the green scanner, and then execute the task indicated by the status fields.

steps.title: Confirm a tote has arrived at the Hospital Station (right side)
steps.instruction: Visually confirm the AGV has brought a tote to the right side of the Hospital Station.
steps.purpose: Ensure you are handling the correct physical arrival location before interacting with the Hospital HMI extraction workflow.
steps.expected_result: A tote is physically present at the Hospital Station right side designated for AGV tote delivery/extraction.
steps.healthy_condition: Tote is at the right side of the Hospital Station ready for extraction.
steps.failure_condition: No tote is present at the Hospital Station right side (or the tote is not at the expected arrival/extraction position).

actions.label: Verify tote arrival position
actions.exact_action: Confirm an AGV has brought a tote to the right side of the Hospital Station.

steps.title: Open the corresponding Hospital HMI screen for tote extraction (based on status fields)
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, open the corresponding screen used to extract the tote from the system. Select the screen based on the information shown in the status fields.
steps.purpose: Select the correct Hospital HMI workflow so the subsequent scan and task execution align with the status fields for the arriving tote.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI tote-extraction screen corresponding to the arriving tote is open, showing status-field information used to determine the workflow.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the status fields on the Hospital HMI screen that determine the extraction workflow.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot identify the correct extraction screen based on the status fields, or the status fields do not reflect the arriving tote.

actions.label: Select extraction screen
actions.exact_action: Open the corresponding screen on the HMI to extract the tote from the system (determined by information in the status fields).

steps.title: Scan the tote barcode using the green scanner
steps.instruction: Scan the tote barcode using the green scanner.
steps.purpose: Capture the tote barcode so the system can populate the Tote ID field for the extraction workflow.
steps.expected_result: The scan is accepted by the Hospital HMI workflow and the Tote ID field begins to populate after scanning.
steps.healthy_condition: The green scanner input is successfully read for the arriving tote barcode.
steps.failure_condition: The scan is not accepted and the Tote ID field does not populate after scanning.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the Tote ID field does not populate after scanning, stop and escalate for assistance rather than proceeding with the task.

actions.label: Scan tote barcode
actions.exact_action: Scan the tote barcode using the green scanner.

steps.title: Verify Tote ID field auto-populates after scanning
steps.instruction: Verify that the Tote ID field automatically populates after scanning.
steps.purpose: Confirm the scan was correctly associated with the tote so you execute the correct task for that tote.
steps.expected_result: The Tote ID field on the Hospital HMI is populated with the scanned tote ID.
steps.healthy_condition: Tote ID field shows a value after the barcode scan.
steps.failure_condition: Tote ID field remains blank or does not populate after scanning.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the Tote ID field does not populate after scanning, stop and escalate for assistance rather than proceeding with the task.

actions.label: Check Tote ID population
actions.exact_action: Verify the Tote ID field automatically populates after scanning.

steps.title: Perform the task indicated by the status fields
steps.instruction: Perform whatever task needs to be performed as determined by the information in the status fields.
steps.purpose: Complete the Hospital Station workflow for the arriving tote based on the status fields shown on the selected HMI screen.
steps.expected_result: The required Hospital Station action for the arriving tote is executed according to the status fields on the active Hospital HMI screen.
steps.healthy_condition: The task corresponding to the status fields is completed on the Hospital HMI workflow for that tote.
steps.failure_condition: You perform an action that does not match the status fields, or the workflow cannot be completed as indicated by the status fields.

actions.label: Execute status-driven task
actions.exact_action: Perform whatever task needs to be performed as determined by the information in the status fields.

steps.title: If returning tote into the system, place it on the induct side (left) flush against end stops
steps.instruction: If the tote is going back into the system, put the tote on the induct side (left side) of the station and ensure it is flush against the end stops.
steps.purpose: Ensure correct physical placement for tote re-entry so the system can handle the tote properly.
steps.expected_result: The tote is positioned on the induct side (left) and is flush against the induct-side end stops.
steps.healthy_condition: Tote is flush against the end stops on the induct side (left).
steps.failure_condition: Tote is not flush against the induct-side end stops or cannot be positioned correctly.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the tote cannot be positioned flush against the induct-side end stops, stop and escalate for assistance.

actions.label: Position tote for re-entry
actions.exact_action: If a tote is going back into the system, put the tote on the induct side (left side) of the station. Ensure the tote is flush against the end stops.

title: Scan Hospital Station Tote With Green Scanner to Determine Reason for Arrival
summary: When an AGV delivers a tote to the hospital station, the operator uses the green scanner to determine why the tote was brought to the station for manual handling.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV brings a tote to a hospital station for manual handling (mis-sort, bad tip, or tote overload scenarios).
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for diagnosing system-wide RMS/WCS issues; it is specifically for determining the tote arrival reason at the hospital station using the green scanner and station/HMI indications.

steps.title: Wait for the AGV to bring the tote to the correct side of the hospital station
steps.instruction: At the hospital station, wait for the AGV to bring the tote to the right side (from the operator’s perspective).
steps.purpose: Ensure the tote is positioned at the hospital station side used for extraction/manual handling.
steps.expected_result: The tote is delivered to the right side of the hospital station (extract side) where the operator can attend it.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGV has arrived at the hospital station and the tote is at the extract side (right side from the operator’s perspective).
steps.failure_condition: The tote is not at the expected right-side (extract side) position, or the AGV/tote is not present at the station.

actions.label: Confirm tote arrival position
actions.exact_action: Wait for the AGV to bring the tote to the right side (from the operator’s perspective).

steps.title: Confirm tote presence using the hospital station stacklight indication
steps.instruction: Visually check the hospital station stacklight to confirm a tote is present at the station.
steps.purpose: Verify the station has a tote present before scanning.
steps.expected_result: The stacklight indicates a tote is present at the hospital station.
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight indicates AGV/tote presence at the station (hospital station stacklight provides information about actions at the station; tote presence is indicated by the stacklight).
steps.failure_condition: Stacklight does not indicate tote presence (e.g., indicates no AGV present).
stop_or_escalate_if: If the stacklight does not indicate tote presence, do not proceed with scanning; re-check station/tote positioning.

actions.label: Check stacklight
actions.exact_action: A stacklight indicates a tote is present.

steps.title: Scan the tote with the green scanner to determine the reason for arrival
steps.instruction: Scan the tote barcode using the green scanner.
steps.purpose: Obtain the scan-based reason the tote was brought to the hospital station for manual handling.
steps.expected_result: A scan-based reason for the tote’s arrival is produced/available for use in manual handling.
steps.healthy_condition: The green scanner successfully scans the tote barcode and provides the reason for arrival (hospital diversion reason).
steps.failure_condition: The green scanner cannot read/produce a reason for the tote arrival (no scan result available).
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the green scanner cannot read/produce a reason for the tote arrival (no scan result available).
Escalate if the tote reason cannot be determined even after re-scanning.

actions.label: Scan tote barcode
actions.exact_action: Scan the tote barcode using the green scanner.

steps.title: Verify the scan result is available on the hospital station HMI (or scanner output) and proceed with manual handling
steps.instruction: Check the hospital station HMI (if present) or the scanner output to confirm the scan result is available, then use that reason to proceed with manual handling.
steps.purpose: Ensure the operator uses the correct reason for arrival to select the appropriate manual handling action.
steps.expected_result: The operator can see the scan-based reason (or the scan-populated tote ID/barcode fields that drive the station’s status) on the hospital station HMI or scanner output and uses it to proceed.
steps.healthy_condition: Hospital HMI shows the relevant fields populated from the green scanner (e.g., Tote ID and Bar Code fields) and the station status messages indicate why the tote is at the station.
steps.failure_condition: The scan result is not available on the hospital station HMI (if used) and/or the operator cannot determine the tote reason even after re-scanning.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the tote reason cannot be determined even after re-scanning.

actions.label: Check HMI fields/status
actions.exact_action: Open the corresponding screen on the HMI to extract the tote from the system (determined by information in the status fields).

title: Interpret Hospital Station Stacklight States (Solid/Flashing Colors)
summary: Use the hospital station stacklight color and flashing pattern to determine the current station condition: Default/Indeterminate, No AGV present, RMS error, Fault, or AGV present (flashing yellow for 15 seconds).
when_to_use: When you need to identify the current hospital station condition by observing the station stacklight (solid vs flashing colors).

steps.title: Locate the hospital station stacklight
steps.instruction: Locate the hospital station’s stacklight (each hospital station has one stacklight).
steps.purpose: Identify the correct stacklight to observe for the station condition.
steps.expected_result: You can visually see the hospital station stacklight that illuminates in sections.
steps.healthy_condition: The correct stacklight for the hospital station is visible and observable.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot clearly identify the stacklight for the intended hospital station.

actions.label: Visually locate stacklight
actions.exact_action: Locate the hospital station’s stacklight (each hospital station has one stacklight).

steps.title: Observe whether the stacklight is solid or flashing
steps.instruction: Observe the stacklight indication and note whether it is solid or flashing.
steps.purpose: Determine which stacklight mapping applies (solid vs flashing patterns).
steps.expected_result: You have identified the stacklight pattern as solid or flashing (and which colors are lit).
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight colors and solid/flashing behavior are clearly observable.
steps.failure_condition: The stacklight pattern is unclear (e.g., cannot determine solid vs flashing or which colors are lit).

actions.label: Check solid vs flashing
actions.exact_action: Observe the stacklight indication and note whether it is solid or flashing.

steps.title: Map Solid Red to Default/Indeterminate
steps.instruction: If the stacklight is Solid Red, record the state as Default/Indeterminate.
steps.purpose: Classify the station condition based on the documented stacklight state.
steps.expected_result: Recorded station condition = Default/Indeterminate when Solid Red is observed.
steps.healthy_condition: Solid Red is observed and the recorded state matches Default/Indeterminate.
steps.failure_condition: Solid Red is observed but the recorded state is not Default/Indeterminate.

actions.label: Record Default/Indeterminate
actions.exact_action: If the stacklight is Solid Red, record the state as Default/Indeterminate.

steps.title: Map Solid Green to No AGV present
steps.instruction: If the stacklight is Solid Green, record the state as No AGV present at the station.
steps.purpose: Classify the station condition based on the documented stacklight state.
steps.expected_result: Recorded station condition = No AGV present at the station when Solid Green is observed.
steps.healthy_condition: Solid Green is observed and the recorded state matches No AGV present at the station.
steps.failure_condition: Solid Green is observed but the recorded state is not No AGV present at the station.

actions.label: Record No AGV present
actions.exact_action: If the stacklight is Solid Green, record the state as No AGV present at the station.

steps.title: Map Red+Yellow+Green to RMS error
steps.instruction: If the stacklight shows Red, Yellow, and Green simultaneously, record the state as RMS error.
steps.purpose: Classify the station condition based on the documented stacklight state.
steps.expected_result: Recorded station condition = RMS error when Red+Yellow+Green are simultaneously lit.
steps.healthy_condition: Red, Yellow, and Green are simultaneously observed and the recorded state matches RMS error.
steps.failure_condition: Red+Yellow+Green are observed but the recorded state is not RMS error.

actions.label: Record RMS error
actions.exact_action: If the stacklight shows Red, Yellow, and Green simultaneously, record the state as RMS error.

steps.title: Map Flashing Red to Fault
steps.instruction: If the stacklight is Flashing Red, record the state as Fault.
steps.purpose: Classify the station condition based on the documented stacklight state.
steps.expected_result: Recorded station condition = Fault when Flashing Red is observed.
steps.healthy_condition: Flashing Red is observed and the recorded state matches Fault.
steps.failure_condition: Flashing Red is observed but the recorded state is not Fault.

actions.label: Record Fault
actions.exact_action: If the stacklight is Flashing Red, record the state as Fault.

steps.title: Map Flashing Yellow (15 seconds) to AGV present
steps.instruction: If the stacklight is Flashing Yellow, confirm it lasts for 15 seconds, then record the state as AGV is present at either position of the station.
steps.purpose: Confirm AGV presence at the hospital station using the documented flashing duration.
steps.expected_result: Recorded station condition = AGV is present at either position of the station when Flashing Yellow persists for 15 seconds.
steps.healthy_condition: Flashing Yellow is observed and lasts for 15 seconds; recorded state matches AGV present at either position.
steps.failure_condition: Flashing Yellow is observed but does not last for 15 seconds, or the recorded state does not match the 15-second Flashing Yellow condition.

actions.label: Confirm 15-second duration
actions.exact_action: If the stacklight is Flashing Yellow, confirm it lasts for 15 seconds, then record the state as AGV is present at either position of the station.

title: Move tipper from 'home' to 'ready' by pressing CYCLE START
summary: After the tipper axes are homed to the 'home' position, press CYCLE START on the operator station control panel to move the tipper motor from 'home' to 'ready'.
when_to_use: Use when the tipper axes have been homed (Z1/A1 and Z2/A2) and the system is at the 'home' position, and you need to start the tipper operation cycle to move the motor to 'ready'.

steps.title: Confirm tipper axes are homed to the 'home' position
steps.instruction: Verify the tipper axes are homed so the system is at the 'home' position (Z1/A1 and Z2/A2).
steps.purpose: Ensure the system is in the correct starting state ('home') before starting the cycle.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is in the 'home' position state (ready to transition to 'ready' when CYCLE START is pressed).
steps.healthy_condition: The system indicates the tipper is at 'home' (not already in 'ready' or another state).
steps.failure_condition: The system is not at 'home' (axes not homed / not in the expected starting state).

actions.label: Verify homed state
actions.exact_action: Ensure the tipper axes have been homed (Z1/A1 and Z2/A2) so the system is at the 'home' position.

steps.title: Press CYCLE START to start the tipper cycle
steps.instruction: On the operator station control panel (Visu_MCP_Dual), press the CYCLE START button.
steps.purpose: Initiate the tipper operation cycle that transitions the motor from 'home' to 'ready'.
steps.expected_result: The tipper motor transitions from 'home' to 'ready' after pressing CYCLE START.
steps.healthy_condition: A state change occurs from 'home' to 'ready' following the CYCLE START press.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing CYCLE START does not change the state from 'home' to 'ready'.
stop_or_escalate_if: If pressing CYCLE START does not change the state from 'home' to 'ready', stop and escalate.

actions.label: Start cycle
actions.exact_action: Press CYCLE START.

steps.title: Verify motor state changes from 'home' to 'ready'
steps.instruction: Observe the motor state indicator/state text on the operator station HMI to confirm it changes from 'home' to 'ready'.
steps.purpose: Confirm the cycle started correctly and the tipper reached the expected state.
steps.expected_result: The motor state changes from 'home' to 'ready' after CYCLE START.
steps.healthy_condition: The HMI shows the motor in 'ready' state (transition completed).
steps.failure_condition: The HMI continues to show 'home' (no transition to 'ready').
stop_or_escalate_if: If the state does not change from 'home' to 'ready', stop and escalate.

actions.label: Check state indicator
actions.exact_action: Observe the motor state change from 'home' to 'ready.'

title: Stop the Operator Station using the CYCLE STOP button on the Operator Station Main Screen
summary: An operator can stop the operator station by pressing the CYCLE STOP button on the operator station main screen.
when_to_use: Use when you need to stop the operator station cycle from the operator station main screen by pressing the CYCLE STOP control.

steps.title: Open the Operator Station Main Screen
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the operator station main screen.
steps.purpose: Get to the screen that contains the CYCLE STOP control for stopping the operator station.
steps.expected_result: The operator station main screen is displayed and the CYCLE STOP control is available for use.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the CYCLE STOP button on the operator station main screen.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot locate the CYCLE STOP button or are not on the operator station main screen.

actions.label: Navigate to operator station main screen
actions.exact_action: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the operator station main screen.

steps.title: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the operator station
steps.instruction: Press the CYCLE STOP button on the operator station main screen.
steps.purpose: Stop the operator station cycle using the documented CYCLE STOP control.
steps.expected_result: The operator station stops after pressing CYCLE STOP.
steps.healthy_condition: After pressing CYCLE STOP, the operator station no longer runs the cycle.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing CYCLE STOP does not stop the operator station cycle.
stop_or_escalate_if: If pressing CYCLE STOP does not stop the operator station, stop further operation and escalate to support.

actions.label: Press CYCLE STOP
actions.exact_action: Press CYCLE STOP on the operator station main screen.

steps.title: Verify the operator station is stopped
steps.instruction: Observe the operator station after pressing CYCLE STOP to confirm it is stopped.
steps.purpose: Confirm the stop action took effect.
steps.expected_result: The operator station is stopped (the cycle is no longer running after pressing CYCLE STOP).
steps.healthy_condition: The cycle does not continue running after CYCLE STOP is pressed.
steps.failure_condition: The cycle continues running after CYCLE STOP is pressed.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the operator station does not stop, stop further operation and escalate to support.

actions.label: Observe cycle behavior
actions.exact_action: Observe that the operator station is stopped (stop action is evidenced by the system no longer running the cycle after pressing CYCLE STOP).

title: Perform Operator Station Daily Preventive Maintenance Checks (Controller, Stacklights, Chute Debris)
summary: Perform a daily operator station inspection to verify the operator station is safe/ready for operation by checking for controller damage, confirming stacklights are operational, and ensuring the chute is free of debris such as stuck labels.
when_to_use: Use this procedure for daily preventive maintenance checks of the OptiSweep operator station to confirm it is safe/ready for operation (controller condition, stacklights operational, chute free of debris such as stuck labels).

steps.title: Visually inspect the operator station controller area for damage
steps.instruction: Go to the operator station and visually inspect the controller area for any damage.
steps.purpose: Confirm the operator station controller is not damaged before proceeding with operation readiness.
steps.expected_result: The controller shows no visible damage.
steps.healthy_condition: No visible damage is observed on the controller area at the operator station.
steps.failure_condition: Damage to the controller is observed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Controller damage is observed

actions.label: Inspect controller area
actions.exact_action: Go to the operator station and visually inspect the controller area for any damage.

steps.title: Check operator station stacklights are operational
steps.instruction: Check the operator station stacklights and confirm they are operational (functioning/visible as intended).
steps.purpose: Verify the stacklights function/are visible as intended as part of daily readiness.
steps.expected_result: Stacklights are operational.
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklights are operational (visible/functioning as intended) at the operator station.
steps.failure_condition: Stacklights are not operational.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stacklights are not operational

actions.label: Verify stacklight operation
actions.exact_action: Check the operator station stacklights and confirm they are operational (i.e., functioning/visible as intended).

steps.title: Inspect chute and clear debris such as stuck labels
steps.instruction: Inspect the chute and remove/clear any debris such as stuck labels.
steps.purpose: Ensure the chute is free of debris that could interfere with operation (e.g., stuck labels).
steps.expected_result: The chute is free of debris (e.g., no stuck labels).
steps.healthy_condition: No debris/stuck labels are present in the chute at the operator station.
steps.failure_condition: Debris/stuck labels are present in the chute.
stop_or_escalate_if: Debris/stuck labels are found in the chute

actions.label: Clear chute debris
actions.exact_action: Inspect the chute and remove/clear any debris such as stuck labels.

steps.title: Stop inspection and escalate if any unsafe condition is found
steps.instruction: If any controller damage is found, or stacklights are not operational, or debris is present in the chute, stop the daily inspection and escalate to maintenance/support as required by site practice.
steps.purpose: Prevent operation when daily readiness checks fail and ensure maintenance/support is engaged.
steps.expected_result: Inspection is stopped and maintenance/support escalation is initiated when any of the three checks fail.
steps.healthy_condition: No escalation is required because controller damage is not observed, stacklights are operational, and the chute is free of debris.
steps.failure_condition: Any of the three checks fail and escalation is not initiated.
stop_or_escalate_if: Controller damage is observed
Stacklights are not operational
Debris/stuck labels are present in the chute

actions.label: Escalate to maintenance/support
actions.exact_action: Stop the daily inspection and escalate to maintenance/support as required by site practice.

title: Clear flashing ESTOP fault at the operator station using HMI RESET
summary: If the operator station ESTOP is flashing, pull out the ESTOP and press RESET on the operator station HMI to clear faults so startup actions (homing/cycle start) can proceed.
when_to_use: Use when the operator station control panel shows the ESTOP is flashing and you need to clear the fault condition so you can proceed with operator station startup actions (homing/cycle start).

steps.title: Check whether the operator station ESTOP is flashing
steps.instruction: At the operator station control panel, check whether the ESTOP is flashing.
steps.purpose: Confirm the flashing ESTOP condition before attempting reset.
steps.expected_result: The ESTOP status is observed as flashing (fault condition present).
steps.healthy_condition: ESTOP is not flashing (no flashing fault condition present).
steps.failure_condition: ESTOP is flashing but you proceed without confirming the flashing condition.

actions.label: Inspect ESTOP indicator
actions.exact_action: Check whether the ESTOP is flashing.

steps.title: Pull out the ESTOP if it is flashing
steps.instruction: If the ESTOP is flashing, pull out the ESTOP.
steps.purpose: Physically clear the flashing ESTOP condition as required by the startup procedure.
steps.expected_result: The ESTOP has been pulled out (physical ESTOP action completed).
steps.healthy_condition: ESTOP is no longer in the flashing state after the pull-out action.
steps.failure_condition: ESTOP remains flashing after the pull-out action.

actions.label: Pull out ESTOP
actions.exact_action: pull out the ESTOP

steps.title: Press HMI RESET to clear faults
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI screen, press RESET to clear any faults.
steps.purpose: Clear the faults indicated by the flashing ESTOP condition using the HMI RESET control.
steps.expected_result: After pressing RESET, the flashing ESTOP fault condition is cleared (the ESTOP is no longer flashing).
steps.healthy_condition: Flashing ESTOP condition is no longer present after RESET.
steps.failure_condition: ESTOP remains flashing after pulling out the ESTOP and pressing HMI RESET.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the ESTOP remains flashing after pulling out ESTOP and pressing HMI RESET, stop and escalate rather than continuing with homing/cycle start.

actions.label: Press RESET
actions.exact_action: press RESET on the HMI screen to clear any faults

steps.title: Confirm the flashing ESTOP condition is cleared before proceeding
steps.instruction: Confirm the fault condition is cleared by checking that the ESTOP is no longer flashing; proceed only if the flashing condition is no longer present.
steps.purpose: Ensure the fault condition is actually cleared before attempting startup actions.
steps.expected_result: The ESTOP is no longer flashing (fault condition cleared).
steps.healthy_condition: ESTOP is not flashing.
steps.failure_condition: ESTOP is still flashing after reset.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the ESTOP remains flashing after pulling out ESTOP and pressing HMI RESET, stop and escalate rather than continuing with homing/cycle start.

actions.label: Re-check ESTOP indicator
actions.exact_action: Confirm the fault condition is cleared (i.e., proceed only if the flashing ESTOP condition is no longer present).

title: Home tipper axes (Z1/A1 and Z2/A2) using AUTO REF and verify home proximity switch stop
summary: Home all tipper axes so the system can proceed to cycle start. Use AUTO REF to home the left tipper axes (Z1/A1) and right tipper axes (Z2/A2), and verify the axis button state changes green→yellow while moving and that the tipper motor stops after sensing the “home” proximity switch.
when_to_use: Use when the system/operator station needs to home every tipper axis (Z1/A1 left tipper and Z2/A2 right tipper) before pressing CYCLE START.

steps.title: Identify left and right tipper axis controls (Z1/A1 and Z2/A2) on the operator station
steps.instruction: At the operator station, identify the axis controls for Z1 and A1 (left tipper) and Z2 and A2 (right tipper) on the operator station HMI.
steps.purpose: Ensure you are using the correct axis controls for the left (Z1/A1) and right (Z2/A2) tippers before starting AUTO REF homing.
steps.expected_result: You can clearly locate the axis controls/indicators corresponding to Z1/A1 (left) and Z2/A2 (right) on the operator station HMI.
steps.healthy_condition: Both left and right tipper axis controls/indicators are visible and selectable on the operator station HMI.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot identify the correct axis controls/indicators for Z1/A1 and Z2/A2 on the operator station HMI.

actions.label: Locate axis controls
actions.exact_action: Identify the axis controls for Z1 and A1 (left tipper) and Z2 and A2 (right tipper).

steps.title: Press AUTO REF to home all tipper axes
steps.instruction: Press AUTO REF to reference/home every axis (Z1/A1 and Z2/A2).
steps.purpose: Start the automatic referencing (homing) sequence for all tipper axes.
steps.expected_result: The homing sequence starts for the axes.
steps.healthy_condition: AUTO REF is accepted and the axis button state begins changing as the axes move.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing AUTO REF does not start homing (no axis movement/state change).
stop_or_escalate_if: If axis buttons do not change green→yellow when AUTO REF is pressed, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Start homing
actions.exact_action: Press AUTO REF.

steps.title: Verify axis button state changes green→yellow while moving
steps.instruction: Observe each axis button for Z1/A1 and Z2/A2 and confirm the axis button changes from green to yellow to indicate it is moving.
steps.purpose: Confirm each axis is actively moving during homing.
steps.expected_result: Each axis button changes from green to yellow during AUTO REF homing.
steps.healthy_condition: Axis button indicators for the axes you are homing show green→yellow transitions while the axes move.
steps.failure_condition: Axis button indicators do not change green→yellow when AUTO REF is pressed.
