stop_or_escalate_if: If axis buttons do not change green→yellow when AUTO REF is pressed, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Check axis button color/state
actions.exact_action: The axis button changes from green to yellow to indicate it is moving.

steps.title: Verify tipper motor stops after sensing the “home” proximity switch
steps.instruction: Watch the tipper motor movement for each side until it senses the “home” proximity switch, then confirm the motor stops.
steps.purpose: Confirm the homing stop condition is working (home proximity switch is sensed).
steps.expected_result: For each axis/side, the tipper motor moves until it senses the “home” proximity switch, then stops.
steps.healthy_condition: Motor motion stops at the home position after sensing the home proximity switch.
steps.failure_condition: The motor does not stop after sensing the “home” proximity switch.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the motor does not stop at the 'home' proximity switch, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Watch for home proximity stop
actions.exact_action: The tipper motor moves until it senses the "home" proximity switch, then stops.

steps.title: Confirm homing is complete for both left (Z1/A1) and right (Z2/A2) axes before proceeding
steps.instruction: Confirm homing is complete for both left (Z1/A1) and right (Z2/A2) axes before proceeding to cycle start.
steps.purpose: Ensure the system is ready for the next action (CYCLE START).
steps.expected_result: Both left and right tipper axes have completed homing (no longer moving as part of AUTO REF).
steps.healthy_condition: Homing motion has finished for both sides, indicating the system can proceed.
steps.failure_condition: One or both sides appear not to have completed homing (e.g., still moving or not stopped at home).
stop_or_escalate_if: If homing is not complete for both left and right axes, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Verify both sides homed
actions.exact_action: Confirm homing is complete for both left (Z1/A1) and right (Z2/A2) axes before proceeding.

title: Identify Operator Station Components (Tipper, Chute, Stacklights, HMI, Push-Buttons, Rotary Station)
summary: Walk up to the OptiSweep operator station and visually locate the key components used to receive parcels from the tippers: two tippers, chute, two stacklights, operator station HMI, four push-buttons, and rotary station.
when_to_use: Use when you need to visually confirm where the operator-station components are located so you can interact with the operator station HMI and push-buttons and understand how parcels flow from the tippers to the chute and rotary station.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to troubleshoot tipper faults, HMI alarms, or system faults—this procedure only identifies physical components and their locations.

steps.title: Locate the operator station area where parcels are received from the tippers
steps.instruction: Walk to the OptiSweep operator station area where an operator receives parcels from the tippers.
steps.purpose: Establish the correct physical area before identifying individual components.
steps.expected_result: You are at the operator station area that contains (at minimum) the two tippers, chute, rotary station, operator station HMI screen, and push-buttons.
steps.healthy_condition: The operator station area is visible and includes the operator station components described in Table 3-1 (Tipper, Chute, Stacklight, Operator station HMI, Push-buttons, Rotary station).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find the operator station area that receives parcels from the tippers (components are not present in the expected area).
stop_or_escalate_if: If the operator station area cannot be located, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for site-specific verification.

actions.label: Visual scan for operator station components
actions.exact_action: Walk up to the operator station area where an operator receives parcels from the tippers.

steps.title: Identify the two tippers at the operator station
steps.instruction: At the operator station, visually locate the two tippers (Tipper = Item 1 in Figure 3-1 / Table 3-1).
steps.purpose: Confirm the two tipper units that deliver parcels to the chute.
steps.expected_result: Both tippers are visible at the operator station and correspond to Item 1 (Tipper) in Figure 3-1.
steps.healthy_condition: Two tipper assemblies are present in the operator station area.
steps.failure_condition: One or both tippers cannot be located.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any component cannot be located (e.g., stacklights not visible on top of the frame or HMI/push-buttons not present), stop and escalate to FORTNA support for site-specific verification.

actions.label: Locate Tipper (Item 1)
actions.exact_action: Identify the two tippers at the operator station.

steps.title: Identify the chute positioned to receive parcels from the tippers
steps.instruction: Visually locate the chute (Chute = Item 2 in Figure 3-1 / Table 3-1) positioned to receive parcels from the tippers.
steps.purpose: Confirm the receiving path from tippers to the operator station.
steps.expected_result: The chute is visible and corresponds to Item 2 (Chute) in Figure 3-1.
steps.healthy_condition: A chute is present in the operator station area aligned with the tippers’ parcel delivery.
steps.failure_condition: The chute cannot be located.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any component cannot be located (e.g., stacklights not visible on top of the frame or HMI/push-buttons not present), stop and escalate to FORTNA support for site-specific verification.

actions.label: Locate Chute (Item 2)
actions.exact_action: Identify the chute positioned to receive parcels from the tippers.

steps.title: Identify the two stacklights mounted on the top of the frame on either side of the chute
steps.instruction: Look on the top of the frame on either side of the chute and identify the two stacklights (Stacklight = Item 3 in Figure 3-1 / Table 3-1).
steps.purpose: Confirm the visual status indicators associated with the operator station.
steps.expected_result: Two stacklights are visible on the top of the frame, one on each side of the chute, matching Item 3 (Stacklight).
steps.healthy_condition: Two stacklights are mounted on top of the frame on either side of the chute.
steps.failure_condition: One or both stacklights cannot be located (e.g., stacklights not visible on top of the frame).
stop_or_escalate_if: If any component cannot be located (e.g., stacklights not visible on top of the frame or HMI/push-buttons not present), stop and escalate to FORTNA support for site-specific verification.

actions.label: Locate Stacklights (Item 3)
actions.exact_action: Identify the two stacklights mounted on the top of the frame on either side of the chute.

steps.title: Identify the operator station HMI screen
steps.instruction: Find the operator station HMI screen (Operator station HMI = Item 5 in Figure 3-1 / Table 3-1).
steps.purpose: Confirm where the operator station HMI is located for interaction.
steps.expected_result: The operator station HMI screen is visible and corresponds to Item 5 (Operator station HMI) in Figure 3-1.
steps.healthy_condition: An HMI screen is present at the operator station and matches the expected location in Figure 3-1.
steps.failure_condition: The operator station HMI screen cannot be located.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any component cannot be located (e.g., stacklights not visible on top of the frame or HMI/push-buttons not present), stop and escalate to FORTNA support for site-specific verification.

actions.label: Locate Operator station HMI (Item 5)
actions.exact_action: Identify the operator station HMI screen.

steps.title: Identify the four push-buttons on the operator station
steps.instruction: Locate the push-button panel on the operator station (Push-buttons = Item 6 in Figure 3-1 / Table 3-1). On the push-button panel, identify the TIP LEFT, TIP RIGHT, and the Surepost left/right buttons as shown in the push-button photo.
steps.purpose: Confirm the physical controls used to interact with the operator station.
steps.expected_result: The push-button panel is visible and corresponds to Item 6 (Push-buttons) in Figure 3-1; the panel includes TIP LEFT, TIP RIGHT, SURE POST LEFT, and SURE POST RIGHT buttons.
steps.healthy_condition: The push-button panel is present and the labeled buttons are visible.
steps.failure_condition: The push-button panel cannot be located or the expected labeled buttons are not present.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any component cannot be located (e.g., stacklights not visible on top of the frame or HMI/push-buttons not present), stop and escalate to FORTNA support for site-specific verification.

actions.label: Locate Push-buttons (Item 6)
actions.exact_action: Identify the four push-buttons on the operator station.

steps.title: Identify the rotary station
steps.instruction: Locate the rotary station under the chute (Rotary station = Item 7 in Figure 3-1 / Table 3-1).
steps.purpose: Confirm the bag rack area under the chute used for parcel bags.
steps.expected_result: The rotary station is visible under the chute and corresponds to Item 7 (Rotary station) in Figure 3-1.
steps.healthy_condition: A rotary station is present under the chute with bag racks; it is the station where bags are manually replenished by operators.
steps.failure_condition: The rotary station cannot be located under the chute.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any component cannot be located (e.g., stacklights not visible on top of the frame or HMI/push-buttons not present), stop and escalate to FORTNA support for site-specific verification.

actions.label: Locate Rotary station (Item 7)
actions.exact_action: Identify the rotary station.

title: Perform Operator Station Lockout/Tagout Using Visu_Dual_MCP and Electrical Panel Power Switch
summary: Safely stop the operator station for lockout/tagout by using the operator station HMI to navigate to the Visu_Dual_MCP screen, press CYCLE STOP, optionally jog the tipper carriages using the JOG controls (+/–) for the correct tipper axis, then turn OFF the operator station electrical panel power switch and apply LOTO.
when_to_use: Use when you need to place the operator station into a stopped state and then perform lockout/tagout at the operator station electrical panel.

steps.title: Navigate to the Visu_Dual_MCP screen on the operator station HMI
steps.instruction: At the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen.
steps.purpose: Open the correct operator station HMI screen that provides CYCLE STOP and (if needed) JOG controls for the tipper carriages.
steps.expected_result: The "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen is displayed on the operator station HMI.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen controls used for stopping and jogging (including CYCLE STOP).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot reach the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot reach the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen.

actions.label: Open Visu_Dual_MCP
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen.

steps.title: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the operator station
steps.instruction: On the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen, press "CYCLE STOP".
steps.purpose: Stop the automatic tipping cycle at the operator station as the first step in preparing for LOTO.
steps.expected_result: The operator station is in a stopped state after pressing CYCLE STOP.
steps.healthy_condition: CYCLE STOP has been pressed and the automatic tipping cycle is halted (operator station is stopped).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot press "CYCLE STOP".
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot press "CYCLE STOP".

actions.label: Stop cycle
actions.exact_action: Press CYCLE STOP.

steps.title: Optionally jog the carriages using JOG (+/–) for the correct tipper axis
steps.instruction: If you need to move the carriages to a different position: press "JOG", select the corresponding axis for the tipper, then use the "+" and "-" buttons to move the carriages.
steps.purpose: If needed, reposition the tipper carriages to a different position while the cycle is stopped, using the JOG controls for the correct axis.
steps.expected_result: The carriages move to the desired position using the selected tipper axis controls after pressing JOG.
steps.healthy_condition: You can select the corresponding tipper axis and the +/– jog controls move the carriages as intended.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the JOG controls or cannot move the carriages using the +/– buttons.

actions.label: Open jogging screen
actions.exact_action: Press JOG.

actions.label: Select tipper axis and jog
actions.exact_action: Select the corresponding axis for the tipper and use the + and – buttons to move the carriages.

steps.title: Turn OFF the operator station electrical panel power switch and apply LOTO
steps.instruction: At the operator station electrical panel, turn the power switch to "OFF" and apply LOTO.
steps.purpose: Complete lockout/tagout by removing power at the operator station electrical panel and applying LOTO.
steps.expected_result: The operator station electrical panel power switch is set to "OFF" and LOTO is applied.
steps.healthy_condition: Power switch is in the OFF position and LOTO is applied at the operator station electrical panel.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot set the electrical panel power switch to "OFF" or LOTO cannot be applied.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the electrical panel power switch cannot be set to "OFF" or LOTO cannot be applied.

actions.label: Set panel power OFF
actions.exact_action: Turn the power switch to "OFF".

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: Apply LOTO.

title: Set tipper to AUTO mode so it waits for WCS instructions
summary: Place the tipper in AUTO mode so it waits for the WCS to send instructions.
when_to_use: Use when starting/operating the tipper and you need the tipper to wait for WCS instructions by placing it into AUTO mode.

steps.title: Locate the tipper mode control on the operator station HMI
steps.instruction: On the operator station control panel (Visu_MCP_Dual / operator station main screen), locate the tipper mode control, including the AUTO button.
steps.purpose: Identify the control used to switch the tipper into AUTO mode.
steps.expected_result: The AUTO control/button is visible and ready to be selected on the operator station HMI/control panel.
steps.healthy_condition: The operator station control panel is displaying the tipper controls including AUTO (and related cycle controls).
steps.failure_condition: The AUTO control/button is not visible or cannot be selected on the operator station HMI/control panel.

actions.label: Find AUTO button
actions.exact_action: Locate the tipper mode control (AUTO button) on the operator station HMI/control panel.

steps.title: Place the tipper in AUTO mode
steps.instruction: Select AUTO on the operator station HMI/control panel to place the tipper in AUTO mode.
steps.purpose: Switch the tipper into automatic mode so it will wait for WCS instructions.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is in AUTO mode.
steps.healthy_condition: After selecting AUTO, the tipper reflects AUTO mode on the operator station HMI/control panel.
steps.failure_condition: The tipper does not reflect AUTO mode after selection.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the tipper does not reflect AUTO mode after selection, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Select AUTO
actions.exact_action: Press the AUTO button to enter automatic mode.

steps.title: Confirm the tipper is waiting for WCS instructions
steps.instruction: Verify on the operator station HMI/control panel that the tipper is in AUTO mode and is waiting for WCS instructions.
steps.purpose: Verify the tipper is in the correct state for WCS-driven operation.
steps.expected_result: Tipper is in AUTO mode and waits for the WCS to send instructions.
steps.healthy_condition: The operator station indicates the tipper is in AUTO mode and in a waiting state for WCS instructions.
steps.failure_condition: The tipper is not in AUTO mode or is not waiting for WCS instructions.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the tipper does not reflect AUTO mode after selection, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Check AUTO/waiting state
actions.exact_action: Confirm the tipper is in AUTO mode and is waiting for WCS instructions.

title: Start the Operator Station: verify AGVs/main disconnect, reset flashing ESTOP, home axes, and press CYCLE START
summary: Bring the operator station from an off/faulted state to the tipper “ready” state by verifying AGVs are powered and the main disconnect is ON, clearing flashing ESTOP faults via HMI RESET, homing all tipper axes (Z1/A1 and Z2/A2) using AUTO REF, then pressing CYCLE START to move from “home” to “ready” and placing the tipper into AUTO mode so it waits for WCS instructions.
when_to_use: Use when the operator station has been turned off or is in a faulted/off state and you need to start it so the tipper can home and then wait for WCS instructions in AUTO mode.

steps.title: Verify AGVs are powered on
steps.instruction: Verify the AGVs are powered on.
steps.purpose: Ensure the fleet/AGVs are available before starting the operator station.
steps.expected_result: AGVs are powered on (observable at the site’s AGV power status indicators).
steps.healthy_condition: AGVs show powered-on status.
steps.failure_condition: AGVs are not powered on.

actions.label: Check AGV power status
actions.exact_action: Verify the AGVs are powered on.

steps.title: Verify main disconnect is ON
steps.instruction: Verify the main disconnect is ON.
steps.purpose: Confirm the operator station power path is enabled before resetting ESTOP and homing axes.
steps.expected_result: Main disconnect is ON (observable at the main disconnect indicator/label).
steps.healthy_condition: Main disconnect indicator shows ON.
steps.failure_condition: Main disconnect is not ON.

actions.label: Check main disconnect
actions.exact_action: Verify the main disconnect is ON.

steps.title: Reset flashing ESTOP faults via HMI RESET
steps.instruction: At the operator station control panel, if the ESTOP is flashing: pull out the ESTOP, then press RESET on the HMI screen to clear any faults.
steps.purpose: Clear any ESTOP-related faults so homing and cycle start can proceed.
steps.expected_result: Flashing ESTOP fault is cleared after pulling out ESTOP and pressing RESET on the HMI.

title: Remove A-Axis Gearbox (LOTO, side panel access, gripper removal, counter-balance handling)
summary: Safely remove the OptiSweep A-axis gearbox assembly by performing LOTO, removing the station side panel to access the motor, removing the gripper, and controlling counter-balance drift after gripper removal (either allow drift to the lower hard stop or remove the counter-balance weight).
when_to_use: Use when the OptiSweep A-axis gearbox must be removed and you need to follow the manual’s LOTO and disassembly sequence, including managing counter-balance drift risk after gripper removal.

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the system
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the system using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure.
steps.purpose: Ensure the system is locked out/tagged out before removing the side panel and disassembling the A-axis gearbox.
steps.expected_result: The system is in a locked-out/tagged-out state prior to side panel removal.
steps.healthy_condition: No unexpected motion occurs when you begin disassembly actions.
steps.failure_condition: Any unexpected motion occurs during disassembly.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any unexpected motion occurs during disassembly, stop and re-check LOTO.

actions.label: Execute Operator Station Lockout/Tagout
actions.exact_action: LOTO the system (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel to access the motor
steps.instruction: Using a 3/8-in. wrench or socket, remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Expose the motor area by removing the nine self-tapping fasteners securing the station side panel.
steps.expected_result: The station side panel is removed and the motor access area is exposed.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel removal is complete without unexpected movement; motor access is visible.
steps.failure_condition: Unexpected motion occurs during side panel removal, or the side panel cannot be removed due to uncontrolled fastener resistance.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any unexpected motion occurs during disassembly, stop and re-check LOTO.

actions.label: Remove side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Remove the gripper
steps.instruction: Remove the gripper (manual cross-reference: "Removal" on page 97).
steps.purpose: Remove the gripper as required by the A-axis gearbox removal sequence; this triggers the counter-balance drift condition that must be managed next.
steps.expected_result: The gripper is removed.
steps.healthy_condition: After gripper removal, you observe the system out-of-balance condition and can control the counter-balance drift as described in the next step.
steps.failure_condition: Counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by the optional counter-balance weight removal approach).
stop_or_escalate_if: If the counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by removing the counter-balance weight as allowed), stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

actions.label: Remove gripper
actions.exact_action: Remove the gripper (see "Removal" on page 97).

steps.title: Control counter-balance drift after gripper removal
steps.instruction: After gripper removal, allow the counter-balance to drift down to the lower hard stop OR remove the counter-balance weight to help balance the system.
steps.purpose: Manage the out-of-balance condition so the counter-balance drift is controlled to the lower hard stop or balanced by removing the counter-balance weight.
steps.expected_result: Counter-balance drift is controlled: either it reaches the lower hard stop or the counter-balance weight is removed to balance the system.
steps.healthy_condition: The counter-balance drift proceeds in a controlled manner to the lower hard stop, or the counter-balance weight is removed as an alternative balancing method.
steps.failure_condition: Counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by removing the counter-balance weight as allowed).
stop_or_escalate_if: If the counter-balance drift cannot be controlled to the lower hard stop (or by removing the counter-balance weight as allowed), stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

actions.label: Allow drift to lower hard stop
actions.exact_action: It is acceptable to allow it to drift to the lower hard stop, or optionally, the counter-balance weight can be removed to help balance the system.

steps.title: Remove the gearbox without removing the motor (motor may be needed for fastener access)
steps.instruction: Remove the gearbox without removing the motor; if fastener access requires it, remove the motor (manual cross-reference: "Motor Removal" on page 106).
steps.purpose: Proceed with gearbox removal while noting that motor removal may be required to access fasteners.
steps.expected_result: You are positioned to remove the gearbox mounting fasteners; motor removal is only performed if required for fastener access.
steps.healthy_condition: Gearbox mounting fasteners are accessible for removal without unnecessary motor removal.
steps.failure_condition: Fasteners cannot be accessed safely without removing the motor, or removal attempts cause uncontrolled movement.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access fasteners safely without causing uncontrolled movement, stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

actions.label: Assess fastener access
actions.exact_action: Remove the gearbox without removing the motor. However, the motor will likely need to be removed for fastener access. See "Motor Removal" on page 106.

steps.title: Remove the gearbox mounting screws
steps.instruction: Remove the eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws mounting the gearbox to the carriage.
steps.purpose: Detach the gearbox from the carriage by removing the eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws.
steps.expected_result: All eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws are removed and the gearbox is no longer secured to the carriage.
steps.healthy_condition: No remaining fasteners secure the gearbox; gearbox can be lifted/removed without binding.
steps.failure_condition: Any screw remains engaged, or the gearbox binds due to misalignment or remaining fasteners.
stop_or_escalate_if: If fasteners resist removal due to Loctite® 277 and you cannot remove them without risking uncontrolled movement, stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

actions.label: Remove gearbox screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the eight (8) M5x18 socket-head screws mounting the gearbox to the carriage.

steps.title: Remove the gearbox
steps.instruction: Remove the gearbox.
steps.purpose: Complete the gearbox removal by lifting the gearbox assembly away from the carriage.
steps.expected_result: The gearbox is removed from the carriage.
steps.healthy_condition: Gearbox removal completes without unexpected motion of the counter-balance system.
steps.failure_condition: Unexpected motion occurs during gearbox removal, or the gearbox cannot be removed due to remaining attachment points.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any unexpected motion occurs during disassembly, stop and re-check LOTO.
If the gearbox cannot be removed cleanly, stop and escalate to qualified support before proceeding.

actions.label: Lift off gearbox
actions.exact_action: Remove the gearbox.

title: Add an AGV to a Zone When There Is No Empty AGV Available (RMS Fault Recovery)
summary: Recover operation by stopping RMS, physically placing an AGV into the zone under the tote rack, adding the AGV in RMS using Tote API Controls, verifying the AGV turns blue and reaches AGV status/state "szonestaging" on the Hospital HMI/lane UI, then stopping again and resuming RMS.
when_to_use: Use when there is no empty AGV available for a zone and you must recover by adding an AGV into the zone under the tote rack, ensuring it reaches the required "szonestaging" state before resuming RMS.

steps.title: E-stop RMS on the RMS / fleet status UI
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), press the E-stop for RMS.
steps.purpose: Stop RMS movement before physically moving and adding the AGV in RMS.
steps.expected_result: RMS is in an E-stopped state on the RMS / fleet status UI.
steps.healthy_condition: E-stop control shows RMS is stopped (not running).
steps.failure_condition: RMS does not enter/maintain the E-stopped state (control does not reflect stopped state).

actions.label: Press RMS E-stop
actions.exact_action: E-stop RMS.

steps.title: Move an AGV into the zone under the tote rack
steps.instruction: Move an AGV into the zone under the tote rack (physical_floor).
steps.purpose: Provide a physical AGV in the correct zone so RMS can stage it.
steps.expected_result: An AGV is physically positioned in the zone under the tote rack.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV is placed in the intended zone location under the tote rack (no mismatch between intended zone and physical placement).
steps.failure_condition: AGV is not in the intended zone under the tote rack (wrong location or not present).

actions.label: Place AGV in zone
actions.exact_action: Move an AGV into the zone under the tote rack.

steps.title: Add the AGV in RMS using Tote API Controls
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), add the AGV using the "Tote API Controls" function.
steps.purpose: Register the physically placed AGV into RMS so it can transition to staging.
steps.expected_result: The AGV is added in RMS via Tote API Controls (AGV appears in RMS roster/map context for the add operation).
steps.healthy_condition: After adding, the AGV begins the transition that results in the AGV turning blue.
steps.failure_condition: The AGV does not appear/does not progress toward turning blue after the add action.

actions.label: Add AGV via Tote API Controls
actions.exact_action: Add AGV in RMS. (See "Tote API Controls" on page 26.)

steps.title: Wait for the AGV to turn blue on the RMS UI
steps.instruction: Wait for the AGV to turn blue on the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui).
steps.purpose: Confirm RMS has accepted the AGV and it is transitioning.
steps.expected_result: The added AGV changes to blue on the RMS UI.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV indicator on RMS transitions to blue after the add action.
steps.failure_condition: AGV does not turn blue within the expected transition window (no blue state change).

actions.label: Observe AGV color/state
actions.exact_action: Wait for AGV to turn blue.

steps.title: Verify AGV status/state is exactly "szonestaging" on the Hospital HMI
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI (hospital_hmi), verify the AGV status/state is exactly "szonestaging".
steps.purpose: Ensure the AGV reached the required staging state before resuming RMS.
steps.expected_result: Hospital HMI shows the AGV state/status value "szonestaging".
steps.healthy_condition: AGV state/status equals exactly "szonestaging".
steps.failure_condition: AGV state/status is not "szonestaging" (including if it is moving to the Hospital).
stop_or_escalate_if: Do not proceed to resume RMS until the AGV state verification step shows "szonestaging".

actions.label: Check AGV state on Hospital HMI
actions.exact_action: Verify AGV status is "szonestaging". (Reference AGV state on HMI.).

steps.title: If AGV is moving to the Hospital, remove and add it again
steps.instruction: If the AGV is moving to the Hospital (Hospital HMI shows Hospital destination/state), remove the AGV and add it again (repeat the add step).
steps.purpose: Correct an undesired destination state so the AGV can reach staging.
steps.expected_result: AGV is removed from the system and then re-added so it can transition back toward "szonestaging".
steps.healthy_condition: After remove/re-add, the AGV can reach "szonestaging" on the Hospital HMI.
steps.failure_condition: AGV repeatedly moves to the Hospital instead of reaching "szonestaging".
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the AGV does not reach "szonestaging" after being added, or if it repeatedly moves to the Hospital instead of staging.

actions.label: Remove and re-add AGV
actions.exact_action: If the AGV is moving to the Hospital, remove the AGV and add it again.

steps.title: Press E-stop again on the RMS / fleet status UI
steps.instruction: Press the E-stop again on the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui).
steps.purpose: Stop RMS again after the AGV reaches the required staging state.
steps.expected_result: RMS reflects the E-stopped state again on the RMS / fleet status UI.
steps.healthy_condition: E-stop control indicates RMS is stopped (not running).
steps.failure_condition: RMS does not enter/maintain the E-stopped state.

actions.label: Press RMS E-stop (second time)
actions.exact_action: Press E-stop again.

steps.title: Resume RMS on the RMS / fleet status UI
steps.instruction: Resume RMS on the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui) (Starting the System procedure reference).
steps.purpose: Resume RMS operation after the AGV is staged correctly.
steps.expected_result: RMS is resumed/started on the RMS / fleet status UI.
steps.healthy_condition: RMS shows resumed/started state after the second E-stop press.
steps.failure_condition: RMS does not resume/started state is not reflected.

actions.label: Resume RMS
actions.exact_action: Resume RMS. (See "Starting the System" on page 65.)

title: Use AGV API Controls to Remove/Recover an AGV and Pause/Resume All AGVs
summary: Use the System HMI API screen’s AGVs section to remove a problematic AGV by ID, recover (add back) the AGV by ID after physical recovery, and pause/resume all AGV movement fleet-wide.
when_to_use: When an AGV needs to be removed from the system (e.g., it has an issue) and later recovered after physical removal/recovery, and you need to pause/resume all AGV movement using the AGV API Controls.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for required physical removal/recovery steps after using Remove AGV (the AGV must be physically removed; if it has a tote, the tote must be taken to the hospital where the tote is removed).

steps.title: Open the System HMI API screen and navigate to the AGVs section
steps.instruction: Open the System HMI API screen and navigate to the AGVs section (AGV API Controls).
steps.purpose: Access the AGV API Controls needed to remove/recover an AGV and pause/resume all AGV movement.
steps.expected_result: The AGVs section is visible with controls including Remove AGV, Recover AGV, Pause All AGVs, and Resume All AGVs.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV API Controls are visible and ready for input (Remove AGV / Recover AGV fields and Pause/Resume buttons are present).
steps.failure_condition: The AGVs section or required controls are not accessible/visible, preventing entry of an AGV ID or clicking Pause/Resume.

actions.label: Verify AGVs section controls are present
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the AGVs section of the API screen.

steps.title: Remove an AGV from the system by AGV ID
steps.instruction: In the AGVs section, enter the target AGV ID in the Remove AGV input field, then click the Remove AGV control/button.
steps.purpose: Remove a problematic AGV from the system so it can be physically recovered.
steps.expected_result: The Remove AGV action is accepted for the entered AGV ID, and the AGV is removed from the system after the required physical removal step.
steps.healthy_condition: After clicking Remove AGV, you can proceed with physical removal of the AGV from the system (and tote handling if applicable).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot physically remove the AGV/tote as required after issuing Remove AGV, or the system behavior does not match the expected fleet behavior after subsequent steps.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot physically remove/recover the AGV/tote as required after using Remove AGV.

actions.label: Enter AGV ID and click Remove AGV
actions.exact_action: Enter the target AGV ID in the Remove AGV input field, then click the Remove AGV control/button.

actions.label: Physically remove AGV (and tote to hospital if present)
actions.exact_action: Physically remove the AGV from the system. If the AGV has a tote, take the tote to the hospital where the tote is removed.

steps.title: Recover (add back) the AGV by AGV ID after physical recovery
steps.instruction: After the physical recovery/add-back step, enter the same (or correct) AGV ID in the Recover AGV input field, then click the Recover AGV control/button.
steps.purpose: Add the physically recovered AGV back into the system.
steps.expected_result: The Recover AGV action is accepted for the entered AGV ID, and the AGV is added back into the system after physical recovery.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGV is successfully re-added to the system and you can proceed to fleet pause/resume actions as needed.
steps.failure_condition: The AGV is not added back as expected after clicking Recover AGV (or you cannot complete the physical recovery/add-back step).

actions.label: Enter AGV ID and click Recover AGV
actions.exact_action: Enter the same (or correct) AGV ID in the Recover AGV input field, then click the Recover AGV control/button.

steps.title: Pause all AGV movement
steps.instruction: Click Pause All AGVs in the AGVs section of the API screen.
steps.purpose: Stop fleet-wide AGV movement when needed during recovery/removal operations.
steps.expected_result: Fleet-wide AGV movement is paused after clicking Pause All AGVs.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV movement is stopped fleet-wide (pause state is in effect).
steps.failure_condition: System does not reflect the expected fleet behavior after Pause All AGVs.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the system does not reflect the expected fleet behavior after Pause All AGVs (use the Get AGV Status pop-up to verify AGV state).

actions.label: Click Pause All AGVs
actions.exact_action: Click Pause All AGVs.

steps.title: Resume all AGV movement
steps.instruction: Click Resume All AGVs in the AGVs section of the API screen.
steps.purpose: Restart fleet-wide AGV movement after recovery/removal operations are complete.
steps.expected_result: Fleet-wide AGV movement resumes after clicking Resume All AGVs.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV movement is running fleet-wide (resume state is in effect).
steps.failure_condition: System does not reflect the expected fleet behavior after Resume All AGVs.

actions.label: Click Resume All AGVs
actions.exact_action: Click Resume All AGVs.

title: Recover an AGV After It Loses a Tote (No Fault) Using RMS and Hospital HMI
summary: Recover from the “AGV LOST TOTE NO FAULT” condition by stopping RMS, physically moving the AGV to the Hospital, removing and re-adding the AGV via the Hospital station PC/HMI workflow, power-cycling the AGV, re-localizing it by rolling over the Inbound Hospital Station QR code, then locating/removing the missing tote and adding it back into the system so the AGV can return the tote to the sorter.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV has lost a tote but is in the “AGV LOST TOTE NO FAULT” recovery scenario, and you need to remove/re-add the AGV and re-localize it at the Inbound Hospital Station so the missing tote can be removed and reintroduced for normal sorter flow.

steps.title: E-stop RMS
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), perform the RMS E-stop action.
steps.purpose: Stop RMS fleet movement before physically handling the AGV and performing remove/re-add actions.
steps.expected_result: RMS is in an E-stopped state (E-stop control/status reflects the stopped condition on the RMS UI).
steps.healthy_condition: RMS remains stopped while you proceed with physical AGV handling and Hospital station remove/add steps.
steps.failure_condition: RMS continues running fleet movement while you attempt physical handling.

actions.label: E-stop RMS
actions.exact_action: E-stop the RMS.

steps.title: Release the AGV brake
steps.instruction: On the AGV that lost a tote, press the brake release.
steps.purpose: Enable safe physical movement of the AGV that lost a tote.
steps.expected_result: The AGV brake is released, allowing the AGV to be pushed.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV can be moved without fighting the brake.
steps.failure_condition: AGV does not move as expected because the brake release did not take effect.

actions.label: Press brake release
actions.exact_action: Press the brake release on the AGV that lost a tote.

steps.title: Push the AGV to the Hospital
steps.instruction: Push the AGV over to the Hospital.
steps.purpose: Move the AGV to the Hospital so it can be removed and re-added via the Hospital station PC/HMI workflow.
steps.expected_result: The AGV is physically positioned at the Hospital station area for the next remove/add step.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV is at the Hospital station area and ready for Hospital station PC/HMI remove/add actions.
steps.failure_condition: AGV cannot be positioned at the Hospital station area (e.g., blocked path).

actions.label: Push to Hospital
actions.exact_action: Push the AGV over to the Hospital.

steps.title: Remove and re-add the AGV at the Hospital station PC/HMI
steps.instruction: At the Hospital station PC, remove the AGV from the system, then add the AGV back into the system using the Hospital station PC workflow/HMI.
steps.purpose: Clear the AGV from the system and reintroduce it so it can be re-localized at the Inbound Hospital Station.
steps.expected_result: The AGV is removed and then inserted back into the system via the Hospital station PC/HMI workflow.
steps.healthy_condition: Hospital HMI workflow completes the remove and insert actions for the specific AGV ID you are recovering.
steps.failure_condition: Hospital HMI remove/add actions do not complete for the AGV ID (AGV not accepted back into the system).

actions.label: Remove AGV
actions.exact_action: At the Hospital station PC, remove the AGV from the system.

actions.label: Add AGV back
actions.exact_action: Then, add the AGV back into the system.

steps.title: Power-cycle the AGV
steps.instruction: Turn the AGV off, then turn it on again.
steps.purpose: Reset AGV state so it can become ready (green lights) for QR re-localization.
steps.expected_result: AGV has been turned off and then back on.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV begins its startup sequence after power on.
steps.failure_condition: AGV does not restart or does not proceed to the expected green-light ready state.

actions.label: Power off/on
actions.exact_action: Turn the AGV off, then turn it on again.

steps.title: Wait for AGV lights to turn green
steps.instruction: Wait for the AGV lights to turn green.
steps.purpose: Confirm the AGV is ready for QR re-localization.
steps.expected_result: AGV lights are green.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV lights are green, indicating ready/operational status after the power cycle.
steps.failure_condition: AGV lights do not turn green after the power cycle.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the AGV does not show green lights after the power cycle.

actions.label: Verify green lights
actions.exact_action: Wait for the AGV lights to turn green.

steps.title: Re-localize by rolling over the Inbound Hospital Station QR code
steps.instruction: Roll the AGV over the QR code in front of the Inbound Hospital Station.
steps.purpose: Re-localize the AGV at the Inbound Hospital Station so it can proceed with tote recovery/removal.
steps.expected_result: AGV has been rolled over the Inbound Hospital Station QR code after lights turned green.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV successfully re-localizes after rolling over the QR code.
steps.failure_condition: AGV does not successfully re-localize after rolling over the Inbound Hospital QR code.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the AGV does not successfully re-localize after rolling over the Inbound Hospital QR code.

actions.label: Roll over QR
actions.exact_action: Roll the AGV over the QR code in front of the Inbound Hospital Station.

steps.instruction: Locate the missing tote and bring it to the Hospital to remove it from the system.

steps.expected_result: The missing tote is located and removed from the system via the Hospital station workflow.
steps.healthy_condition: Tote removal is completed for the missing tote at the Hospital station.
steps.failure_condition: Missing tote cannot be located, or cannot be removed from the system via the Hospital station PC/HMI controls.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the missing tote cannot be located or cannot be removed/added via the Hospital station PC/HMI controls.

actions.label: Locate missing tote
actions.exact_action: Locate the missing tote and bring it to the Hospital to remove it from the system.

steps.title: Add the tote back into the system
steps.instruction: Add the tote back into the system using the Hospital station PC workflow/HMI.
steps.purpose: Reintroduce the tote so normal sorter flow can resume.
steps.expected_result: The tote is added back into the system via the Hospital station workflow.
steps.healthy_condition: Tote add action completes successfully for the tote you removed.
steps.failure_condition: Tote cannot be added back into the system via the Hospital station PC/HMI controls.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the missing tote cannot be located or cannot be removed/added via the Hospital station PC/HMI controls.

actions.label: Add tote

title: Clear AGV Motionless on Floor Fault Using RMS (If Needed), E-Stop Zone Map, and Blue RESET
summary: For an AGV motionless on the floor (fault), locate the faulted AGV (optionally using RMS to identify the AGV error), stop the appropriate E-stop zone using the E-stop zone map, remove the faulted AGV, pull the E-STOP, and press the blue RESET button to resume operation.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV is motionless on the floor and the issue is identified as a fault, requiring physical removal of the faulted AGV and an E-stop zone reset to resume system operation.

steps.title: Locate the faulted AGV (use RMS if needed)
steps.instruction: If the faulted AGV is not immediately obvious, use the RMS / fleet status UI to identify the AGV error/faulted unit.
steps.purpose: Identify which AGV is faulted so the correct E-stop zone can be stopped and the correct unit can be removed.
steps.expected_result: You have identified the faulted AGV that is motionless on the floor.
steps.healthy_condition: RMS indicates the faulted AGV/error state for the unit you are targeting for removal.
steps.failure_condition: RMS does not clearly identify the faulted AGV (or you cannot confidently determine which AGV is faulted).
stop_or_escalate_if: If RMS does not clearly identify the faulted AGV, escalate for assistance locating the faulted unit.

actions.label: Check RMS for faulted AGV
actions.exact_action: Reference RMS for AGV error (if needed to locate the faulted AGV).

steps.title: Stop the appropriate E-stop zone using the E-stop zone map
steps.instruction: Reference the E-stop zone map and press the E-STOP for the appropriate E-stop zone.
steps.purpose: Bring the correct zone to a stopped state before removing the faulted AGV.
steps.expected_result: The appropriate E-stop zone is stopped.
steps.healthy_condition: The E-stop you pressed corresponds to the zone for the faulted AGV identified in Step 1.
steps.failure_condition: You press the wrong E-stop zone (zone does not match the faulted AGV location).

actions.label: Press zone E-stop
actions.exact_action: Press E-STOP to stop the appropriate E-stop zone (per E-stop zone map).

steps.title: Remove the faulted AGV
steps.instruction: Remove the faulted AGV from the floor/system area.
steps.purpose: Clear the physical fault condition by removing the faulted AGV from the system/floor.
steps.expected_result: The faulted AGV has been removed.
steps.healthy_condition: The faulted AGV is no longer present in the faulted location/zone.
steps.failure_condition: The faulted AGV remains in place (fault condition not cleared).

actions.label: Remove AGV
actions.exact_action: Remove the faulted AGV.

steps.title: Pull the E-STOP
steps.instruction: Pull the E-STOP.
steps.purpose: Complete the E-stop reset sequence before pressing blue RESET.
steps.expected_result: The E-STOP has been pulled (reset sequence is ready for blue RESET).
steps.healthy_condition: E-STOP is in the pulled state as part of the reset procedure.
steps.failure_condition: E-STOP is not pulled (blue RESET is pressed without completing the sequence).

actions.label: Pull E-STOP
actions.exact_action: Pull E-STOP.

steps.title: Press the blue RESET button
steps.instruction: Press the blue RESET button.
steps.purpose: Reset the system so operation resumes after the faulted AGV is removed and E-stop is pulled.
steps.expected_result: The system resumes operation after the reset.
steps.healthy_condition: System operation resumes (no longer remains in the faulted/stopped state).
steps.failure_condition: System does not resume operation after pressing the blue RESET button.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the system does not resume operation after pressing the blue RESET button, escalate.

actions.label: Press blue RESET
actions.exact_action: Press the blue RESET button.

steps.title: Confirm the system resumes operation
steps.instruction: Confirm that the system resumes operation following the blue RESET.
steps.purpose: Verify recovery succeeded and the system is back to running.
steps.expected_result: Operation resumes.
steps.healthy_condition: System is running/operational after reset.
steps.failure_condition: System remains stopped/not resumed after reset.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the system does not resume operation after pressing the blue RESET button, escalate.

actions.label: Verify operation resumed
actions.exact_action: Confirm the system resumes operation.

title: Recover Non-Recoverable Fault: AGV Stuck Using Operator Station HMI (Visu_ManControl → CellIO Status → OUT W1 forced value)
summary: On the operator station HMI, verify the non-recoverable AGV-stuck fault by confirming the selected tipper shows OUT Fault Status = 82 on the CellIO Status screen. Then force OUT W1 to either 3 (continue work) or 32771 (send the AGV to the hospital) by entering the value, checking the enable checkbox, waiting 10 seconds, and unchecking. Finally, press CYCLE START to restart operation.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV remains at the tipper after tote-tipping is complete (non-recoverable fault), and the operator station HMI indicates the AGV-stuck condition that requires forcing OUT W1 via the CellIO Status screen.

steps.title: Navigate to Visu_ManControl
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_ManControl" screen.
steps.purpose: Open the operator station HMI screen that provides access to the CellIO Status screen for tipper I/O verification and forced-value recovery.
steps.expected_result: The "Visu_ManControl" screen is displayed on the operator station HMI.
steps.healthy_condition: The HMI is on the "Visu_ManControl" screen and the "CellIO Status" button is available for selection.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the "CellIO Status" button because the HMI is not on the "Visu_ManControl" screen.

actions.label: Open Visu_ManControl
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the "Visu_ManControl" screen.

steps.title: Open CellIO Status
steps.instruction: Press the "CellIO Status" button on the "Visu_ManControl" screen.
steps.purpose: Access the tipper-specific I/O status and forced-value controls needed to recover the AGV stuck fault.
steps.expected_result: The CellIO Status screen (cell control input/output values per tipper) is opened.
steps.healthy_condition: The CellIO Status screen shows tipper selection and the OUT Fault Status / OUT W1 forced value controls for the selected tipper.
steps.failure_condition: The CellIO Status screen does not open or the OUT Fault Status / OUT W1 forced value controls are not visible.

actions.label: Press CellIO Status
actions.exact_action: Press the "CellIO Status" button.

steps.title: Select the stuck tipper
steps.instruction: Select the tipper where the AGV is stuck.
steps.purpose: Ensure the OUT Fault Status and OUT W1 forced value controls apply to the specific tipper where the AGV is stuck.
steps.expected_result: The selected tipper on the CellIO Status screen corresponds to the tipper where the AGV is currently stuck.
steps.healthy_condition: The tipper selection reflects the correct stuck tipper, and the OUT Fault Status field updates for that tipper.
steps.failure_condition: A different tipper than the one with the stuck AGV is selected (leading to an incorrect OUT Fault Status value).

actions.label: Select stuck tipper
actions.exact_action: Select the tipper where the AGV is stuck.

steps.title: Verify OUT Fault Status = 82
steps.instruction: Verify the "OUT Fault Status" field shows value 82 for the selected stuck tipper.
steps.purpose: Confirm the fault condition matches the documented non-recoverable AGV stuck fault before applying the forced OUT W1 value.
steps.expected_result: "OUT Fault Status" shows value 82 for the selected tipper.
steps.healthy_condition: "OUT Fault Status" equals 82 on the CellIO Status screen for the selected tipper.
steps.failure_condition: "OUT Fault Status" is not 82 for the selected tipper.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if "OUT Fault Status" does not show value 82 for the selected stuck tipper.

actions.label: Check OUT Fault Status
actions.exact_action: The OUT Fault Status should have a value of 82.

steps.title: Enter OUT W1 forced value (3 or 32771)
steps.instruction: Ensure the correct tipper is selected, then enter a forced value in the "OUT W1" forced value box: use 3 if the tote and AGV are ready to continue working, or 32771 if the AGV needs to go to the hospital.
steps.purpose: Apply the documented forced value to OUT W1 to either continue work or send the AGV to the hospital, depending on the required outcome.
steps.expected_result: The "OUT W1" forced value box contains either 3 or 32771 as selected for the recovery outcome.
steps.healthy_condition: The forced value entered matches the intended recovery path: 3 for continue work, 32771 for hospital routing.
steps.failure_condition: The wrong forced value is entered for the intended outcome (e.g., 3 when the AGV must go to the hospital).

actions.label: Enter OUT W1 forced value
actions.exact_action: Enter a value of 3 in the OUT W1 forced value box if the tote and AGV are ready to continue working. If the AGV needs to go to the hospital, enter a value of 32771.

steps.title: Enable the forced OUT W1 value
steps.instruction: Check the box next to the value introduced in the forced value box.
steps.purpose: Apply the forced OUT W1 value by enabling it via the checkbox next to the introduced forced value.
steps.expected_result: The checkbox enabling the forced OUT W1 value is checked (enabled).
steps.healthy_condition: The forced-value enable checkbox is checked for the entered OUT W1 value.
steps.failure_condition: The checkbox is not checked (forced value not enabled).

actions.label: Check enable checkbox
actions.exact_action: Check the box next to the value introduced in the forced value box.

steps.title: Wait 10 seconds, then uncheck OUT W1 forced value
steps.instruction: Wait 10 seconds, then uncheck the box for value OUT W1.
steps.purpose: Apply the forced OUT W1 value for the documented duration, then remove the forced enable to complete the recovery action.
steps.expected_result: After 10 seconds, the OUT W1 forced-value enable checkbox is unchecked.
steps.healthy_condition: The forced-value checkbox transitions from checked to unchecked after the 10-second wait.
steps.failure_condition: The checkbox remains checked beyond 10 seconds, or it is unchecked too early.

actions.label: Uncheck after 10 seconds
actions.exact_action: Wait 10 seconds, then uncheck the box for value OUT W1.

steps.title: Press CYCLE START to restart operation
steps.instruction: Press "CYCLE START" to restart operation.
steps.purpose: Restart operation after applying the forced OUT W1 value to recover from the non-recoverable AGV stuck fault.
steps.expected_result: "CYCLE START" is pressed and operation restart is initiated.
steps.healthy_condition: The system proceeds with the restart sequence after CYCLE START (operator can observe the restart behavior on the operator station HMI).
steps.failure_condition: Operation does not restart as expected after pressing CYCLE START.

title: Recover Non-Recoverable Fault: AGV Stuck Using Operator Station HMI (Visu_ManControl → CellIO Status → OUT W1 forced value)

steps.title: Select the stuck tipper

actions.label: Select stuck tipper

steps.title: Verify OUT Fault Status = 82

steps.healthy_condition: "OUT Fault Status" equals 82 on the CellIO Status screen for the selected tipper.
steps.failure_condition: "OUT Fault Status" is not 82 for the selected tipper.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if "OUT Fault Status" does not show value 82 for the selected stuck tipper.

actions.label: Check OUT Fault Status
actions.exact_action: The OUT Fault Status should have a value of 82.

steps.title: Enter OUT W1 forced value (3 or 32771)
steps.instruction: Ensure the correct tipper is selected, then enter a forced value in the "OUT W1" forced value box: use 3 if the tote and AGV are ready to continue working, or 32771 if the AGV needs to go to the hospital.
steps.purpose: Apply the documented forced value to OUT W1 to either continue work or send the AGV to the hospital, depending on the required outcome.
steps.expected_result: The "OUT W1" forced value box contains either 3 or 32771 as selected for the recovery outcome.
steps.healthy_condition: The forced value entered matches the intended recovery path: 3 for continue work, 32771 for hospital routing.
steps.failure_condition: The wrong forced value is entered for the intended outcome (e.g., 3 when the AGV must go to the hospital).

actions.label: Enter OUT W1 forced value
actions.exact_action: Enter a value of 3 in the OUT W1 forced value box if the tote and AGV are ready to continue working. If the AGV needs to go to the hospital, enter a value of 32771.

steps.title: Enable the forced OUT W1 value

steps.healthy_condition: The forced-value enable checkbox is checked for the entered OUT W1 value.
steps.failure_condition: The checkbox is not checked (forced value not enabled).

actions.label: Check enable checkbox
actions.exact_action: Check the box next to the value introduced in the forced value box.

steps.title: Wait 10 seconds, then uncheck OUT W1 forced value
steps.instruction: Wait 10 seconds, then uncheck the box for value OUT W1.

steps.expected_result: After 10 seconds, the OUT W1 forced-value enable checkbox is unchecked.
steps.healthy_condition: The forced-value checkbox transitions from checked to unchecked after the 10-second wait.
steps.failure_condition: The checkbox remains checked beyond 10 seconds, or it is unchecked too early.

actions.label: Uncheck after 10 seconds
actions.exact_action: Wait 10 seconds, then uncheck the box for value OUT W1.

steps.title: Press CYCLE START to restart operation

steps.failure_condition: Operation does not restart as expected after pressing CYCLE START.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the fault does not clear after applying the forced value and restarting, escalate to Fortna support for further troubleshooting (do not continue repeated forced-value toggling without guidance).

actions.label: Restart operation

title: Start OptiSweep AGV System From Shut-down Mode (Reset Metrics → Start → Close out/Bag Out → Running)
summary: Use the OptiSweep system screen to bring the AGV system from Shut-down Mode into the normal “Running” state by verifying the required number of empty AGVs, resetting metrics, starting the system, performing close out (Bag Out) until the system returns to “Running,” and then shutting down when finished.
when_to_use: Use this procedure when the OptiSweep AGV system is in Shut-down Mode and you need to start it into normal “Running” operation using the documented start-up sequence (Reset metrics → Start → Close out/Bag Out → Running).

steps.title: Verify nine (9) empty AGVs are present (5 north, 4 south)
steps.instruction: Confirm there are nine (9) AGVs without totes in the system: five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south rack. If not, move an AGV into the zone missing an empty AGV, then add that AGV to RMS after moving it.
steps.purpose: Ensure the required precondition for starting the system is met (enough AGVs without totes in the north/south rack zones).
steps.expected_result: You have five (5) empty AGVs under the north rack and four (4) empty AGVs under the south rack (total nine (9) empty AGVs).
steps.healthy_condition: The empty-AGV counts match the required distribution: 5 north and 4 south.
steps.failure_condition: The system does not have nine (9) empty AGVs total, or the distribution is not 5 north and 4 south.

actions.label: Check empty AGV counts
actions.exact_action: Confirm there are nine (9) AGVs without totes in the system: five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south rack.

actions.label: Move AGV into missing empty zone (if needed)
actions.exact_action: Move an AGV into the zone missing an empty AGV, then add that AGV to the RMS after moving the AGV.

steps.title: Open the System in Shut-down Mode screen and verify Shut-down Mode
steps.instruction: Open the system screen shown as “System in Shut-down Mode” (Figure 5-1) and verify the system mode indicates Shut-down.
steps.purpose: Confirm you are starting from the correct system state (Shut-down Mode) before resetting metrics and starting.
steps.expected_result: The system mode indicator on the “System in Shut-down Mode” screen shows Shut-down.
steps.healthy_condition: System mode is displayed as Shut-down on the referenced system screen.
steps.failure_condition: The system mode is not Shut-down (e.g., already Running or in another state).

actions.label: Verify system mode
actions.exact_action: Open the system screen shown as "System in Shut-down Mode" (Figure 5-1) and verify the system mode indicates Shut-down.

steps.title: Reset metrics
steps.instruction: On the “System in Shut-down Mode” screen (Figure 5-1), use the control option to Reset metrics.
steps.purpose: Prepare the system for the start-up sequence by resetting metrics (also noted as making pulling reports easier).
steps.expected_result: Metrics are reset using the Reset metrics control on the system screen.
steps.healthy_condition: Reset metrics control is executed as part of the start-up sequence.
steps.failure_condition: Metrics are not reset before starting the system.

actions.label: Reset metrics
actions.exact_action: Reset the metrics.

steps.title: Start the system
steps.instruction: On the “System in Shut-down Mode” screen (Figure 5-1), use the control to Start the system.
steps.purpose: Transition the system from Shut-down Mode into the start-up process.
steps.expected_result: The system start control is executed as part of the start-up sequence.
steps.healthy_condition: System Startup is initiated from the Shut-down Mode screen.
steps.failure_condition: System does not progress toward close out/Bag Out completion after starting.

actions.label: Start system
actions.exact_action: Start the system.

steps.title: Perform close out (Bag Out) until system returns to Running
steps.instruction: Perform close out (Bag Out) and continue until the system status returns to “Running.”
steps.purpose: Complete the required close out (Bag Out) step so the system returns to normal “Running” operation.
steps.expected_result: After close out (Bag Out) is completed, the system status returns to “Running.”
steps.healthy_condition: System status transitions back to “Running” after Bag Out completes.
steps.failure_condition: The system does not return to “Running” after Bag Out.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop the procedure if the system does not return to "Running" after Bag Out; escalate to Fortna support for further troubleshooting.

actions.label: Close out (Bag Out)
actions.exact_action: Close out. After close out (Bag Out) is completed, the system goes back to "Running".

steps.title: Shut down when the start-up process is complete and you are done
steps.instruction: When the start-up process is complete and you are done with the procedure, shut down using the documented shut down step/control.
steps.purpose: Return the system to Shut-down when the start-up process is complete and you are finished with the procedure.
steps.expected_result: System shutdown is initiated using the documented shut down control/step.
steps.healthy_condition: System Shutdown is executed after the system has returned to Running and you are done with the procedure.
steps.failure_condition: Shutdown is not performed when the procedure is complete (leaving the system running when it should be shut down).

actions.label: Shut down system
actions.exact_action: 4. Shut down.

title: Start OptiSweep AGV System (Reset Metrics → Start System → Close Out/Bag Out → Verify Running → Shut Down)
summary: Perform the required AGV start-up prerequisites (nine empty AGVs: five under the north rack and four under the south rack), start the OptiSweep system 15 minutes before the sort, run the documented start sequence (Reset Metrics → Start System → Close Out/Bag Out), verify the system returns to the "Running" state after Bag Out, and then shut down.
when_to_use: Use to start the OptiSweep AGV system for an upcoming sort, ensuring the system is properly prepared (nine empty AGVs) and that the system transitions back to the "Running" state after close out (Bag Out).

steps.title: Verify nine empty AGVs are present (5 north / 4 south)
steps.instruction: Verify there are nine (9) AGVs without totes in the system: five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south rack.
steps.purpose: Ensure the documented prerequisite for starting the system is met (enough AGVs without totes in the north and south rack zones).
steps.expected_result: You confirm five (5) empty AGVs under the north rack and four (4) empty AGVs under the south rack.
steps.healthy_condition: North rack has 5 AGVs without totes and south rack has 4 AGVs without totes.
steps.failure_condition: Fewer than nine empty AGVs are present, or the north/south distribution is not 5 north and 4 south.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the nine empty AGV prerequisite cannot be met (5 under north rack, 4 under south rack), do not proceed until an empty AGV is moved into the missing zone and added to the RMS.

actions.label: Check empty AGV counts by rack zone
actions.exact_action: Verify there are nine (9) AGVs without totes in the system—five (5) under the north rack and four (4) under the south rack.

steps.title: Move an empty AGV into the missing zone and add it to RMS (if needed)
steps.instruction: If fewer than nine empty AGVs are present, move an AGV without a tote into the zone that is missing an empty AGV, then add that AGV to the RMS after moving it.
steps.purpose: Satisfy the prerequisite when the system is started without nine totes/empty AGVs by moving an empty AGV into the deficient zone and registering it in RMS.
steps.expected_result: The missing zone now has an empty AGV, and the moved AGV has been added to RMS.
steps.healthy_condition: After adding the moved AGV in RMS, the AGV is successfully registered (per the RMS add screen procedure, the AGV turns blue and its status is verified as "szonestaging").
steps.failure_condition: The missing zone remains without an empty AGV, or the moved AGV does not successfully register in RMS (e.g., does not turn blue / cannot be verified as "szonestaging").
stop_or_escalate_if: If the nine empty AGV prerequisite cannot be met (5 under north rack, 4 under south rack), do not proceed without moving an empty AGV into the missing zone and adding it to the RMS.

actions.label: Move empty AGV into deficient zone
actions.exact_action: Move an AGV without a tote into the zone that is missing an empty AGV.

actions.label: Add AGV to RMS
actions.exact_action: Make sure to add the AGV to the RMS after moving the AGV.

steps.title: Confirm start timing (15 minutes before sort starts)
steps.instruction: Confirm the system start will occur 15 minutes before the sort starts.
steps.purpose: Meet the documented timing requirement for starting the system relative to the sort.
steps.expected_result: You confirm the start time is set to occur 15 minutes before the sort begins.
steps.healthy_condition: System start is initiated at the required lead time (15 minutes before sort starts).
steps.failure_condition: System start is initiated too late (not 15 minutes before sort starts).

actions.label: Check timing vs sort start
actions.exact_action: Make sure to start the system 15 minutes before the sort starts.

steps.title: Reset metrics
steps.instruction: On the system control surface (System API Controls), perform the Reset Metrics step.
steps.purpose: Reset metrics as the first step in the documented start sequence (to make pulling reports easier).
steps.expected_result: Metrics have been reset (Reset Metrics action completed on the System API Controls screen).
steps.healthy_condition: Reset Metrics is executed as the first step in the sequence before starting the system.
steps.failure_condition: Reset Metrics is skipped or not executed before starting the system.

actions.label: Reset metrics
actions.exact_action: Reset the metrics.

steps.title: Start the system
steps.instruction: On the system control surface (System API Controls), start the system using the System Startup control.
steps.purpose: Start the OptiSweep system as the second step in the documented start sequence.
steps.expected_result: The system is placed into the running state via the System Startup control.
steps.healthy_condition: System Startup is executed after Reset Metrics and before Close Out (Bag Out).
steps.failure_condition: System Startup is not executed, or the system does not progress to the expected state for close out.

actions.label: Start system
actions.exact_action: Start the system.

steps.title: Perform close out (Bag Out)
steps.instruction: On the system control surface (System API Controls), perform Close Out (Bag Out) as the next step in the sequence.
steps.purpose: Execute the documented close out (Bag Out) step as part of the start-up sequence.
steps.expected_result: Close out (Bag Out) is completed.
steps.healthy_condition: Close Out (Bag Out) completes as the third step in the sequence.
steps.failure_condition: Close Out (Bag Out) is not completed.

actions.label: Close out (Bag Out)
actions.exact_action: Close out.

steps.title: Verify system returns to "Running" after Bag Out
steps.instruction: After close out (Bag Out) is completed, verify the system state returns to "Running".
steps.purpose: Confirm the required observable state transition after close out (Bag Out).
steps.expected_result: System state is "Running" after Bag Out completes.
steps.healthy_condition: System state shows "Running".
steps.failure_condition: System state does not return to "Running" after Bag Out is completed.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the system does not return to "Running" after close out (Bag Out), stop and escalate for support rather than continuing the sequence.

actions.label: Check system state
actions.exact_action: After close out (Bag Out) is completed, verify the system state returns to "Running".

steps.title: Shut down the system
steps.instruction: On the system control surface (System API Controls), shut down the system using the System Shutdown control.
steps.purpose: Complete the documented sequence by shutting down after verifying the system is back in "Running".
steps.expected_result: System shutdown is initiated/completed via the System Shutdown control.
steps.healthy_condition: Shutdown is performed as the final step after Bag Out and verification of "Running".
steps.failure_condition: Shutdown is not performed as the final step, or shutdown is attempted before Bag Out completion and "Running" verification.

actions.label: Shut down system
actions.exact_action: Shut down.

title: Recover Empty AGVs That Lost Tasks After RMS Restart (Remove/Re-add AGVs Twice)
summary: If empty AGVs lose their tasks after an RMS restart, stop RMS, remove and re-add the affected empty AGVs without totes twice, verify each AGV is in the "szonestaging" state on the HMI, press E-stop again when ready, then resume RMS.
when_to_use: Use when empty AGVs have lost their tasks because the RMS was restarted, and the recovery guidance calls for removing and re-adding the AGVs twice and confirming "szonestaging" before resuming RMS.

steps.title: E-stop RMS on the RMS / fleet status UI
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), press the E-stop for RMS.
steps.purpose: Stop RMS before performing the remove/re-add recovery cycle for empty AGVs that lost tasks after an RMS restart.
steps.expected_result: RMS is in an E-stopped state on the RMS / fleet status UI.
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS E-stop control is engaged/active on the RMS / fleet status UI.
steps.failure_condition: RMS is not stopped (E-stop does not engage) or the UI does not reflect an E-stopped state.
stop_or_escalate_if: If RMS E-stop cannot be engaged, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Press RMS E-stop
actions.exact_action: E-stop RMS.

steps.title: Remove and re-add empty AGVs without totes twice using Tote API Controls
steps.instruction: Using the Tote API Controls flow within the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), remove and re-add the affected empty AGVs without totes twice.
steps.purpose: Restore task assignment for empty AGVs that lost tasks after RMS restart by performing the required remove/re-add cycle twice.
steps.expected_result: Each affected empty AGV has been removed and re-added twice via the RMS Tote API Controls flow.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGVs proceed through the expected post-add state progression (next step will verify "szonestaging").
steps.failure_condition: The AGVs do not progress as expected after the remove/re-add cycle, or the remove/re-add operation cannot be completed.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the remove/re-add cycle cannot be completed twice, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Remove/re-add AGVs twice (no totes)
actions.exact_action: Remove and re-add AGVs without totes twice. (See "Tote API Controls" on page 26.)

steps.title: Verify AGVs are in "szonestaging" on the HMI
steps.instruction: If the system needs to be restarted, verify on the HMI (hospital_hmi) that the affected AGVs are in the "szonestaging" state by referencing the AGV state/value on the HMI.
steps.purpose: Ensure the required AGV state is achieved before pressing E-stop again and resuming RMS.
steps.expected_result: The affected empty AGVs show AGV status/state value "szonestaging" on the HMI.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV status is "szonestaging" for the affected empty AGVs.
steps.failure_condition: Any affected empty AGV is not in "szonestaging" state.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if AGVs cannot be brought to "szonestaging".

actions.label: Check AGV state = szonestaging
actions.exact_action: Verify AGV status is "szonestaging". (Reference AGV state on HMI.)

steps.title: Press E-stop again when ready to resume
steps.instruction: When the affected empty AGVs are confirmed in "szonestaging" on the HMI, press the E-stop again on the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui) when ready to resume.
steps.purpose: Complete the required stop/resume sequence after the AGVs are confirmed in "szonestaging".
steps.expected_result: The RMS E-stop control is pressed again (as indicated by the RMS / fleet status UI).
steps.healthy_condition: E-stop again action is accepted and the system is ready for RMS resumption.
steps.failure_condition: E-stop again cannot be performed or RMS does not proceed to the resume-ready state.
stop_or_escalate_if: Do not resume RMS until AGVs are confirmed in "szonestaging" state on the HMI.

actions.label: Press E-stop again
actions.exact_action: Press the E-stop again when ready to resume.

steps.title: Resume RMS on the RMS / fleet status UI
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), resume RMS.
steps.purpose: Restart RMS operations after the recovery cycle and state verification.
steps.expected_result: RMS resumes/starts successfully on the RMS / fleet status UI.
steps.healthy_condition: RMS is resumed and the affected empty AGVs are no longer in the lost-task condition.
steps.failure_condition: Lost-task condition persists after resuming RMS.

steps.title: Press RESET on the operator station HMI

steps.purpose: Initiate the automatic referencing sequence for the tipper axes.
steps.expected_result: The automatic referencing sequence is initiated (next step is AUTO REF to reference all tipper axes).
steps.healthy_condition: The HMI is ready to proceed to AUTO REF for referencing.
steps.failure_condition: RESET does not initiate the referencing workflow (cannot proceed to a referencing state).

steps.healthy_condition: The HMI shows the 'R' icons associated with referencing.
steps.failure_condition: Referencing does not progress (no indication of 'R' icons changing during the referencing process).

actions.label: Press AUTO REF
actions.exact_action: Press AUTO REF to reference all of the axes of the tippers.

steps.title: Confirm referencing completion by verifying 'R' icons turn green

steps.failure_condition: AUTO cannot be engaged after referencing completion.

actions.label: Press AUTO

steps.title: Press CYCLE START to restart operation
steps.instruction: Press CYCLE START on the operator station HMI to restart operation.

steps.healthy_condition: Referencing progresses and the 'R' icons are ready to change state when referencing completes.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the 'R' icons do not turn green, do not proceed to AUTO/CYCLE START; stop and escalate for support.

steps.failure_condition: The 'R' icons do not turn green.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the 'R' icons do not turn green, do not proceed to AUTO/CYCLE START; stop and escalate for support.

steps.title: Navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) on the operator station HMI
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen using the F3 key.
steps.purpose: Open the correct operator station HMI screen used for stopping the automatic tipping cycle prior to manual maintenance positioning.
steps.expected_result: The operator station HMI is displaying the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen.
steps.healthy_condition: You are on the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) where the CYCLE STOP control is available.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot reach the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) or the screen shown is not the "Visu_Dual_MCP" interface.

actions.label: Open Visu_Dual_MCP (F3)
actions.exact_action: navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3)

steps.title: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the automatic tipping cycle
steps.instruction: On the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen, press CYCLE STOP.
steps.purpose: Stop the automatic tipping cycle so the end effector can be moved into position for maintenance procedures.
steps.expected_result: The automatic tipping cycle is stopped after pressing CYCLE STOP.
steps.healthy_condition: After pressing CYCLE STOP, the automatic tipping cycle is no longer running (cycle has stopped).
steps.failure_condition: The automatic tipping cycle does not stop after pressing CYCLE STOP.
