title: Recover an AGV from a "Bump" fault (Exception Codes 21057/21060) using RMS E-stop and AGV RESET
summary: When an AGV cannot be recovered by Geek+ and the RMS shows an AGV "Bump" fault (Exception Codes 21057 or 21060), stop RMS, remove the obstruction, hold the AGV RESET button for two seconds to clear the fault, press E-stop again, and resume RMS.
when_to_use: Use this procedure when the RMS / fleet status UI shows an AGV "Bump" fault and the exception code is 21057 or 21060, and the AGV needs on-site recovery by removing the obstruction and resetting the AGV.

steps.title: Identify the AGV "Bump" fault and confirm the Exception Code (21057 or 21060)
steps.instruction: In the RMS / fleet status UI, locate the AGV "Bump" fault screen and confirm the Exception Code shown is 21057 or 21060.
steps.purpose: Confirm the fault type and exception code so the correct recovery sequence is used.
steps.expected_result: The RMS "Bump" fault screen for the affected AGV shows Exception Code 21057 (Robot front collision bar triggers) or 21060 (robot triggers the obstacle avoidance).
steps.healthy_condition: The active fault shown on the RMS "Bump" fault screen matches 21057 or 21060 for the intended AGV.
steps.failure_condition: The RMS fault screen shows a different exception code than 21057/21060, or the "Bump" fault screen cannot be found for the affected AGV.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the exception code is not 21057 or 21060, stop and use the appropriate recovery procedure for that fault.

actions.label: Verify Exception Code
actions.exact_action: Identify the AGV "Bump" fault screen and confirm the exception code shown is 21057 or 21060.

steps.title: E-stop the RMS
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI, activate the E-stop function.
steps.purpose: Put RMS into a stopped state before physical obstruction removal and AGV reset.
steps.expected_result: RMS is in an E-stopped state (E-stop activated) while the "Bump" fault recovery sequence proceeds.
steps.healthy_condition: E-stop is active and the recovery sequence is not attempted while RMS is running.
steps.failure_condition: E-stop is not activated (RMS continues running) while attempting obstruction removal or AGV RESET.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot reliably activate RMS E-stop, stop and escalate for further recovery steps.

actions.label: Activate RMS E-stop
actions.exact_action: E-stop the RMS.

steps.title: Remove the obstruction that caused the bump
steps.instruction: Remove the physical obstruction causing the bump (for example, at the AGV/robot front collision bar area).
steps.purpose: Clear the physical cause of the bump so the AGV can recover.
steps.expected_result: The physical obstruction is removed so the AGV/robot front collision bar area is clear.
steps.healthy_condition: The obstruction is cleared and the area is safe for the AGV to be reset and RMS to be resumed.
steps.failure_condition: The obstruction remains in place or cannot be removed safely.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot safely remove the obstruction, do not proceed with reset/resume; escalate.

actions.label: Remove obstruction
actions.exact_action: Remove the obstruction.

steps.title: Click and hold AGV RESET for two seconds to clear the fault
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI, click the AGV RESET button and hold it for two (2) seconds.
steps.purpose: Clear the "Bump" fault on the affected AGV.
steps.expected_result: The AGV RESET action is held for two seconds to clear the fault.
steps.healthy_condition: The fault-clearing action completes (as indicated by the recovery sequence proceeding to the next step).
steps.failure_condition: AGV RESET is not held for two seconds, or the fault does not clear after the sequence.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the "Bump" fault does not clear after the two-second AGV RESET, stop and escalate for further recovery steps.

actions.label: Hold AGV RESET
actions.exact_action: Click the AGV RESET button for two (2) seconds to clear the fault.

steps.title: Press E-stop again
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI, press E-stop again.
steps.purpose: Follow the required recovery sequence after AGV RESET.
steps.expected_result: RMS E-stop is pressed again as part of the recovery sequence.
steps.healthy_condition: The sequence proceeds exactly as specified: E-stop again after AGV RESET.
steps.failure_condition: E-stop is not pressed again after AGV RESET.

actions.label: Activate RMS E-stop again
actions.exact_action: Press E-stop again.

steps.title: Resume RMS
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI, resume RMS to normal operation.
steps.purpose: Return RMS to normal operation after the fault is cleared.
steps.expected_result: RMS is resumed to normal operation and the affected AGV is no longer showing the active "Bump" fault.
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS no longer displays the active "Bump" fault for the affected AGV and RMS is back in normal operation.
steps.failure_condition: The "Bump" fault remains active after the sequence, or RMS cannot be resumed to normal operation.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the "Bump" fault does not clear after the two-second AGV RESET, stop and escalate for further recovery steps.

actions.label: Resume RMS
actions.exact_action: Resume RMS.

title: Install Counter-balance (CB) Weights and Restart Operator Station
summary: Securely install the counter-balance (CB) weights using the specified screws/torque, ensure side guarding is reinstalled, and restart the operator station so the system can resume operation.
when_to_use: Use when CB weights have been removed and must be reinstalled, and the operator station must be restarted to resume operation.

steps.title: Hold the CB weights in place
steps.instruction: At the tipper carriage counter-balance weights location, hold the CB weights in place with two people.
steps.purpose: Prevent the CB weights from falling during installation of the fasteners.
steps.expected_result: CB weights are held securely in position at the mounting location while the four M10 socket head screws are installed.
steps.healthy_condition: Weights remain stable in the intended mounting position (no uncontrolled drop).
steps.failure_condition: CB weights cannot be held in place during screw installation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the CB weights cannot be held in place during screw installation.

actions.label: Hold CB weights
actions.exact_action: Hold the CB weights in place.

steps.title: Install four M10 socket head screws with lock washers and tighten to ~51 Nm
steps.instruction: Install the four (4) M10 socket head screws with the lock washers and tighten to approximately ~51 Nm (65 ft-lbs).
steps.purpose: Secure the CB weights to the carriage using the specified fasteners and torque.
steps.expected_result: All four CB weight fasteners are installed with lock washers and tightened to ~51 Nm (65 ft-lbs).
steps.healthy_condition: Torque wrench indicates tightening to ~51 Nm (65 ft-lbs) for each of the four screws; lock washers are present under the screw heads.
steps.failure_condition: Tightening cannot reach the specified ~51 Nm (65 ft-lbs).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if tightening cannot reach the specified ~51 Nm (65 ft-lbs).

actions.label: Install and torque screws
actions.exact_action: install the four (4) M10 socket head screws with the lock washer. Tighten to ~51 Nm (65 ft-lbs).

steps.title: Observe acceptable carriage movement if the gripper is not mounted
steps.instruction: After the weights are in place, if the gripper is not yet mounted, observe the carriage movement; it may begin to move and this movement is acceptable because the weights will drift to the lower hard stop.
steps.purpose: Confirm the system behaves as expected when the gripper is not yet mounted (weights drift to the lower hard stop).
steps.expected_result: If the gripper is not mounted, carriage movement occurs and the weights drift to the lower hard stop.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriage movement proceeds toward the lower hard stop (no indication of abnormal behavior described in the procedure).
steps.failure_condition: Carriage movement does not drift to the lower hard stop as described.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if carriage movement does not drift to the lower hard stop as described.

actions.label: Observe carriage drift
actions.exact_action: the carriage may begin to move. The movement is acceptable as the weights will drift to the lower hard stop.

steps.title: Reinstall top and/or bottom side guarding if necessary
steps.instruction: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side guarding if necessary.
steps.purpose: Restore guarding to the configuration required for safe operation.
steps.expected_result: Top and/or bottom side guarding panels are reinstalled (as needed) after CB weight installation.
steps.healthy_condition: Side guarding is reinstalled and appears aligned/secure (no misalignment/unsafe condition).
steps.failure_condition: Side guarding cannot be reinstalled or appears misaligned/unsafe after reinstallation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if side guarding cannot be reinstalled or appears misaligned/unsafe after reinstallation.

actions.label: Reinstall side guarding
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side guarding, if necessary.

steps.title: Restart the operator station
steps.instruction: Restart the operator station (manual references “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
steps.purpose: Bring the operator station back to a running state after mechanical work is complete.
steps.expected_result: Operator station restarts successfully after CB weight installation and guarding reinstallation.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator station is in a restarted/running state (no restart failure indicated).
steps.failure_condition: Operator station does not restart after completing the installation and guarding steps.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the operator station does not restart after completing the installation and guarding steps, escalate to FORTNA support for the appropriate restart/troubleshooting procedure.

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

title: Remove Counter-balance (CB) Weights From OptiSweep Tipper Carriage
summary: Use a two-person, LOTO-protected mechanical procedure to remove the counter-balance (CB) weight assembly from the OptiSweep tipper carriage by removing four M10 socket head screws while supporting the ~20 kg weights during the final fastener removal, then allow the carriage/gripper to drift to the lower hard stop.
when_to_use: When you need to remove the OptiSweep tipper counter-balance (CB) weight assembly (CB weights) from the tipper carriage using the documented LOTO and fastener removal steps.

steps.title: Confirm two-person setup and required PPE/tools
steps.instruction: Before approaching the OptiSweep tipper carriage, confirm you have two people available and the required PPE/tools: safety glasses, gloves; 16-mm hex wrench; 3/8-in. wrench/socket; and the replacement part CB weights.
steps.purpose: Ensure the required two-person support and correct tools/PPE are available before starting LOTO and fastener removal.
steps.expected_result: Two people are available and the required PPE/tools are ready for use at the tipper carriage.
steps.healthy_condition: You can proceed to LOTO and fastener removal without needing to stop to find PPE/tools.
steps.failure_condition: You do not have two people available or any required PPE/tool/part is missing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if you cannot maintain the required two-person setup for the procedure.

actions.label: Verify two-person and tool readiness
actions.exact_action: Confirm you have two people available and the required PPE/tools: safety glasses, gloves; 16-mm hex wrench; 3/8-in. wrench/socket; replacement part CB weights.

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.instruction: LOTO the tipper using the manual reference "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" (page 2).
steps.purpose: De-energize and secure the tipper station for safe mechanical work.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is LOTO-protected prior to removing the CB weight fasteners.
steps.healthy_condition: You have completed the LOTO step and are ready to remove the CB weight fasteners.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to remove CB weight fasteners without completing LOTO.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if LOTO is not completed before fastener removal.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove top and/or bottom side guarding if necessary
steps.instruction: Remove the top and/or bottom side guarding, if necessary, to access the CB weights.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the CB weights and their mounting fasteners.
steps.expected_result: CB weights mounting area is accessible for locating and removing the four M10 socket head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: You can clearly access the CB weights and fasteners without obstruction.
steps.failure_condition: Guarding remains in place such that the CB weight fasteners cannot be accessed safely.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if you cannot access the CB weight fasteners safely.

actions.label: Remove guarding as needed
actions.exact_action: Remove the top and/or bottom side guarding, if necessary.

steps.title: Locate the four M10 socket head screws holding the CB weights
steps.instruction: Locate the four (4) M10 socket head screws holding the CB weights in place (including lock washers and counterbalance plates as shown in Figure 7-4).
steps.purpose: Identify the exact fasteners to remove the CB weight assembly.
steps.expected_result: All four M10 socket head screws are identified and reachable for removal.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the four M10 socket head screws and associated lock washers on the CB weight assembly.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot identify all four M10 socket head screws or access them for removal.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if you cannot locate all four M10 socket head screws.

actions.label: Identify CB weight fasteners
actions.exact_action: Locate the four (4) M10 socket head screws holding the CB weights in place.

steps.title: Remove the four M10 socket head screws while supporting the weights during the 4th fastener removal
steps.instruction: Remove the four (4) M10 socket head screws holding the CB weights in place. As you remove the 4th (last) fastener, hold the weights so they do not fall. The weights are about 20 kg (44 lb) total.
steps.purpose: Safely detach the CB weights without dropping them.
steps.expected_result: The CB weights are removed without dropping during removal of the 4th (last) fastener.
steps.healthy_condition: During the final fastener removal, the weights remain securely supported by the two-person team and do not fall.
steps.failure_condition: The CB weights are not securely supported during the 4th fastener removal (risk of dropping).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the CB weights cannot be securely supported during removal of the 4th fastener (risk of dropping).

actions.label: Remove M10 fasteners
actions.exact_action: Remove the four (4) M10 socket head screws holding the CB weights in place.

actions.label: Support weights during final fastener removal
actions.exact_action: As the 4th fastener is removed, hold the weights so they do not fall.

steps.title: Observe carriage movement after CB weights removal (drift to lower hard stop)
steps.instruction: After the weights are removed, observe the carriage movement. Movement is acceptable because the gripper will drift to the lower hard stop.
steps.purpose: Confirm the expected post-removal mechanical behavior.
steps.expected_result: After CB weights removal, the carriage/gripper drifts to the lower hard stop.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriage movement occurs and the gripper drifts to the lower hard stop as expected.
steps.failure_condition: The carriage/gripper does not drift to the lower hard stop after the weights are removed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the carriage/gripper does not drift to the lower hard stop after the weights are removed.

actions.label: Visual observation of drift
actions.exact_action: Observe the carriage movement: movement is acceptable as the gripper will drift to the lower hard stop.

title: Replace ClearLink (CLINK) Controller by Transferring Connections and Mounting New Unit
summary: Safely replace a ClearLink (CLINK) controller by transferring all existing connections from the old controller to the new controller, mounting the new controller in the box/stand using the specified screws, reinstalling side panels, and preparing the operator station to restart.
when_to_use: Use when a ClearLink (CLINK) controller needs replacement and you must transfer the existing wiring connections to the new controller, then remount and secure the controller and side panels before restarting the operator station.

steps.title: Identify the old and new ClearLink (CLINK) controllers
steps.instruction: Identify the old ClearLink (CLINK) controller to be replaced and the new ClearLink (CLINK) controller to be installed.
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct units are used so connections are transferred to the intended replacement controller.
steps.expected_result: You have correctly identified both the old CLINK controller (to remove/transfer from) and the new CLINK controller (to receive the transferred connections).
steps.healthy_condition: The old and new controllers are clearly distinguishable and you are prepared to match each cable/connection to the corresponding port on the new unit.
steps.failure_condition: Uncertainty about which controller is old vs. new, or inability to match connection points/ports for the transfer.

actions.label: Confirm controller identities
actions.exact_action: Identify the old ClearLink (CLINK) controller and the new ClearLink (CLINK) controller to be installed.

steps.title: Transfer all connections from the old controller to the new controller
steps.instruction: Transfer all the connections from the old controller to the new controller, matching the connection points/ports so each cable lands on the corresponding port on the new unit.
steps.purpose: Preserve the existing wiring by moving each cable to the corresponding port on the replacement controller.
steps.expected_result: All cables are connected to the new CLINK controller on the corresponding ports (no missing connections).
steps.healthy_condition: Each cable is landed on the matching port on the new controller; connection transfer is complete.
steps.failure_condition: Any connection cannot be transferred to the corresponding port on the new controller.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if any connection cannot be transferred to the corresponding port on the new controller.

actions.label: Match and transfer cable connections
actions.exact_action: Transfer all the connections from the old controller to the new controller (match the connection points/ports so each cable lands on the corresponding port on the new unit).

steps.title: Place the new controller in the box and fasten with two (2) M5 socket-head screws
steps.instruction: Place the new controller in the box and fasten it with the two (2) M5 socket-head screws.
steps.purpose: Secure the controller to the controller box using the specified fasteners.
steps.expected_result: The new CLINK controller is secured inside the box using exactly two (2) M5 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Controller is seated in the box and the two M5 socket-head screws are installed.
steps.failure_condition: Controller is not secured with the specified two (2) M5 socket-head screws, or the controller cannot be fastened as specified.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the controller/box cannot be secured with the specified screws.

actions.label: Install M5 screws
actions.exact_action: fasten with the two (2) M5 socket-head screws.

steps.expected_result: The control box is positioned on the stand using the M8 button-head screws, with excess cable routed back into the stand and no wires pinched.
steps.healthy_condition: Cables are not pinched at the stand/box interface; excess cable is managed inside the stand.
steps.failure_condition: Cables appear pinched, or the control box cannot be positioned with safe cable routing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if cables appear pinched.

actions.label: Mount box and check cable routing
actions.exact_action: Hang the control box on the M8 button-head screws on the stand, ensuring excess cable is fed back into the stand and not pinch any wires.

steps.title: Tighten the four (4) M8 button-head screws securing the controller box to the stand
steps.instruction: Tighten the four (4) M8 button-head screws securing the controller box to the stand.
steps.purpose: Ensure the controller box is firmly secured to the stand.
steps.expected_result: All four (4) M8 button-head screws are tightened and the controller box is secured to the stand.
steps.healthy_condition: No looseness at the controller box mounting points; all four M8 screws are installed and tightened.
steps.failure_condition: Any of the four M8 screws cannot be tightened as required, or the box is not secured.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the controller/box cannot be secured with the specified screws.

actions.label: Tighten M8 screws
actions.exact_action: Tighten the four (4) M8 button-head screws securing the controller box to the stand.

steps.title: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels if necessary
steps.instruction: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.
steps.purpose: Restore the station enclosure after controller installation.
steps.expected_result: The top and/or bottom side panels are reinstalled as needed to close the station.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panels are in place (as applicable) after the controller replacement.
steps.failure_condition: Side panels are left off when they were required to be reinstalled.

actions.label: Reinstall side panels
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.

steps.title: Restart the operator station (handoff to “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66)
steps.instruction: Restart the operator station (referenced as “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
steps.purpose: Bring the operator station back online after the physical replacement and panel reinstallation.
steps.expected_result: The operator station restart sequence is initiated/completed per the referenced “Starting The Operator Station” procedure.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator station is restarted and ready for normal operation per the referenced procedure.
steps.failure_condition: Operator station does not restart successfully (exact observable failure conditions are not provided in the excerpt).

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).

title: Remove and unplug Controller PCA in a tipper station (Controller PCA Replacement — Removal)
summary: Safely remove the Controller PCA from an OptiSweep tipper station by applying LOTO, accessing the controller box, loosening the controller box mounting screws, removing the ribbon cable retainer screws, and unplugging the PCA connections (FFC, ribbon cable, and three Molex connectors) so the assembly is ready for replacement.
when_to_use: When performing Controller PCA Replacement — Removal on an OptiSweep tipper station and you must remove/unplug the Controller PCA connections for replacement.

steps.title: Apply LOTO to the tipper
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely locked out before touching internal components.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out (LOTO confirmed) before proceeding to internal components.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is confirmed applied to the tipper prior to any internal access.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confirm LOTO is applied to the tipper before touching internal components.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if you cannot confirm LOTO is applied to the tipper before touching internal components.

actions.label: Perform LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the controller box and mounting hardware inside the tipper station.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (when needed) and the motor access area is reachable.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel is removed cleanly using the specified nine (9) self-tapping securing screws (3/8-in. wrench/socket).
steps.failure_condition: Side panel cannot be removed as expected (e.g., screws count does not match nine (9) self-tapping securing screws).

actions.label: Check if side panel removal is needed
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Loosen the four M8 button-head screws to release the controller box
steps.instruction: Loosen the four (4) M8 button-head screws that secure the controller box. Do not remove the fasteners—loosen them so the controller box can be lifted off the fasteners.
steps.purpose: Free the controller box so it can be lifted off the fasteners without removing the fasteners.
steps.expected_result: Controller box is released such that it can be lifted off after loosening the four (4) M8 button-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: All four (4) M8 button-head screws are loosened (not removed) and the controller box can be lifted off the fasteners.
steps.failure_condition: Controller box cannot be lifted after loosening the four (4) M8 button-head screws (do not force).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the controller box cannot be lifted after loosening the four M8 button-head screws (do not force).

actions.label: Loosen controller box screws
actions.exact_action: Loosen the four (4) M8 button-head screws to release the controller box. The fasteners do not need to be removed, only loosened, and the box can be lifted off the fasteners.

steps.title: Remove the two M3 socket-head screws holding the ribbon cable retainer
steps.instruction: Remove the two (2) M3 socket-head screws holding the ribbon cable retainer in place.
steps.purpose: Release the ribbon cable retainer so the ribbon cable connection can be unplugged.
steps.expected_result: Ribbon cable retainer is released after removing the two (2) M3 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Both M3 socket-head screws are removed and the retainer is free to release the ribbon cable.
steps.failure_condition: Screws/retainers do not match the documented counts (2x M3) or the retainer does not release as expected.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to FORTNA support if screws/retainers do not match the documented counts (4x M8, 2x M3).

actions.label: Remove ribbon cable retainer screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the two (2) M3 socket-head screws holding the ribbon cable retainer in place.

steps.title: Unplug all PCA connections (FFC, ribbon cable, and three Molex connectors)
steps.instruction: Unplug all connections from the PCA: FFC, ribbon cable, and the three Molex connectors.
steps.purpose: Disconnect the Controller PCA from all electrical/mechanical connections so it can be removed and replaced.
steps.expected_result: All PCA connections are unplugged: FFC and ribbon cable are disconnected, and three Molex connectors are unplugged.
steps.healthy_condition: Connections unplug without excessive force; the PCA connection points are visibly disconnected (FFC/ribbon cable removed from their connection points; three Molex connectors unplugged).
steps.failure_condition: Any PCA connections cannot be unplugged without excessive force.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if any PCA connections cannot be unplugged without excessive force or if screws/retainers do not match the documented counts (4x M8, 2x M3).
Escalate to FORTNA support if any PCA connections cannot be unplugged without excessive force or if screws/retainers do not match the documented counts (4x M8, 2x M3).

actions.label: Unplug PCA connections
actions.exact_action: Unplug all the connections from the PCA (FFC, ribbon cable, three Molex connectors).

title: Recover a Faulted AGV Carrying a Tote (RMS stop → Hospital HMI remove → re-add → resume RMS)
summary: When an AGV is faulted while carrying a tote, stop RMS, remove the faulted AGV from RMS, remove the AGV via the Hospital HMI, add the AGV back into RMS, press E-stop again, and resume RMS.
when_to_use: Use this recovery procedure when an AGV is faulted while carrying a tote and you need to restore normal RMS operation by removing the faulted AGV from RMS, removing it at the Hospital HMI, re-adding it to RMS, and resuming RMS.

steps.title: E-stop RMS
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI, perform an E-stop for RMS.
steps.purpose: Stop RMS movement before removing the faulted AGV and tote handling at the Hospital.
steps.expected_result: RMS is in an E-stopped state (E-stop RMS action is applied on the RMS UI).
steps.healthy_condition: RMS is stopped (E-stop RMS state active) so you can safely remove the faulted AGV from RMS.
steps.failure_condition: RMS is not stopped (E-stop RMS action does not take effect), preventing safe removal/recovery actions.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot place RMS into the E-stop state, stop and escalate.

actions.label: E-stop RMS
actions.exact_action: E-stop RMS.

steps.title: Remove the faulted AGV from RMS
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI, use the “AGV API Controls” controls to remove the faulted AGV from RMS (enter the AGV ID and use the Remove AGV action).
steps.purpose: Remove the faulted AGV from RMS so it can be handled at the Hospital.
steps.expected_result: The faulted AGV is removed from the system via the AGV API Controls Remove AGV action.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGV is no longer present/active in RMS after the Remove AGV action (as reflected by the RMS AGV management view).
steps.failure_condition: The AGV cannot be removed from RMS using AGV API Controls (removal action does not succeed).
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the faulted AGV cannot be removed from RMS.

actions.label: Remove AGV (AGV API Controls)
actions.exact_action: Remove AGV An AGV can be removed from the system by entering the AGV ID.

steps.title: Remove the AGV at the Hospital HMI
steps.instruction: Take the tote to the Hospital and remove the AGV via the Hospital HMI using the “Add/Remove AGV” screen.
steps.purpose: Physically take the tote to the Hospital and remove the AGV via the Hospital HMI.
steps.expected_result: The AGV is removed from the system at the Hospital via the Hospital HMI Add/Remove AGV screen.
steps.healthy_condition: Hospital HMI Add/Remove AGV workflow completes for the AGV being removed (AGV removal action executed on the screen).
steps.failure_condition: Hospital HMI does not successfully remove the AGV.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the Hospital HMI does not successfully remove the AGV.

actions.label: Remove AGV (Hospital HMI Add/Remove AGV)
actions.exact_action: The "Add/Remove AGV Screen" is used to add a removed AGV to the system or remove an AGV from the system.

steps.title: Add the AGV back into RMS
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI, use the “AGV API Controls” controls to add the AGV back into RMS (enter the AGV ID and use the Recover AGV action).
steps.purpose: Reintroduce the recovered AGV into RMS so fleet operation can resume.
steps.expected_result: The AGV is added back into the system via the AGV API Controls Recover AGV action.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGV is present/active in RMS after the Recover AGV action (as reflected by the RMS AGV management view).
steps.failure_condition: The AGV cannot be added back into RMS using AGV API Controls.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if RMS cannot be resumed after re-adding the AGV.

actions.label: Recover AGV (AGV API Controls)
actions.exact_action: Recover AGV Enter an AGV ID to add it to the system.

steps.title: Press E-stop again on RMS
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI, press E-stop again on RMS.
steps.purpose: Apply the E-stop again after re-adding the AGV, per the fault recovery sequence.
steps.expected_result: RMS E-stop is pressed again (E-stop RMS action applied a second time).
steps.healthy_condition: RMS remains in the E-stopped state after the second E-stop press, consistent with the recovery sequence.
steps.failure_condition: Second E-stop press does not take effect.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot apply the second E-stop, stop and escalate.

actions.label: E-stop RMS (second press)
actions.exact_action: Press the E-Stop again.

steps.title: Resume RMS
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI, resume RMS using the “Starting the System” procedure controls.
steps.purpose: Resume normal RMS operation after the faulted AGV has been removed, handled at the Hospital, and re-added.
steps.expected_result: RMS resumes after the faulted AGV has been removed from RMS, removed at the Hospital HMI, and re-added into RMS.
steps.healthy_condition: RMS is running again (system resumes operation) following the recovery sequence.
steps.failure_condition: RMS cannot be resumed after re-adding the AGV.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if RMS cannot be resumed after re-adding the AGV.

actions.label: Resume RMS
actions.exact_action: Resume RMS. (See "Starting the System" on page 65.)

title: Replace Flat-Flex Cable (FFC) at the A-axis PCA on a LOTOed tipper station
summary: Replace the flat-flex cable (FFC) connected to the A-axis PCA on a tipper station that has been LOTOed. Use the correct replacement part and ensure the correct left/right ClearLink controller hardware is installed (left/right are not interchangeable due to different IP addresses). The procedure removes the two FFC clamps (four M3 socket-head screws), unplugs/replugs the FFC, then reinstalls the clamps and the station side panel (nine self-tapping securing screws).
when_to_use: Use when you need to restore correct tipper station operation by replacing the flat-flex cable (FFC) connected to the A-axis PCA on a tipper station that is taken out of service via LOTO.
not_for: Do not proceed if you cannot confirm the correct left/right controller hardware for the tipper station (left/right ClearLink controllers are not interchangeable due to different IP addresses).
Do not proceed if the FFC cannot be unplugged/plugged cleanly or the clamps cannot be resecured with the four (4) M3 socket-head screws.

steps.title: Identify the correct tipper station side/controller to service (left vs right)
steps.instruction: Before starting the hardware replacement, confirm you are servicing the correct tipper station side/controller (left vs right). Do not assume left/right controller hardware can be swapped.
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct controller-side hardware is used because left/right ClearLink controllers are not interchangeable due to different IP addresses.
steps.expected_result: You have confirmed the correct left/right controller hardware for the specific tipper station you are servicing.
steps.healthy_condition: The controller-side hardware for the tipper station matches the correct left/right unit (not interchangeable because IP addresses differ).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confirm the correct left/right controller hardware for the tipper station.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the left/right controller hardware cannot be confirmed as the correct non-interchangeable unit (IP addresses differ).

actions.label: Confirm left/right controller identity
actions.exact_action: Identify the correct tipper station side/controller to service (left vs right ClearLink controllers are not interchangeable because IP addresses differ).

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the tipper station
steps.instruction: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).
steps.purpose: Make the tipper station safe for physical hardware replacement.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is in a LOTO state before any panel removal or cable work begins.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is applied to the tipper prior to accessing the motor and A-axis PCA.
steps.failure_condition: Work begins without LOTO applied to the tipper.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel to access the motor (if necessary)
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Provide physical access to the motor area where the A-axis PCA and FFC clamps are located.
steps.expected_result: The station side panel is removed and the motor area is accessible.
steps.healthy_condition: Nine (9) self-tapping securing screws are removed and the side panel is off, exposing the motor access area.
steps.failure_condition: The side panel is not removed (or screws are not removed) such that the A-axis PCA area cannot be accessed.

actions.label: Remove side panel screws
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Remove the FFC clamps at the A-axis PCA
steps.instruction: Starting at the A-axis PCA, remove the four (4) M3 socket-head screws holding the two (2) FFC clamps.
steps.purpose: Release the old FFC from the A-axis PCA connection.
steps.expected_result: The four (4) M3 socket-head screws are removed and the two (2) FFC clamps are released.
steps.healthy_condition: The FFC clamps are unfastened at the A-axis PCA (four M3 screws removed) so the FFC can be unplugged.
steps.failure_condition: The clamps cannot be released because the four (4) M3 socket-head screws are not removed or the clamps remain secured.

actions.label: Remove M3 screws securing clamps
actions.exact_action: Starting at the A-axis PCA, remove the four (4) M3 socket-head screws holding the two (2) FFC clamps.

steps.title: Unplug the old FFC
steps.instruction: Unplug the old FFC from the clamps.
steps.purpose: Remove the defective/old flat-flex cable from the A-axis PCA clamps.
steps.expected_result: The old FFC is unplugged from the two FFC clamps.
steps.healthy_condition: The old FFC is fully disconnected from the clamp connection at the A-axis PCA.
steps.failure_condition: The FFC cannot be unplugged cleanly.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the FFC cannot be unplugged/plugged cleanly or the clamps cannot be resecured with the four (4) M3 socket-head screws.

actions.label: Unplug old FFC
actions.exact_action: Unplug the old FFC from the clamps.

steps.title: Plug in the new FFC
steps.instruction: Plug in the new flat-flex cable (FFC).
steps.purpose: Install the correct replacement flat-flex cable at the A-axis PCA.
steps.expected_result: The new FFC is seated into the clamp connection at the A-axis PCA.
steps.healthy_condition: The new FFC is correctly positioned for clamp reinstallation (ready to be secured by the two FFC clamps).
steps.failure_condition: The new FFC cannot be plugged in cleanly or does not seat properly for clamp securing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the FFC cannot be unplugged/plugged cleanly or the clamps cannot be resecured with the four (4) M3 socket-head screws.

actions.label: Install new FFC
actions.exact_action: Plug in the new flat-flex cable (FFC).

steps.title: Reinstall the FFC clamps and secure with M3 socket-head screws
steps.instruction: Reinstall the FFC clamps and secure them using the four (4) M3 socket-head screws.
steps.purpose: Secure the new FFC so it remains properly connected at the A-axis PCA.
steps.expected_result: Both FFC clamps are reinstalled and secured using the four (4) M3 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: The new FFC is held in place by the two clamps, with all four (4) M3 socket-head screws installed.
steps.failure_condition: The clamps cannot be resecured with the four (4) M3 socket-head screws.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the FFC cannot be unplugged/plugged cleanly or the clamps cannot be resecured with the four (4) M3 socket-head screws.

actions.label: Secure clamps with M3 screws
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the FFC clamps and reinstall the FFC clamps using the M3 socket-head screws.

steps.title: Reinstall the station side panel
steps.instruction: Reinstall the station side panel using the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.
steps.purpose: Restore the station enclosure after the FFC replacement.
steps.expected_result: The station side panel is reinstalled and secured with nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel is fully fastened (nine self-tapping screws installed) and the station is physically reassembled.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel is not fully secured (missing screws) or cannot be reinstalled.

actions.label: Reinstall side panel
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the station side panel using the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.

title: Perform Full Replacement of the Z-Axis Cable Carrier (without replacing air line or FFC)
summary: Replace the Z-axis cable carrier end-to-end while preserving the existing air line and FFC, then verify the carrier is seated (cross bars closed, dividers clear of the FFC, joints fully seated/uniform end-to-end) and restart the operator station.
when_to_use: Use when the Z-axis cable carrier must be fully replaced end-to-end while keeping the existing air line and FFC.

steps.title: Apply LOTO to the tipper
steps.instruction: Apply LOTO to the tipper using the manual’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” method.
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely locked out before any mechanical disassembly.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is under lockout/tagout (LOTO) and safe to service.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is applied before removing the station side panel or disconnecting any carrier/FFC/air-line ties.
steps.failure_condition: Work begins without LOTO, or LOTO is incomplete/unclear.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel to access the motor (if necessary)
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the Z-axis cable carrier components.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed and motor area is accessible.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine (9) self-tapping securing fasteners are removed and the side panel is off without damaging surrounding wiring/hoses.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel is not fully removed (fasteners left in place) or access is blocked.

actions.label: Remove side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Mark the air line and FFC entry/exit points
steps.instruction: Mark the air line and FFC at both ends where they enter and exit the cable carrier using marker or tape.
steps.purpose: Preserve alignment so the air line and FFC can be reinstalled in the same positions.
steps.expected_result: Clear marks exist on the air line and FFC at both ends (entry/exit points).
steps.healthy_condition: Marks are visible and correspond to the entry/exit locations at both ends of the cable carrier.
steps.failure_condition: Marks are missing, ambiguous, or only applied to one end.

actions.label: Mark air line and FFC
actions.exact_action: Mark the air line and FFC at both ends where they enter and exit the cable carrier using a marker or tape.

steps.title: Document air line tie method and cut wire ties
steps.instruction: Note how the air line is tied to the cable carrier (take a picture) and cut the wire ties.
steps.purpose: Ensure the air line is re-tied in the same routing/tie configuration.
steps.expected_result: Air line tie points are documented and wire ties are cut so the carrier can be detached.
steps.healthy_condition: A picture exists showing the air line tie method; wire ties are cut without damaging the air line.
steps.failure_condition: Air line tie method is not documented or air line is damaged during tie removal.

actions.label: Take picture of air line tie
actions.exact_action: Note how the air line is tied to the cable carrier (take a picture) and cut the wire ties.

steps.title: Remove M3 screws holding FFC clamps in place (at both ends)
steps.instruction: At both ends of the cable carrier, remove the M3 socket-head screws holding the FFC clamps in place. Confirm the clamps should stay in place on the FFC; if they fall off, mark the FFC.
steps.purpose: Release the cable carrier from the FFC clamps while preserving clamp/FFC alignment.
steps.expected_result: FFC clamps are released from the cable carrier; clamps remain on the FFC or the FFC is marked if clamps fall off.
steps.healthy_condition: FFC clamps remain seated on the FFC; if not, FFC is marked to restore alignment later.
steps.failure_condition: FFC clamps fall off and FFC is not marked, risking misalignment.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the FFC clamps did not stay in place during removal and the FFC was not marked, stop and correct clamp alignment before proceeding.

actions.label: Remove FFC clamp screws
actions.exact_action: At both ends of the cable carrier, remove the M3 socket-head screws holding the FFC clamps in place.

actions.label: Confirm clamp retention / mark FFC
actions.exact_action: These clamps should stay in place on the FFC, but if they fall off, this is reason for marking the FFC.

steps.title: Detach the cable carrier by removing M3 screws at both ends
steps.instruction: Detach the cable carrier by removing the four M3 screws at both ends of the cable carrier.
steps.purpose: Remove the old cable carrier from the FFC and air line.
steps.expected_result: Cable carrier is mechanically detached from both ends.
steps.healthy_condition: All four M3 screws at each end are removed and the carrier is free to open/snap off.
steps.failure_condition: Carrier remains fixed due to missed screws.

actions.label: Remove end screws
actions.exact_action: Detach the cable carrier by removing the four M3 screws at both ends of the cable carrier.

steps.title: Open cross bars and remove the old cable carrier
steps.instruction: Open all the cross bars on the outside of the cable carrier, and remove it from the FFC and air line. You may have to snap one end of the cable carrier off to fully remove it.
steps.purpose: Remove the old carrier without disturbing the air line and FFC beyond what is required.
steps.expected_result: Old cable carrier is removed from the FFC and air line.
steps.healthy_condition: Cross bars are fully opened and carrier comes free without pulling on the FFC or air line.
steps.failure_condition: Carrier cannot be removed because cross bars are not fully opened or it is still attached.

actions.label: Open cross bars
actions.exact_action: Open all the cross bars on the outside of the cable carrier

actions.label: Remove carrier
actions.exact_action: remove it from the FFC and air line. You may have to snap one end of the cable carrier off to fully remove it.

steps.title: Position the new cable carrier with dividers against the air line
steps.instruction: Open all the cross bars on the new cable carrier and probably one end. Put the new cable carrier roughly in place while positioning the internal dividers all the way to one side, against the air line.
steps.purpose: Set the new carrier in the correct orientation and clearance before snapping it closed.
steps.expected_result: New carrier is positioned roughly in place with internal dividers positioned against the air line.
steps.healthy_condition: Dividers are positioned all the way to one side against the air line before snapping cross bars closed.
steps.failure_condition: Dividers are not positioned against the air line, increasing risk of divider pressing on the FFC.

actions.label: Open new carrier cross bars
actions.exact_action: Open all the cross bars on the new cable carrier and probably one end.

actions.label: Position dividers against air line
actions.exact_action: Put the new cable carrier roughly in place while positioning the internal dividers all the way to one side, against the air line.

steps.title: Snap cross bars closed ensuring dividers do not press on the FFC
steps.instruction: “Snap” all the cross bars closed, ensuring none of the dividers are pressing on the FFC; snap the end back on if necessary.
steps.purpose: Lock the carrier in place while preserving FFC clearance.
steps.expected_result: All cross bars are snapped closed and dividers are not pressing on the FFC.
steps.healthy_condition: No divider contact/pressure on the FFC is visible; carrier ends are fully snapped in place.
steps.failure_condition: Any divider is pressing on the FFC.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check alignment/clearance if dividers are pressing on the FFC.

actions.label: Snap cross bars closed
actions.exact_action: “Snap” all the cross bars closed ensuring none of the dividers are pressing on the FFC and snap the end back on if necessary.

steps.title: Mount both ends of the cable carrier with M3 flat-head screws
steps.instruction: Mount both ends using four M3 flat-head screws.
steps.purpose: Secure the carrier ends to the station structure.
steps.expected_result: Both ends are mounted with four M3 flat-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: All specified screws are installed at both ends and the carrier is firmly secured.
steps.failure_condition: Any end is missing screws or carrier is loose.

actions.label: Install mounting screws
actions.exact_action: Mount both ends using four M3 flat-head.

steps.title: Attach FFC clamps using M3 socket-head screws aligned to marks
steps.instruction: Attach the FFC clamps using the M3 socket-head screws at both cable carrier ends; ensure the FFC clamps align with the marks from Step 1.
steps.purpose: Restore correct FFC clamp alignment and secure the FFC to the carrier ends.
steps.expected_result: FFC clamps are secured at both ends and aligned to the previously applied marks.
steps.healthy_condition: Clamp positions match the Step 1 marks; clamps are seated and secured with M3 socket-head screws.
steps.failure_condition: Clamp alignment does not match the marks (risk of FFC misalignment).

actions.label: Install FFC clamp screws
actions.exact_action: Attach the FFC clamps using the M3 socket-head screws at both cable carrier ends; ensure the FFC clamps align with the marks from Step 1.

steps.title: Wire-tie the air line in the cable carrier using marks
steps.instruction: Position the air line in the cable carrier using the marks from Step 1 and wire tie it in place.
steps.purpose: Restore air line routing and secure it within the carrier.
steps.expected_result: Air line is positioned according to Step 1 marks and secured with wire ties.
steps.healthy_condition: Air line routing matches the marks and is firmly wire-tied without slack or strain.
steps.failure_condition: Air line is mispositioned relative to marks or not secured.

actions.label: Wire-tie air line
actions.exact_action: Position the air line in the cable carrier using the marks from Step 1 and wire tie in place.

steps.title: Inspect cable carrier seating, clearance, and joint uniformity
steps.instruction: Inspect the cable carrier: verify all cross bars are closed, the dividers are not pressing on the FFC, and all the cable carrier joints are fully seated. The cable carrier should look very uniform end to end.
steps.purpose: Confirm the carrier is correctly installed before restarting.
steps.expected_result: Cross bars are closed; dividers are not pressing on the FFC; joints are fully seated; carrier appears uniform end-to-end.
steps.healthy_condition: Visual inspection shows uniform end-to-end appearance with no divider pressure on the FFC and fully seated joints.
steps.failure_condition: Any cross bar is not closed, dividers press on the FFC, or joints are not fully seated (non-uniform appearance).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check alignment/clearance if dividers are pressing on the FFC or if cable carrier joints do not appear fully seated/uniform end-to-end.

actions.label: Visual inspection
actions.exact_action: Inspect the cable carrier to ensure all the cross bars are closed, the dividers are not pressing on the FFC, and all the cable carrier joints are fully seated.

steps.title: Reinstall top and/or bottom side panels (if necessary)
