steps.healthy_condition: After clicking a button, the UI transitions to the next maintenance screen (the Maintenance Menu buttons are no longer shown).
steps.failure_condition: After clicking the selected button, the screen does not change (or it does not open the corresponding maintenance function screen).
stop_or_escalate_if: If the selected button does not change screens, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for further troubleshooting.

actions.label: Click maintenance function button
actions.exact_action: Click the desired button (Manual Control, IO Diagnostics, Persistent Variables, or Default) to open the corresponding maintenance function screen.

steps.title: Confirm the screen transitioned to the selected maintenance function
steps.instruction: Confirm the Hospital HMI no longer shows the Maintenance Menu buttons and instead shows the maintenance function screen corresponding to the button you selected.
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct maintenance function screen opened for the selected button.
steps.expected_result: The UI displays the selected maintenance function screen (Manual Control / IO Diagnostics / Persistent Variables / Default).
steps.healthy_condition: The Maintenance Menu buttons are replaced by the selected function’s screen content.
steps.failure_condition: The Maintenance Menu buttons remain visible, or the displayed screen does not correspond to the selected function.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the screen does not transition correctly to the selected maintenance function, stop and escalate to FORTNA support for further troubleshooting.

actions.label: Check destination screen
actions.exact_action: Confirm the screen changes to the selected maintenance function (i.e., the UI no longer shows the Maintenance Menu buttons and instead shows the next maintenance screen for the selected function).

title: Remove Idler Pulley Assembly (A-axis / counterbalance belt system) on a LOTOed tipper
summary: LOTO the tipper, access the station side panel if needed, manually position and secure the A-axis/counterbalance using the actuator base threaded holes, remove belt clamps, release belt tension, unfasten the idler pulley assembly (M8x25 screws), and slide the idler pulley assembly out of the column. If needed, transfer the M6x35 tensioning screws to the new assembly.
when_to_use: Use when removing/replacing the tipper’s idler pulley assembly as part of a mechanical maintenance/recovery task, following the manual’s LOTO and belt-tension release precautions to prevent dropping once tension is released.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a software/controls troubleshooting guide (it is a mechanical removal procedure).
Do not proceed to release belt tension unless the A-axis/counterbalance is secured with the specified M6 socket-head screws.

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the tipper
steps.instruction: Apply lockout/tagout to the tipper (manual references “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” on page 2).
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is locked out/tagged out before any mechanical removal work.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is LOTOed and ready for mechanical work.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is in place before removing any side panel or fasteners.
steps.failure_condition: Mechanical removal begins without LOTO.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove station side panel if necessary to access the motor
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor area as needed for the idler pulley assembly removal.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed and the motor access area is available.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine self-tapping securing screws are removed and the side panel is off without forcing.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel is not fully secured/removed (e.g., screws left in place) or panel removal is attempted without removing the specified screws.

actions.label: Check if side panel removal is needed
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Position A-axis and counterbalance between actuator base threaded holes
steps.instruction: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base: there are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.purpose: Set the A-axis/counterbalance carriages to the correct location so they can be secured and will not drop when belt tension is released.
steps.expected_result: A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are located between the specified threaded holes on their respective rails.
steps.failure_condition: Carriages are not between the threaded holes (mispositioned), increasing risk of dropping when tension is released.

actions.label: Manually position carriages
actions.exact_action: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

steps.title: Thread M6 socket-head screws below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.instruction: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages.
steps.purpose: Mechanically secure the A-axis/counterbalance so it cannot drop once belt tension is released.
steps.expected_result: M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages, preventing drop when belt tension is released.
steps.healthy_condition: Both carriages are secured by the M6 socket-head screws below them.
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screws are not installed below both carriages before belt tension is released.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance is not held securely by the threaded M6 socket-head screws before loosening belt tension (risk of dropping).

actions.label: Install M6 securing screws
actions.exact_action: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

steps.title: Remove belt clamps by removing six M6x20 countersunk screws
steps.instruction: Remove the belt clamps by removing the six (6) M6x20 countersunk screws with a 5-mm hex wrench from each clamp to free the carriages from the belt.
steps.purpose: Free the carriages from the belt so belt tension can be released and the idler pulley assembly can be removed.
steps.expected_result: Belt clamps are removed and carriages are free from the belt.
steps.healthy_condition: All six M6x20 countersunk screws per clamp are removed and the clamp(s) are off without binding the belt.
steps.failure_condition: Any clamp fasteners remain installed, preventing carriage/belt separation.

actions.label: Remove belt clamp screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the belt clamps by removing the six (6) M6x20 countersunk screws with a 5-mm hex wrench from each clamp to free the carriages from the belt.

steps.title: Release belt tension by loosening two M6x35 socket-head screws
steps.instruction: Release belt tension by loosening the two (2) M6x35 socket-head screws on the bottom side of the assembly.
steps.purpose: Remove tension from the belt so the idler pulley assembly can be unfastened and slid out.
steps.expected_result: Belt tension is released after loosening the two M6x35 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: After loosening, the belt is no longer under tension (mechanically slackened) while the A-axis/counterbalance remains secured by the M6 screws.
steps.failure_condition: Belt tension is released without the A-axis/counterbalance being secured (risk of dropping).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance is not held securely by the threaded M6 socket-head screws before loosening belt tension (risk of dropping).

actions.label: Loosen tensioning screws
actions.exact_action: Release belt tension by loosening the two (2) M6x35 socket-head screws on the bottom side of the assembly.

steps.title: Remove idler pulley assembly and slide it out of the column
steps.instruction: Remove the two (2) M8x25 socket-head screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place, then slide the idler pulley assembly out of the column. If needed, transfer the M6x35 tensioning screws from the removed idler pulley assembly to the new assembly.
steps.purpose: Unfasten the idler pulley assembly and remove it from the tipper column for replacement.
steps.expected_result: The two M8x25 screws are removed and the idler pulley assembly slides out of the column; if required, M6x35 tensioning screws are transferred to the new assembly.
steps.healthy_condition: Idler pulley assembly is fully removed with no remaining fasteners; tensioning screws are available on the new assembly if the manual note applies.
steps.failure_condition: Idler pulley assembly does not slide out after removing the two M8x25 socket-head screws (possible remaining fasteners or misalignment).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the idler pulley assembly does not slide out after removing the two M8x25 socket-head screws (possible remaining fasteners or misalignment).

actions.label: Remove mounting screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the two (2) M8x25 socket-head screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place

actions.label: Slide assembly out
actions.exact_action: then slide the idler pulley assembly out of the column.

actions.label: Transfer tensioning screws if needed
actions.exact_action: NOTE: Transfer the M6x35 tensioning screws from the removed idler pulley assembly to the new assembly if needed.

title: Replace OptiSweep Idler Pulley Assembly — LOTO tipper and prevent A-axis/counterbalance drop during removal
summary: Safely prepare the OptiSweep tipper for idler pulley assembly removal by performing lockout/tagout (LOTO) and mechanically restraining the A-axis and counterbalance so they cannot drop when belt tension is released.
when_to_use: Use when preparing an OptiSweep tipper station for idler pulley assembly removal and you must (1) lockout/tagout the tipper and (2) prevent the A-axis/counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.
not_for: Do not proceed if LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper station.
Do not proceed if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified threaded holes or if M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.

steps.title: Identify the specific tipper station and perform LOTO
steps.instruction: Identify the specific tipper station to be serviced, then perform lockout/tagout (LOTO) on the tipper using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct tipper station is isolated and safe for mechanical preparation before accessing/removing components.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out/tagged out for the intended station.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is successfully completed for the intended tipper station (i.e., you can proceed with the mechanical preparation steps).
steps.failure_condition: LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper station.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper.

actions.label: Perform tipper LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor area if required for the idler pulley assembly removal preparation.
steps.expected_result: The station side panel is removed (when needed), exposing the motor area for the subsequent A-axis/counterbalance positioning steps.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel removal is complete (when required) and the motor area is accessible.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot remove the side panel as described (e.g., screws cannot be removed with the specified tool).

actions.label: Remove side panel screws
actions.exact_action: use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Manually position the A-axis and counterbalance between the threaded holes
steps.instruction: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail; the carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.purpose: Set the A-axis/counterbalance to the correct mechanical position so restraint screws can be installed and prevent dropping when belt tension is released.
steps.expected_result: The A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are correctly located between the holes on the respective rails (as shown in the idler pulley assembly diagram).
steps.failure_condition: The A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified threaded holes.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified holes.

actions.label: Position A-axis/counterbalance
actions.exact_action: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

steps.title: Thread M6 socket-head screws below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.instruction: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages.
steps.purpose: Mechanically restrain the A-axis/counterbalance so it cannot drop once belt tension is released during the idler pulley assembly removal job.
steps.expected_result: M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages, providing mechanical restraint against dropping when belt tension is released.
steps.healthy_condition: M6 socket-head screws are installed in the specified holes below both carriages (with carriages in the positioned location from the prior step).
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described or if the M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.

actions.label: Install M6 restraint screws
actions.exact_action: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

steps.title: Escalate if LOTO or mechanical positioning/restraint cannot be completed
steps.instruction: If LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper, or if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified holes or the M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages, stop and escalate to FORTNA support or follow the site’s safety escalation process.
steps.purpose: Ensure unsafe or non-compliant preparation does not proceed.
steps.expected_result: You stop the procedure and escalate rather than proceeding with idler pulley assembly removal preparation.
steps.healthy_condition: Any inability to meet the LOTO/mechanical restraint requirements results in escalation and no further removal preparation steps are attempted.
steps.failure_condition: Proceeding despite inability to complete LOTO or install the mechanical restraint screws as specified.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if LOTO cannot be performed on the intended tipper.
Escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described or if the M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.

actions.label: Escalate
actions.exact_action: Escalate if LOTO cannot be performed on the intended tipper or if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described or if the M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.

title: Install CLINK Sensor Wiring for Z-Axis (I/O1/DI6/DI7) and A-Axis (PCA) and Restart Operator Station
summary: Install the CLINK sensor wiring by feeding the sensor through the rear wire routing hole and fastening it with an M3 button-head screw, routing Z-axis wires through the column and out the lower grommet into the control box (I/O1, DI6, or DI7), routing A-axis wires around the gearbox into the PCA, then restarting the operator station so the sensor connections are active.
when_to_use: Use when CLINK sensor wiring for the Z-axis and A-axis needs to be installed/reconnected so the sensor connections are active after wiring work.

steps.title: Feed the sensor through the rear wire routing hole and fasten with the M3 button-head screw
steps.instruction: Feed the sensor through the wire routing hole on the rear side and fasten it in place using the M3 button-head screw.
steps.purpose: Mechanically secure the CLINK sensor and prepare it for correct wire routing.
steps.expected_result: The sensor is mechanically fastened at the rear wire routing hole using the M3 button-head screw.
steps.healthy_condition: The sensor is secured with the M3 button-head screw at the rear wire routing hole (no loose mounting).
steps.failure_condition: The sensor is not secured (e.g., screw not installed/loose) or not seated at the rear wire routing hole.

actions.label: Fasten CLINK sensor
actions.exact_action: Feed the sensor through the wire routing hole on the rear side and fasten in place using the M3 button-head screw.

steps.title: Route Z-axis wires through the column and out the lower grommet into the control box (I/O1, DI6, or DI7)
steps.instruction: Route the Z-axis wires by dropping them down through the column and out the lower grommet into the control box, then plug into either I/O1, DI6, or DI7.
steps.purpose: Ensure the Z-axis CLINK wiring reaches the correct control box inputs.
steps.expected_result: Z-axis wiring exits via the lower grommet into the control box and is connected to one of I/O1, DI6, or DI7.
steps.healthy_condition: Z-axis wires follow the column path and terminate at a control box port labeled I/O1, DI6, or DI7.
steps.failure_condition: Z-axis wires do not exit through the lower grommet into the control box, or they are not plugged into I/O1, DI6, or DI7.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check wiring routing if the Z-axis wires are not exiting through the lower grommet into the control box or if they are not plugged into I/O1, DI6, or DI7.

actions.label: Verify Z-axis wire exit and port
actions.exact_action: Route the wire: Z-axis wires drop down through the column and out the lower grommet into the control box and plug into either I/O1, DI6, or DI7.

steps.title: Route A-axis wires around the gearbox and plug into the PCA
steps.instruction: Route the A-axis wires around the gearbox and plug them into the PCA.
steps.purpose: Ensure the A-axis CLINK wiring reaches the correct PCA connector.
steps.expected_result: A-axis wiring is routed around the gearbox and connected to the PCA.
steps.healthy_condition: A-axis wires follow the gearbox routing path and terminate at the PCA connector.
steps.failure_condition: A-axis wires are not routed around the gearbox or are not plugged into the PCA.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check wiring routing if the A-axis wires are not routed around the gearbox or are not plugged into the PCA.

actions.label: Verify A-axis wire routing and PCA connection
actions.exact_action: Route the wire: A-axis wires route around the gearbox and plug into the PCA.

steps.title: Restart the operator station
steps.instruction: Restart the operator station using the procedure referenced as "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66.
steps.purpose: Activate the sensor connections after wiring installation.
steps.expected_result: The operator station has been restarted.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator station restart completes successfully (per the referenced restart procedure on page 66).
steps.failure_condition: Operator station restart does not complete successfully.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the operator station restart does not complete successfully, escalate to support and use the operator-station restart troubleshooting guidance (not included in this section).

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

title: Install Tip or A-Axis Cable (A-axis PCA to cable carrier/grommet and sensor/valve M8 connectors)
summary: Replace/install the Tip or A-Axis cable by routing it correctly around the gearbox and into the cable carrier, securing it, routing all required M8 connectors through the grommet, connecting the labeled Valve/tote detect/LONG/SHORT gripper sensors, installing the valve cover without pinching wires, reinstalling side panels if needed, and restarting the operator station.
when_to_use: Use when the Tip or A-Axis cable needs replacement/installation and you must ensure correct cable routing, grommet use, labeled M8 connector connections (Valve, tote detect, LONG/SHORT gripper sensors), valve cover installation without pinching wires, and a successful operator station restart.

steps.title: Plug new cable into A-axis PCA and route around gearbox into cable carrier
steps.instruction: Plug the new Tip or A-Axis cable into the A-axis PCA, then route the cable around the gearbox and into and around the cable carrier.
steps.purpose: Establish correct electrical connection at the A-axis PCA and ensure the cable follows the required routing path around the gearbox and into the cable carrier.
steps.expected_result: The cable is plugged into the A-axis PCA and physically routed around the gearbox and into/around the cable carrier along the intended path.
steps.healthy_condition: Cable routing matches the installation diagram: cable passes around the gearbox and into/around the cable carrier without being misrouted.
steps.failure_condition: Cable is routed incorrectly around the gearbox/cable carrier or not properly seated at the A-axis PCA.

actions.label: Verify PCA plug-in and routing path
actions.exact_action: Plug the new cable into the A-axis PCA and route the cable around the gearbox and into and around the cable carrier.

steps.title: Close cross bars with dividers between cable and air line
steps.instruction: Close all the cross bars, ensuring the dividers are positioned between the cable and the air line.
steps.purpose: Prevent cable/air-line interference by ensuring the cable is separated from the air line using the dividers when the cross bars are closed.
steps.expected_result: All cross bars are closed and the dividers are between the cable and the air line.
steps.healthy_condition: Dividers visibly separate the cable from the air line within the cross-bar assembly.
steps.failure_condition: Dividers are not positioned between the cable and air line.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check wiring/routing if the dividers are not positioned between the cable and air line.

actions.label: Close cross bars and position dividers
actions.exact_action: Close all the cross bars, ensuring the dividers are between the cable and air line.

steps.title: Align cable markings and wire-tie in place (both cable carrier ends and A-axis carriage tie point)
steps.instruction: Align the cable markings to the cable carrier and wire-tie in place as before, including both ends of the cable carrier and the tie point on the A-axis carriage.
steps.purpose: Secure the cable in the correct position using the same alignment and tie points as before.
steps.expected_result: Cable markings align to the cable carrier and wire ties secure both ends of the cable carrier and the tie point on the A-axis carriage.
steps.healthy_condition: Cable remains in the intended position with ties at both cable carrier ends and the A-axis carriage tie point.
steps.failure_condition: Cable markings are misaligned or ties are missing/incorrect at the specified tie points.

actions.label: Align markings and secure with wire ties
actions.exact_action: Align the cable markings to the cable carrier and wire tie in place as before, including both ends of the cable carrier and the tie point on the A-axis carriage.

steps.title: Ensure no dangling wires near A-axis PCA; contain with wire ties
steps.instruction: Near the A-axis PCA, ensure no wires are dangling; use wire ties as needed to contain the cable.
steps.purpose: Reduce risk of interference or damage by ensuring the area near the A-axis PCA is tidy and secured.
steps.expected_result: No dangling wires are present near the A-axis PCA; cable is contained/secured with wire ties as needed.
steps.healthy_condition: Wires near the A-axis PCA are restrained and do not hang freely.
steps.failure_condition: Any wires are dangling near the A-axis PCA.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check wiring/routing if any wires are dangling near the A-axis PCA.

actions.label: Check for dangling wires and secure
actions.exact_action: Near the A-axis PCA, ensure no wires are dangling. Use wire ties as needed to contain the cable.

steps.title: Route all four M8 connectors through grommet and push jacketed cable end through
steps.instruction: Route all four M8 connectors through the grommet one at a time, then finish by pushing the end of the jacketed cable through the grommet.
steps.purpose: Ensure strain relief and correct cable pass-through by routing connectors and jacket through the grommet.
steps.expected_result: All four M8 connectors are routed through the grommet and the jacketed cable end is pushed through the grommet.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectors pass through the grommet without being forced or misrouted; jacketed cable end is seated through the grommet.
steps.failure_condition: Any M8 connector is not routed through the grommet or the jacketed cable end is not pushed through.

actions.label: Pass connectors and jacket through grommet
actions.exact_action: Route all four M8 connectors though the grommet one at a time and finish by pushing the end of the jacketed cable through the grommet.

steps.title: Connect 3-pin M8 connector labeled "Valve" to the valve
steps.instruction: Connect the 3-pin M8 connector labeled "Valve" to the valve.
steps.purpose: Restore the valve sensor/actuator connection using the correctly labeled M8 connector.
steps.expected_result: The 3-pin M8 connector labeled "Valve" is connected to the valve.
steps.healthy_condition: Valve connector is fully seated and matches the label "Valve".
steps.failure_condition: Valve connector is not connected or is connected to the wrong target.

actions.label: Connect Valve M8
actions.exact_action: Connect the 3-pin M8 connector labeled "Valve" to the valve.

steps.title: Connect 4-pin M8 connector to tote detect sensor
steps.instruction: Connect the 4-pin M8 connector to the tote detect sensor.
steps.purpose: Restore tote detect sensing by connecting the correctly labeled 4-pin M8 connector to the tote detect sensor.
steps.expected_result: The 4-pin M8 connector is connected to the tote detect sensor.
steps.healthy_condition: Tote detect connector is fully seated at the tote detect sensor.
steps.failure_condition: Tote detect connector is not connected or is connected incorrectly.

actions.label: Connect tote detect M8
actions.exact_action: Connect the 4-pin M8 connector to the tote detect sensor.

steps.title: Connect 3-pin M8 connector labeled "LONG" to longer gripper sensor
steps.instruction: Connect the 3-pin M8 connector labeled "LONG" to the longer gripper sensor.
steps.purpose: Restore the longer gripper sensor connection using the correctly labeled connector.
steps.expected_result: The 3-pin M8 connector labeled "LONG" is connected to the longer gripper sensor.
steps.healthy_condition: LONG connector is fully seated at the longer gripper sensor.
steps.failure_condition: LONG connector is not connected or is connected to the wrong gripper sensor.

actions.label: Connect LONG gripper M8
actions.exact_action: Connect the 3-pin M8 connector labeled "LONG" to the longer gripper sensor.

steps.title: Connect 3-pin M8 connector labeled "SHORT" to shorter gripper sensor
steps.instruction: Connect the 3-pin M8 connector labeled "SHORT" to the shorter gripper sensor.
steps.purpose: Restore the shorter gripper sensor connection using the correctly labeled connector.
steps.expected_result: The 3-pin M8 connector labeled "SHORT" is connected to the shorter gripper sensor.
steps.healthy_condition: SHORT connector is fully seated at the shorter gripper sensor.
steps.failure_condition: SHORT connector is not connected or is connected to the wrong gripper sensor.

actions.label: Connect SHORT gripper M8
actions.exact_action: Connect the 3-pin M8 connector labeled "SHORT" to the shorter gripper sensor.

steps.title: Install valve cover with M4x50 screws; avoid pinching wires; seat grommet into tote sensor wire notch
steps.instruction: Install the valve cover using the four M4x50 socket-head screws. Make sure not to pinch any wires along the edges of the cover, and insert the grommet into the notch for the tote sensor wire.
steps.purpose: Reassemble the valve cover while preventing wire damage and ensuring the grommet is seated correctly for the tote sensor wire.
steps.expected_result: Valve cover is installed with four M4x50 socket-head screws; no wires are pinched along the cover edges; grommet is inserted into the notch for the tote sensor wire.
steps.healthy_condition: Cover edges do not trap wires; grommet sits in the tote sensor wire notch.
steps.failure_condition: Wires appear pinched at the valve cover edges or grommet is not seated into the tote sensor wire notch.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check wiring/routing if wires appear pinched at the valve cover edges.
Stop and re-check wiring/routing if the grommet is not seated into the notch for the tote sensor wire.

actions.label: Install valve cover and seat grommet
actions.exact_action: Install the valve cover using the four M4x50 socket-head screws. Make sure to not pinch any wires along the edges of the cover, and insert the grommet into the notch for the tote sensor wire.

steps.title: Reinstall top and/or bottom side panels if necessary
steps.instruction: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.
steps.purpose: Restore station enclosure panels after completing cable installation and valve cover reassembly.
steps.expected_result: Top and/or bottom side panels are reinstalled as required for the station configuration.
steps.healthy_condition: Panels are back in place (no open access panels left if they were removed).
steps.failure_condition: Side panels remain removed when they were required to be reinstalled.

actions.label: Reinstall side panels
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.

steps.title: Restart operator station
steps.instruction: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).
steps.purpose: Bring the operator station back online after physical reassembly so the system can resume normal operation.
steps.expected_result: Operator station restarts successfully after reassembly.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator station is running after restart attempt.
steps.failure_condition: Operator station does not restart successfully.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the operator station does not restart successfully, escalate using the site’s standard support process.

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

title: Manually Jog the Tipper End Effector Using Operator Station HMI (Visu_Dual_MCP)
summary: Use the operator station HMI jogging screen (Visu_Dual_MCP) to stop the automatic tipping cycle and manually move the tipper axes (Z1/A1 for left, Z2/A2 for right) using the +/− controls in Manual Mode.
when_to_use: When you need to move the tipper end effector into a desired maintenance position by manually jogging the left and/or right tipper axes from the operator station HMI (Visu_Dual_MCP).

steps.title: Navigate to the Visu_Dual_MCP jogging screen (F3)
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3).
steps.purpose: Open the operator station HMI screen that provides the CYCLE STOP and JOG controls for tipper jogging.
steps.expected_result: The "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen is displayed and you can access the CYCLE STOP and JOG controls.
steps.healthy_condition: You are on the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) with the tipper operator controls visible.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) or the CYCLE STOP/JOG controls are not available.

actions.label: Open Visu_Dual_MCP (F3)
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3).

steps.title: Stop the automatic tipping cycle using CYCLE STOP
steps.instruction: Press "CYCLE STOP" to stop the automatic tipping cycle.
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is not running the automatic tipping cycle before entering manual jogging.
steps.expected_result: The automatic tipping cycle is stopped (CYCLE STOP action has been applied).
steps.healthy_condition: The operator station is in a state where you can proceed to press JOG to open the jogging screen.
steps.failure_condition: The automatic tipping cycle does not stop (you cannot proceed to jogging as expected).

actions.label: Press CYCLE STOP
actions.exact_action: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the automatic tipping cycle.

steps.title: Open the jogging screen using JOG
steps.instruction: Press "JOG" to open the jogging screen.
steps.purpose: Enter the manual jogging interface where axis +/− controls are available.
steps.expected_result: The jogging screen opens and shows Manual Mode.
steps.healthy_condition: Manual Mode is indicated on the jogging screen.
steps.failure_condition: The jogging screen does not open or Manual Mode is not indicated.

actions.label: Press JOG
actions.exact_action: Press JOG to open the jogging screen.

steps.title: Confirm Manual Mode and identify axis controls (Z1, Z2, A1, A2)
steps.instruction: On the jogging screen, confirm you are in "Manual Mode" and identify the axis controls for Z1, Z2, A1, and A2.
steps.purpose: Ensure you are in the correct mode and you select the correct axis controls for the left vs right tipper.
steps.expected_result: Manual Mode is shown and the axis +/− controls for Z1, Z2, A1, and A2 are visible.
steps.healthy_condition: You can clearly see the Z1 Axis, Z2 Axis, A1 Axis, and A2 Axis sections with +/− buttons.
steps.failure_condition: Manual Mode is not indicated or one/both axis control groups are not visible.

actions.label: Verify Manual Mode and axis controls
actions.exact_action: Confirm you are in "Manual Mode" and identify the axis controls for Z1, Z2, A1, and A2.

steps.title: Jog the left tipper axes (Z1/A1) or right tipper axes (Z2/A2) using +/−
steps.instruction: Select the axis you want to move and use the "−" and "+" buttons to move it: Z1 (vertical movement) and A1 (rotate gripper) move the left tipper; Z2 and A2 move the right tipper.
steps.purpose: Move the tipper end effector into the desired maintenance position by jogging the correct axes.
steps.expected_result: The selected axis responds to the jog command while Manual Mode is active.
steps.healthy_condition: Jogging causes the intended axis motion for the selected tipper (left via Z1/A1, right via Z2/A2).
steps.failure_condition: The axis does not respond to jog commands or the wrong tipper side moves relative to the axis selection.

actions.label: Select axis and jog with +/−
actions.exact_action: Select the axis you want to move and use the − and + buttons to move the axis.

steps.title: Use correct +/− motion behavior for Z and A axes
steps.instruction: Use the +/− behavior as documented: "+" moves the Z-axis up and rotates the A-axis toward the operator; "−" moves the Z-axis down and rotates the A-axis away from the operator.
steps.purpose: Ensure the axis moves in the intended direction to reach the maintenance position safely.
steps.expected_result: Pressing "+" produces Z up + A toward operator motion; pressing "−" produces Z down + A away motion.
steps.healthy_condition: Axis motion direction matches the documented +/− behavior.
steps.failure_condition: Axis motion direction is opposite of the documented behavior or does not match the selected axis.

actions.label: Jog with correct +/− direction
actions.exact_action: The + button moves the Z-axis up and rotates the A-axis towards the operator. The − button moves the Z-axis down and rotates the A-axis away from the operator.

steps.title: Avoid hard stops; stop jogging before the axis reaches a hard stop
steps.instruction: Stop jogging before the axis reaches a hard stop. Do not push the axis into the hard stop.
steps.purpose: Prevent the axis from registering a fault due to contact with a hard stop.
steps.expected_result: No hard-stop fault is registered while jogging.
steps.healthy_condition: You can position the end effector without triggering a fault indication.
steps.failure_condition: The axis registers a fault after being pushed to a hard stop.
stop_or_escalate_if: If an axis is driven into a hard stop and the axis registers a fault, stop further jogging and escalate to maintenance/support for the fault condition.

actions.label: Monitor for hard-stop fault indication
actions.exact_action: If you push the axis until it hits a hard stop, the axis will register a fault.

title: Manually Reference Tipper Axes Using Operator Station HMI (Visu_Dual_MCP)
summary: Use the operator station HMI to stop the automatic tipping cycle, open the reference screen, and manually reference the required tipper axis(es) when the circled 'R' indicator shows they need referencing.
when_to_use: When maintenance requires manually referencing the tipper axis(es) using the operator station HMI reference screen (Visu_Dual_MCP).

steps.title: Navigate to Visu_Dual_MCP (F3) on the operator station HMI
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3).
steps.purpose: Open the correct operator station screen used to stop the automatic tipping cycle and access referencing controls.
steps.expected_result: The operator station HMI displays the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) with the tipping cycle controls available.
steps.healthy_condition: The "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) is visible and ready for interaction (including the CYCLE STOP control).
steps.failure_condition: The "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) is not displayed, or the expected controls for stopping the tipping cycle are not present.

actions.label: Open Visu_Dual_MCP (F3)
actions.exact_action: navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3)

steps.title: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the automatic tipping cycle
steps.instruction: Press "CYCLE STOP" to stop the automatic tipping cycle.
steps.purpose: Stop the automatic tipping cycle before opening the reference screen and moving axes for referencing.
steps.expected_result: The automatic tipping cycle is stopped (CYCLE STOP is pressed while in Auto tipping cycle context).
steps.healthy_condition: CYCLE STOP is successfully engaged/pressed and the system is no longer running the automatic tipping cycle.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing CYCLE STOP does not stop the automatic tipping cycle.

actions.label: Stop automatic tipping cycle
actions.exact_action: Press "CYCLE STOP"

steps.title: Press REF to open the reference screen
steps.instruction: Press "REF" to open the reference screen.
steps.purpose: Open the HMI reference screen where axis referencing is initiated based on the circled 'R' indicator.
steps.expected_result: The reference screen opens.
steps.healthy_condition: The reference screen is visible and shows axis information with a circled 'R' indicator next to the axis information.
steps.failure_condition: The reference screen does not open after pressing REF.
stop_or_escalate_if: Reference screen does not open after pressing REF.

actions.label: Open reference screen
actions.exact_action: Press "REF"

steps.title: Check circled 'R' indicator and select axis needing referencing
steps.instruction: On the reference screen, check the circled 'R' indicator next to the axis information. If the circled 'R' is clear, that axis needs to be referenced. Select the axis to be referenced.
steps.purpose: Identify which axis(es) require referencing and prepare to initiate movement for the selected axis.
steps.expected_result: The circled 'R' status is visible next to axis information, and the axis requiring referencing is selected.
steps.healthy_condition: The circled 'R' indicator is visible next to axis information, and the operator selects an axis where the circled 'R' is clear (needs referencing).
steps.failure_condition: The circled 'R' indicator/axis information area is not visible or does not respond as expected.
stop_or_escalate_if: Circled 'R' indicator/axis selection area is not visible or does not respond as expected.

actions.label: Inspect circled 'R' status
actions.exact_action: check the circled 'R' next to the axis information

actions.label: Select axis needing referencing
actions.exact_action: Select the axis to be referenced

steps.title: Press '-' to start movement of the selected axis for referencing
steps.instruction: Press the '-' button to start the movement of the selected axis.
steps.purpose: Initiate the axis movement required to perform referencing for the selected axis.
steps.expected_result: Pressing '-' starts movement of the selected axis for referencing.
steps.healthy_condition: Axis movement begins after pressing '-' for the selected axis.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing the '-' button does not start axis movement for the selected axis.
stop_or_escalate_if: Pressing '-' does not start axis movement for the selected axis.

actions.label: Start axis movement
actions.exact_action: press the '-' button

title: Recover Non-Recoverable Operator Station Motor Fault Using MCP_Dual (F3) Manual Jog, Reset, and Cycle Start
summary: When a non-recoverable operator station motor fault (e.g., motor overload) cannot be recovered in software, use the operator station HMI MCP_Dual screen (F3) to stop the cycle, enter manual jog mode, clear any axis faults with RESET, jog the correct axes to reposition the tote on/near the robot, then return to automatic mode and press CYCLE START to release the grippers and command the robot to the hospital station. After the robot leaves the tipper, press RESET.
when_to_use: Use this procedure when the operator station has a non-recoverable motor fault (example given: motor overload) and the station needs to be manually reset so the tote can be repositioned and the robot can be commanded to the hospital station.

steps.title: Navigate to MCP_Dual (F3) on the operator station HMI
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the "MCP_Dual" screen (F3).
steps.purpose: Open the manual recovery interface for non-recoverable operator station motor faults.
steps.expected_result: The MCP_Dual (F3) screen is displayed with the Manual Mode/Fault area and the visible controls used for recovery (including RESET and cycle controls).
steps.healthy_condition: MCP_Dual (F3) is visible and shows the Manual Mode Fault area and axis status indicators (Z1, Z2, A2, A1).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot reach the MCP_Dual (F3) screen or the required controls (RESET / cycle controls) are not available.

actions.label: Open MCP_Dual (F3)
actions.exact_action: navigate to the "MCP_Dual" screen (F3)

steps.title: Stop the tipping cycle with CYCLE STOP
steps.instruction: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the tipping cycle.
steps.purpose: Halt the tipping cycle before switching to manual jog and resetting faults.
steps.expected_result: The tipping cycle is stopped (cycle is halted) on the MCP_Dual (F3) screen.
steps.healthy_condition: CYCLE STOP has been pressed and the cycle is in a stopped state.
steps.failure_condition: The cycle does not stop after pressing CYCLE STOP.

actions.label: Stop cycle
actions.exact_action: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the tipping cycle.

steps.title: Enter manual jog mode with JOG
steps.instruction: Press JOG to enter manual jog mode.
steps.purpose: Enable manual axis jogging to reposition the tote and clear faults.
steps.expected_result: Manual jog mode is active (Manual Mode indicator/status is shown) on MCP_Dual (F3).
steps.healthy_condition: Manual Mode is indicated and the manual jog controls are available.
steps.failure_condition: Manual jog mode does not activate after pressing JOG.

actions.label: Enter manual jog
actions.exact_action: Press JOG to enter manual jog mode.

steps.title: Clear any axis faults with RESET
steps.instruction: If any of the axes show a fault, press RESET to clear the fault.
steps.purpose: Remove axis fault indications so manual jogging and recovery can proceed.
steps.expected_result: Axis fault indicators clear after pressing RESET (no longer indicated on the affected axis/axes).
steps.healthy_condition: No axis fault indicators remain visible on MCP_Dual (F3) after RESET.
steps.failure_condition: Axis fault indicators remain visible after pressing RESET while in manual jog mode.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot clear an axis fault using RESET while in manual jog mode (fault remains indicated on one or more axes).

actions.label: Reset axis faults
actions.exact_action: press RESET to clear the fault

steps.title: Jog axes to reposition the tote on/near the robot
steps.instruction: If the tote is lifted off the robot, jog either the Z-axis or A-axis, or both, to position the tote on or nearly on the robot. Use A1 and Z1 for the left axis; use A2 and Z2 for the right tipper.
steps.purpose: Place the tote so the robot can be commanded to the hospital station.
steps.expected_result: The tote is positioned on or nearly on the robot by jogging the correct axis controls (left: A1/Z1, right: A2/Z2).
steps.healthy_condition: Tote is positioned on/near the robot using the correct left/right axis controls (A1/Z1 for left; A2/Z2 for right).
steps.failure_condition: Tote cannot be positioned on/near the robot using the available axis jog controls for the correct side.

actions.label: Jog left tipper axes (if needed)
actions.exact_action: Use A1 and Z1 for the left axis

actions.label: Jog right tipper axes (if needed)
actions.exact_action: use A2 and Z2 for the right tipper

steps.title: Return to automatic mode with AUTO
steps.instruction: Press AUTO to enter automatic mode.
steps.purpose: Switch from manual jog mode back to automatic mode to start the recovery cycle.
steps.expected_result: Automatic mode is active (Manual Mode indicator clears/changes) on MCP_Dual (F3).
steps.healthy_condition: AUTO mode is entered and the screen reflects automatic mode context.
steps.failure_condition: AUTO does not switch the system into automatic mode.

actions.label: Enter auto
actions.exact_action: Press AUTO to enter automatic mode.

steps.title: Start cycle with CYCLE START to release grippers and command hospital
steps.instruction: Press CYCLE START. The grippers will release and the robot will be commanded to go to the hospital station.
steps.purpose: Release the grippers and command the robot to the hospital station after tote positioning and reset.
steps.expected_result: Grippers release and the robot is commanded to go to the hospital station.
steps.healthy_condition: After pressing CYCLE START, grippers release and robot proceeds toward the hospital station.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing CYCLE START does not result in gripper release and a command for the robot to go to the hospital station.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if pressing CYCLE START does not result in gripper release and a command for the robot to go to the hospital station.

actions.label: Start recovery cycle
actions.exact_action: Press CYCLE START.

steps.title: After robot leaves tipper, press RESET
steps.instruction: After the robot has left the tipper, press RESET.
steps.purpose: Complete the recovery sequence after the robot departs the tipper area.
steps.expected_result: RESET is pressed after robot departure from the tipper, completing the recovery sequence.
steps.healthy_condition: Robot has left the tipper and RESET is pressed as the final action in the sequence.
steps.failure_condition: RESET is pressed before the robot has left the tipper, or the sequence cannot be completed as instructed.

actions.label: Final reset
actions.exact_action: After the robot has left the tipper, press RESET.

title: Perform Operator Station Daily Preventive Maintenance Inspection (Controller, Stacklights, Chute Debris)
summary: Perform a daily preventive maintenance inspection of the OptiSweep operator station by checking the controller for visible damage, confirming the stacklights are operational, and ensuring the chute area is free of debris such as stuck labels.
when_to_use: Use this procedure for the daily preventive maintenance inspection of the OptiSweep operator station to verify it is safe to operate (controller condition, stacklights operational, and chute free of debris such as stuck labels).

steps.title: Inspect the operator station controller for visible damage
steps.instruction: At the operator station, visually inspect the controller for any visible damage (e.g., cracks, loose components, or other physical damage).
steps.purpose: Verify the controller is not visibly damaged before the station is used.
steps.expected_result: The controller shows no visible damage.
steps.healthy_condition: No visible damage is observed on the controller.
steps.failure_condition: Visible damage is observed on the controller.
stop_or_escalate_if: Controller has visible damage.

actions.label: Visual controller inspection
actions.exact_action: Inspect the operator station for Damage to the controller.

steps.title: Verify operator station stacklights are operational
steps.instruction: At the operator station, observe the stacklights and confirm they illuminate/operate as expected (i.e., they are operational).
steps.purpose: Confirm the stacklights are functioning as required for safe operation.
steps.expected_result: Stacklights are operational (they illuminate/operate as expected).
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklights illuminate/operate as expected.
steps.failure_condition: Stacklights do not operate (non-operational).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stacklights are not operational.

actions.label: Observe stacklight operation
actions.exact_action: Stacklights are operational.

steps.title: Inspect the chute area for debris (e.g., stuck labels)
steps.instruction: Inspect the operator station chute area and confirm it is free of debris such as stuck labels.
steps.purpose: Ensure the chute is clear so debris does not interfere with operation.
steps.expected_result: Chute area is clear with no stuck labels or other debris present.
steps.healthy_condition: No debris (e.g., stuck labels) is present in the chute area.
steps.failure_condition: Debris is present in the chute area (e.g., stuck labels).
stop_or_escalate_if: Chute contains debris (e.g., stuck labels).

actions.label: Visual chute debris check
actions.exact_action: Chute is free of debris (e.g., stuck labels).

steps.title: Stop inspection and escalate if any required condition is not met
steps.instruction: If you find controller damage, non-operational stacklights, or chute debris (e.g., stuck labels), stop the inspection and escalate to the appropriate maintenance support. For tipper-related maintenance, contact Lifecycle Performance Services (LPS) at 888-444-4647.
steps.purpose: Prevent unsafe operation by escalating when inspection findings indicate a problem.
steps.expected_result: Inspection is stopped and maintenance support is contacted/escalated due to the identified issue.
steps.healthy_condition: No escalation is needed because all inspection checks pass.
steps.failure_condition: Inspection continues despite controller damage, non-operational stacklights, or chute debris.
stop_or_escalate_if: Controller has visible damage.
Stacklights are not operational.
Chute contains debris (e.g., stuck labels).

actions.label: Escalate to maintenance support
actions.exact_action: If any damage, non-operational stacklights, or chute debris is found, stop the inspection and escalate to the appropriate maintenance support.

title: Navigate OptiSweep Operator Station HMI Screens Using F-Keys, On-Screen Buttons, and Next Screen Drop-Down

when_to_use: When you need to open the correct live operator station HMI screen at a tipper station (main control panel, data, or alarms) or navigate to a specific item / jump to another available screen.

steps.purpose: Ensure you are using the correct operator station HMI display for screen navigation.
steps.expected_result: You can visually identify the operator station HMI display at the right side of the tipper station.
steps.healthy_condition: The operator station HMI display is present and readable enough to see the current screen and navigation controls.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find the operator station HMI display on the right side of the tipper station, or the display is not usable.

stop_or_escalate_if: If pressing F6 does not navigate to the expected screen name ("Visu_Alarm"), stop and escalate to support/site troubleshooting rather than continuing to operate the station from an unknown screen state.

steps.failure_condition: Arrow buttons do not move between items, or the center button does not select/activate the navigated item.

steps.expected_result: After selecting from the Next Screen drop-down, the HMI navigates to the chosen next screen.

steps.failure_condition: The Next Screen drop-down does not change the active screen after selection.

steps.healthy_condition: You can clearly confirm the active screen corresponds to the required Visu_* screen before continuing.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confirm the active screen name, or the screen appears inconsistent with the required Visu_* screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot confirm the required screen is visible, stop and escalate to support/site troubleshooting rather than continuing to operate the station from an unknown screen state.
