title: Determine Tipper/Station Status From Operator Station Stacklights
summary: Use the operator station stacklight color/flash/horn pattern to identify the current status of the corresponding tipper and station, including RMS error, E-stop, tipping state, and bagout/surepost indications.
when_to_use: When you need to determine the current documented status of a tipper/station from the operator station stacklights (solid vs flashing colors, and horn alarm pattern when present).
not_for: Do not use this procedure to clear or reset E-stop or RMS error conditions.

steps.title: Go to the affected operator station
steps.instruction: Walk to the operator station for the affected tipper/station and position yourself so you can clearly see both stacklights.
steps.purpose: Ensure you are observing the correct stacklights for the tipper/station in question.
steps.expected_result: You can visually identify both stacklights at the operator station for the affected tipper/station.
steps.healthy_condition: Both stacklights are visible and you can distinguish solid vs flashing behavior.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot clearly see one or both stacklights (blocked view, distance, or unclear flashing).

actions.label: Visually confirm stacklight visibility
actions.exact_action: Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).

steps.title: Observe both stacklights and record solid vs flashing colors
steps.instruction: Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).
steps.purpose: Capture the observable stacklight pattern that maps to the documented tipper/station status.
steps.expected_result: You have identified each stacklight’s state (solid/flashing) and color(s).
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight colors and flashing behavior are unambiguous (e.g., solid blue vs flashing green, etc.).
steps.failure_condition: The stacklight pattern is unclear (e.g., intermittent visibility) or does not allow confident identification of solid vs flashing and color(s).

actions.label: Note stacklight state and color(s)
actions.exact_action: Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).

steps.title: If horn alarm pattern is indicated, determine long vs intermittent horn during flashing
steps.instruction: If the source indicates a horn alarm pattern for the flashing state you are seeing, also observe whether there is a long horn alarm or intermittent horn alarm during the flashing pattern.
steps.purpose: Some documented stacklight patterns include horn alarm timing; capturing it improves status mapping accuracy.
steps.expected_result: You have determined whether the horn alarm is long or intermittent during the flashing pattern.
steps.healthy_condition: Horn alarm timing is clearly distinguishable as long vs intermittent while the stacklight is flashing.
steps.failure_condition: Horn alarm timing cannot be distinguished (e.g., noise/unclear audio).

actions.label: Determine horn alarm timing
actions.exact_action: Observe whether there is a long horn alarm or intermittent horn alarm during the flashing pattern.

steps.title: Match the observed stacklight pattern to the documented tipper/station status meanings
steps.instruction: Match the observed pattern to the documented meanings for tipper/station status, including RMS error, E-stop, tipping state, and surepost/bagout indications.
steps.purpose: Convert the observed solid/flashing color (and horn timing when applicable) into the documented status.
steps.expected_result: You can map the observed stacklight solid/flashing color combination (and horn timing when present) to one documented status.
steps.healthy_condition: The observed pattern matches one of the documented combinations (examples include Solid Blue, Solid Green, Solid Red, Solid White, Solid Red+Yellow+Green, Flashing Blue, Flashing Green, Flashing Red, Flashing White, Flashing Yellow, and horn-timed combinations).
steps.failure_condition: The observed stacklight pattern does not match any documented combination.
stop_or_escalate_if: Observed stacklight pattern does not match any documented combination

actions.label: Map stacklight pattern to documented status
actions.exact_action: Match the observed pattern to the documented meanings: Solid Blue (Tipper paused), Solid Green (Tipping in process), Solid Red (Estop activated), Solid White (AGV present post-tipping), Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error), Flashing Blue (Tipper disabled), Flashing Green (Tipper starved), Flashing Red (Tipper faulted), Flashing White (SurePost tote being sent), Flashing Yellow (AGV present pre-tipping), Flashing Green+Yellow+Green with long horn alarm (Sort starting), Flashing White with intermittent horn alarm (Bagout complete).

steps.title: Stop and escalate for E-stop activated or RMS error
steps.instruction: If the mapped status indicates E-stop activated (Solid Red) or RMS error (Solid Red+Yellow+Green), stop and escalate immediately.
steps.purpose: Ensure critical conditions are handled appropriately and not cleared via this interpretation procedure.
steps.expected_result: You have identified whether the mapped status is Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error) and escalated accordingly.
steps.healthy_condition: Mapped status is not Solid Red (E-stop activated) and not Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error).
steps.failure_condition: Mapped status is Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error) and escalation is not initiated.
stop_or_escalate_if: Solid Red indicates Estop is activated
Solid Red+Yellow+Green indicates an RMS error

actions.label: Escalate critical condition
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the observed stacklight pattern indicates Estop activated (Solid Red) or RMS error (Solid Red+Yellow+Green).

title: Install Pneumatic Cylinder After Replacement (transfer fittings, bracket/rod end, reconnect air, reassemble, restart operator station)
summary: Reinstall a replaced pneumatic cylinder correctly so the lift plate rod end is pinned/retained, air lines are reconnected, covers/panels are reinstalled, and the operator station is restarted to resume normal operation.
when_to_use: Use this procedure after replacing a pneumatic cylinder when the cylinder must be reinstalled with the correct mechanical retention (rod end pin + retaining ring), air line reconnection, and reassembly, followed by restarting the operator station.

steps.title: Transfer air fittings and spherical rod end to the new cylinder
steps.instruction: Transfer the air fittings and the spherical rod end from the old cylinder to the new cylinder.
steps.purpose: Ensure the new cylinder has the correct air fittings and spherical rod end configuration before installation.
steps.expected_result: The new pneumatic cylinder has the air line fittings and spherical rod end installed/attached as transferred from the old cylinder.
steps.healthy_condition: Air line fittings and spherical rod end on the new cylinder match the transferred configuration from the old cylinder (no missing components).
steps.failure_condition: Air line fittings or the spherical rod end are not fully transferred/installed on the new cylinder.

actions.label: Transfer fittings and rod end
actions.exact_action: Transfer the air fittings and spherical rod end from the old cylinder to the new cylinder.

steps.title: Mount cylinder bottom in bracket and install bracket half with two M6 screws
steps.instruction: Place the bottom of the cylinder in the bracket, then install the other half of the bracket using two (2) M6 socket head screws.
steps.purpose: Secure the cylinder mechanically in the bracket using the specified fasteners.
steps.expected_result: The cylinder bottom is seated in the bracket and the other half of the bracket is installed using two (2) M6 socket head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Bracket halves are installed with exactly two (2) M6 socket head screws securing the cylinder in place.
steps.failure_condition: Cylinder bottom is not seated in the bracket or the bracket half is not secured with the two (2) M6 socket head screws.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the rod end cannot be fully seated between the lift plate brackets or if the pin/retaining ring cannot be installed securely.

actions.label: Seat cylinder and install bracket with M6 screws
actions.exact_action: Place the bottom of the cylinder in the bracket and install the other half of the bracket with the two (2) M6 socket head screws.

steps.title: Install rod end between lift plate brackets and secure with pin and retaining ring
steps.instruction: Slip the rod end between the brackets on the lift plate, then insert the pin and retaining ring.
steps.purpose: Provide correct mechanical retention of the lift plate rod end.
steps.expected_result: The rod end is positioned between the lift plate brackets and the pin and retaining ring are installed.
steps.healthy_condition: Pin and retaining ring are installed to retain the rod end between the lift plate brackets.
steps.failure_condition: Rod end cannot be fully seated between the lift plate brackets or the pin/retaining ring cannot be installed securely.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the rod end cannot be fully seated between the lift plate brackets or if the pin/retaining ring cannot be installed securely.

actions.label: Seat rod end and install pin/retaining ring
actions.exact_action: Slip the rod end between the brackets on the lift plate and insert the pin and retaining ring.

steps.title: Reconnect air lines
steps.instruction: Reconnect the air lines.
steps.purpose: Restore pneumatic connections required for cylinder operation.
steps.expected_result: Air lines are reconnected to the pneumatic cylinder as required by the installation.
steps.healthy_condition: Air line reconnections are complete (no disconnected fittings at the cylinder connection points).
steps.failure_condition: Air line reconnection is incomplete or fittings cannot be reattached as required.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if air line reconnection is incomplete or fittings cannot be reattached as required.

actions.label: Reconnect air lines
actions.exact_action: Reconnect the air lines.

steps.title: Replace cover plate using eight M8 button-head screws
steps.instruction: Replace the cover plate using the eight (8) M8 button-head screws.
steps.purpose: Reinstall the cover plate to restore the station’s protective enclosure.
steps.expected_result: Cover plate is installed and fastened with eight (8) M8 button-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: All eight (8) M8 button-head screws are installed securing the cover plate.
steps.failure_condition: Cover plate is not fully fastened or fewer than eight (8) M8 button-head screws are installed.

actions.label: Install cover plate with M8 screws
actions.exact_action: Replace the cover plate using the eight (8) M8 button-head screws.

steps.title: Reinstall top and/or bottom side panels if necessary
steps.instruction: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.
steps.purpose: Restore side panel enclosure components that may have been removed for access.
steps.expected_result: Top and/or bottom side panels are reinstalled if they were removed.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panels are in place (top and/or bottom as applicable) with no missing panels.
steps.failure_condition: Side panels that were removed are not reinstalled.

actions.label: Reinstall side panels
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.

steps.title: Restart the operator station
steps.instruction: Re-start the operator station (see “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
steps.purpose: Resume normal operation after mechanical and pneumatic reassembly.
steps.expected_result: The operator station is restarted after reassembly.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator station returns to normal operation after restart.
steps.failure_condition: Operator station restart does not bring the station back to normal operation after restart.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the operator station restart does not bring the station back to normal operation after restart, escalate for further troubleshooting.

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

title: Remove a Tipppper Pneumatic Cylinder (LOTO, side panel, gripper cover, air lines, retaining ring/pin, lower bracket screws)
summary: Safely remove the tipper pneumatic cylinder assembly for replacement by following the documented disassembly sequence and verifying the cylinder is released before removal.
when_to_use: Use when replacing the OptiSweep tipper pneumatic cylinder assembly and you need to remove it in the documented sequence (LOTO → side panel/gripper cover access → disconnect air lines → release lift plate via retaining ring/pin → remove lower bracket screws to free the cylinder).

steps.title: Apply LOTO to the tipper
steps.instruction: Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) to the tipper using the manual’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” method.
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely de-energized/locked out before any disassembly.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out (LOTO applied) before proceeding to remove side panel/gripper cover components.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is in place and you can proceed with cover removal without needing to energize or actuate the tipper.
steps.failure_condition: You begin disassembly without LOTO, or LOTO cannot be confirmed as applied.
stop_or_escalate_if: If LOTO cannot be applied/confirmed, stop and do not proceed with cover removal or air line disconnection.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel (if needed) to access the motor
steps.instruction: If necessary for access, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the gripper cover and pneumatic cylinder components.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (when needed) and the motor area is accessible.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine (9) self-tapping side panel securing screws are removed and the side panel comes off without forcing.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel cannot be removed because screws are missing/incorrect, or fastener sizes/counts do not match the documented nine (9) self-tapping screws.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if fasteners do not match the documented counts/sizes (nine self-tapping side panel screws).

actions.label: Check access need
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Remove the gripper cover
steps.instruction: Remove the gripper cover by removing the eight (8) M8 button head screws.
steps.purpose: Expose the pneumatic cylinder and air line connections.
steps.expected_result: Gripper cover is removed and the pneumatic cylinder area is accessible.
steps.healthy_condition: All eight (8) M8 button head screws are removed and the cover comes off without forcing.
steps.failure_condition: Cover cannot be removed because screws are missing/incorrect, or fastener sizes/counts do not match the documented eight (8) M8 button head screws.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if fasteners do not match the documented counts/sizes (eight M8 gripper cover screws).

actions.label: Remove gripper cover screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the gripper cover by removing the eight (8) M8 button head screws.

steps.title: Disconnect the two air lines from the pneumatic cylinder
steps.instruction: Remove the two (2) air lines from the pneumatic cylinder.
steps.purpose: Depressurize/disconnect pneumatic supply to allow safe release of the lift plate and cylinder removal.
steps.expected_result: Both air lines are disconnected from the pneumatic cylinder.
steps.healthy_condition: Air line connections are fully disconnected (no remaining connected hoses/lines at the cylinder ports).
steps.failure_condition: Air lines cannot be removed, or connections do not separate as expected.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop/escalate if air lines cannot be removed.

actions.label: Disconnect air lines
actions.exact_action: Remove the two (2) air lines from the pneumatic cylinder.

steps.title: Release the lift plate by removing the retaining ring and pulling the pin
steps.instruction: At the rod end of the cylinder, remove one retaining ring and pull the pin releasing the lift plate; the lift plate will drop a short distance.
steps.purpose: Allow the lift plate to drop a short distance so the cylinder can be freed.
steps.expected_result: Lift plate releases and drops a short distance after removing the retaining ring and pulling the pin.
steps.healthy_condition: Lift plate visibly drops a short distance consistent with the procedure description.
steps.failure_condition: Lift plate does not release after removing the retaining ring/pin as described.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the lift plate does not release after removing the retaining ring/pin as described; re-check that the correct retaining ring and pin are removed before proceeding.

actions.label: Remove retaining ring and pull pin
actions.exact_action: At the rod end of the cylinder, remove one retaining ring and pull the pin releasing the lift plate which will drop a short distance.

steps.title: Free the cylinder by removing the two lower bracket screws
steps.instruction: At the bottom of the cylinder, remove two (2) M6 socket head screws to release half of the lower bracket and free the air cylinder.
steps.purpose: Detach the cylinder assembly from the lower bracket so it can be removed for replacement.
steps.expected_result: Cylinder is freed after removing the two (2) M6 socket head screws (lower bracket released).
steps.healthy_condition: After removing both M6 socket head screws, the lower bracket releases as described and the cylinder can be freed without binding.
steps.failure_condition: Cylinder does not free after removing the two (2) M6 socket head screws, or fasteners do not match the documented counts/sizes.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if fasteners do not match the documented counts/sizes (two M6 socket head screws at bottom).

actions.label: Remove lower bracket screws
actions.exact_action: At the bottom of the cylinder, remove two (2) M6 socket head screws to release half of the lower bracket and free the air cylinder.

title: Apply Pneumatic LOTO at an Operator Station Shut-off Valve
summary: Safely isolate the pneumatic supply for a specific OptiSweep operator station by turning that station’s pneumatic shut-off valve to OFF and applying LOTO to secure the OFF position.
when_to_use: Use when you need to isolate pneumatic power for a specific operator station by securing its pneumatic shut-off valve in the OFF position with LOTO.

steps.title: Identify the operator station’s pneumatic shut-off valve
steps.instruction: Locate the pneumatic shut-off valve for the specific operator station you need to isolate (each operator station has its own shut-off valve).
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct operator station pneumatic supply is isolated before turning the valve OFF and applying LOTO.
steps.expected_result: You have positively identified the pneumatic shut-off valve that corresponds to the targeted operator station.
steps.healthy_condition: The valve you selected is clearly associated with the targeted operator station (not another station).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot positively identify the correct operator station’s pneumatic shut-off valve.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot positively identify the correct operator station’s shut-off valve.

actions.label: Identify correct station valve
actions.exact_action: Each operator station has its own shut-off valve.

steps.title: Turn the shut-off valve to OFF
steps.instruction: Turn the identified shut-off valve to “OFF.”
steps.purpose: Place the targeted operator station pneumatic supply into the OFF state prior to lockout/tagout.
steps.expected_result: The targeted operator station pneumatic shut-off valve is in the OFF position.
steps.healthy_condition: The valve handle/indicator shows OFF for the targeted station.
steps.failure_condition: The valve does not remain in the OFF position after turning it to OFF (unexpected movement/behavior).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the valve does not remain in the OFF position after turning it to OFF (unexpected movement/behavior).

actions.label: Set valve OFF
actions.exact_action: Turn the shut-off valve to “OFF.”

steps.title: Apply LOTO to the valve
steps.instruction: Apply LOTO to the valve to lockout/tagout the OFF position.
steps.purpose: Secure the OFF position so pneumatic power remains isolated during the work.
steps.expected_result: The targeted operator station pneumatic shut-off valve is secured with LOTO in the OFF position.
steps.healthy_condition: A lock and tag are applied such that the valve remains secured in OFF.
steps.failure_condition: LOTO is not applied to secure the OFF position (valve not secured/lockout not present).

actions.label: Lockout/tagout OFF
actions.exact_action: 2. LOTO the valve.

title: Remove Pneumatic Valve From Tipper (LOTO, side panel access, valve cover screws, M8 connector disconnect)
summary: Safely prepare the OptiSweep tipper for pneumatic valve replacement by performing lockout/tagout (LOTO), exposing the valve cover (including removing the station side panel if needed), removing the valve cover fasteners, and disconnecting the valve’s M8 electrical connector.
when_to_use: Use when you are preparing the OptiSweep tipper station for pneumatic valve replacement and need to LOTO the tipper, access the valve cover, remove the valve cover fasteners, and disconnect the valve’s M8 electrical connector.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for diagnosing tipper station faults on HMI/DB/API surfaces; this is a physical prep/removal step set for valve replacement.

steps.title: Gather required tools and PPE
steps.instruction: On the physical floor, stage the replacement pneumatic valve, PPE (safety glasses and gloves), and the required hex wrenches (2.5-mm, 3-mm, 5-mm, 6-mm), plus a 3/8-in. wrench or socket and Loctite®.
steps.purpose: Ensure you have the specified tools, PPE, and replacement part before starting LOTO and disassembly.
steps.expected_result: You have the specified tools/PPE available to proceed with LOTO, side panel access (if needed), valve cover fastener removal, and M8 connector disconnection.
steps.healthy_condition: All required tools/PPE are present and ready for use before you begin disassembly.
steps.failure_condition: Missing required tools/PPE or inability to proceed without improvising (e.g., wrong wrench size).

actions.label: Stage tools and PPE
actions.exact_action: Gather required tools and PPE: replacement pneumatic valve; safety glasses and gloves; 2.5-mm, 3-mm, 5-mm, and 6-mm hex wrenches; 3/8-in. wrench or socket; Loctite®

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the tipper
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the manual’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” procedure (referenced on page 2).
steps.purpose: De-energize and secure the tipper for safe mechanical/electrical work.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out/tagged out prior to removing the valve cover and disconnecting the M8 electrical connector.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed and the tipper is secured before proceeding to side panel/valve cover removal.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot safely complete LOTO or LOTO cannot be verified as applied before disassembly.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot safely perform LOTO.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove station side panel for motor/valve access (if necessary)
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the valve cover area by removing the station side panel when required.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (when necessary) to access the motor/valve cover area.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel removal is complete without forcing fasteners; access to the motor/valve cover area is unobstructed.
steps.failure_condition: Valve cover access cannot be achieved without forcing screws/fasteners, or side panel removal is unsafe.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the valve cover cannot be removed without forcing fasteners.

actions.label: Remove side panel screws
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Remove valve cover fasteners (four M4 socket head screws)
steps.instruction: Remove the four (4) M4 socket head screws holding the valve cover in place.
steps.purpose: Expose the pneumatic valve by removing the valve cover.
steps.expected_result: The four (4) M4 socket head screws are removed and the valve cover is no longer secured.
steps.healthy_condition: All four M4 socket head screws are removed cleanly; valve cover is ready to be accessed for the M8 connector disconnect.
steps.failure_condition: Fasteners cannot be removed without forcing, or the valve cover cannot be removed safely.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the valve cover cannot be removed without forcing fasteners.

actions.label: Remove valve cover screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the four (4) M4 socket head screws holding the valve cover in place.

steps.title: Disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the valve edge
steps.instruction: Disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the valve.
steps.purpose: Disconnect electrical connection to the pneumatic valve to complete the removal/prep stage.
steps.expected_result: The M8 electrical connector is disconnected from the edge of the valve.
steps.healthy_condition: Connector disconnect is achieved without excessive force; no visible wiring/connector damage is observed during disconnect.
steps.failure_condition: M8 connector cannot be disconnected without excessive force, or wiring/connector damage is observed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the M8 connector cannot be disconnected without excessive force or if wiring/connector damage is observed.

actions.label: Disconnect M8 connector
actions.exact_action: Disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the valve.

title: Manually Reference/Position Tipper End Effector for Maintenance Using Visu_Dual_MCP (Navigate + CYCLE STOP)
summary: Navigate to the Visu_Dual_MCP screen on the operator station HMI and press CYCLE STOP to stop the automatic tipping cycle so the end effector can be manually positioned for maintenance procedures.
when_to_use: Use when maintenance requires manually moving the tipper end effector into position, and you need to stop the automatic tipping cycle first.

steps.title: Navigate to the Visu_Dual_MCP screen (F3) on the operator station HMI
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3).
steps.purpose: Open the correct HMI screen that contains the CYCLE STOP control used to halt the automatic tipping cycle.
steps.expected_result: The operator station HMI is displaying the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3).
steps.healthy_condition: The "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen is active and ready for control inputs (including CYCLE STOP).
steps.failure_condition: The HMI is not on the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3), so CYCLE STOP cannot be applied to stop the automatic tipping cycle.

actions.label: Open Visu_Dual_MCP (F3)
actions.exact_action: navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3)

steps.title: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the automatic tipping cycle
steps.instruction: Press CYCLE STOP on the Visu_Dual_MCP screen to stop the automatic tipping cycle.
steps.purpose: Stop the automatic tipping cycle so the end effector can be manually moved into position for maintenance.
steps.expected_result: The automatic tipping cycle is stopped after pressing CYCLE STOP.
steps.healthy_condition: After pressing CYCLE STOP, the system is no longer running the automatic tipping cycle (cycle is halted), enabling manual positioning for maintenance.
steps.failure_condition: The automatic tipping cycle does not stop after pressing CYCLE STOP.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the automatic tipping cycle does not stop after pressing CYCLE STOP, stop and escalate for support rather than attempting manual movement.

actions.label: Stop automatic cycle
actions.exact_action: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the automatic tipping cycle.

title: Remove and replace a Limit/Home sensor (A-axis or Z-axis) with LOTO
summary: Perform LOTO on the OptiSweep tipper, unplug the defective Limit/Home proximity sensor, and remove it from its mounting location. A-axis sensors are unplugged from a PCA near the A-axis motor; Z-axis sensors are unplugged from the CLINK controller inside the control box.
when_to_use: Use when a Limit/Home proximity sensor (A-axis or Z-axis) is defective and must be unplugged and physically removed for replacement.

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the tipper
steps.instruction: Apply Operator Station Lockout/Tagout to the tipper (LOTO the tipper).
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely locked out/tagged out before unplugging the sensor.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is in a locked-out/tagged-out state prior to sensor unplugging/removal.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed and the tipper is secured such that sensor unplugging/removal can be performed safely.
steps.failure_condition: LOTO cannot be completed or the tipper lockout/tagout controls are not accessible/clear.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if LOTO cannot be completed or the tipper lockout/tagout controls are not accessible/clear.

actions.label: LOTO the tipper
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Unplug the sensor
steps.instruction: Unplug the Limit/Home sensor.
steps.purpose: Disconnect the defective Limit/Home proximity sensor electrically before physical removal.
steps.expected_result: The defective sensor is electrically disconnected (unplugged) from its connection point.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor unplugging is straightforward and does not require forcing or damaging nearby wiring/connectors.
steps.failure_condition: The sensor cannot be unplugged without forcing (risk of damaging PCA/CLINK controller wiring).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the sensor cannot be unplugged without forcing (risk of damaging the PCA/CLINK controller wiring or the wire routing).

actions.label: Unplug sensor
actions.exact_action: Unplug the sensor.

steps.title: Identify sensor type by location (A-axis vs Z-axis)
steps.instruction: Identify whether the defective sensor is an A-axis sensor or a Z-axis sensor by its location and connection type.
steps.purpose: Use the correct physical removal method based on where the sensor is mounted and connected.
steps.expected_result: You correctly determine the sensor location: A-axis sensors are plugged into a PCA near the A-axis motor; Z-axis sensors are plugged into the CLINK controller inside the control box.
steps.healthy_condition: A-axis sensor is recognized as PCA-near-A-axis-motor connection; Z-axis sensor is recognized as CLINK-controller-inside-control-box connection.
steps.failure_condition: Sensor location/type cannot be confidently identified, leading to incorrect removal approach.

actions.label: Identify by location
actions.exact_action: A-axis sensors are plugged into a printed circuit assembly (PCA) near the A-axis motor; Z-axis sensors are plugged into the CLINK controller inside the control box.

steps.title: Remove the mounting screw and feed the sensor through the wire routing hole
steps.instruction: Remove the M3 button-head screw holding the sensor in place and feed the sensor through the hole where the wire is routed.
steps.purpose: Physically detach the sensor from its mounting location and free it from the routed wiring path.
steps.expected_result: The sensor is unfastened (M3 button-head screw removed) and can be fed through the wire routing hole.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor removal proceeds without forcing; the wire routing hole allows the sensor to pass cleanly.
steps.failure_condition: Forcing is required to remove the sensor, risking damage to PCA/CLINK controller wiring or wire routing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the sensor cannot be unplugged or removed without forcing (risk of damaging the PCA/CLINK controller wiring or the wire routing).

actions.label: Remove M3 screw
actions.exact_action: Remove the M3 button-head screw holding the sensor in place and feed the sensor through the hole where the wire is routed.

steps.title: For Z-axis sensors: pull the sensor from the column
steps.instruction: If the sensor is Z-axis, pull the Z-axis sensor from the column.
steps.purpose: Complete physical removal for Z-axis sensor assemblies.
steps.expected_result: The Z-axis sensor is fully removed from the column.
steps.healthy_condition: The sensor pulls free without resistance that would require forcing.
steps.failure_condition: The sensor cannot be pulled free without forcing (risk of damaging wiring or mounting).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the sensor cannot be unplugged or removed without forcing (risk of damaging the PCA/CLINK controller wiring or the wire routing).

actions.label: Pull Z-axis sensor
actions.exact_action: Pull the Z-axis sensor from the column.

steps.title: For A-axis sensors: pull the sensor away; cut wire tie if needed
steps.instruction: If the sensor is A-axis, pull the defective A-axis sensor away. If needed, cut the wire tie to free the sensor.
steps.purpose: Complete physical removal for A-axis sensor assemblies, including freeing it from any wire tie restraint.
steps.expected_result: The A-axis sensor is removed from its mounting location; any wire tie that blocks removal is cut if required.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor removal is achieved without damaging the PCA wiring; wire tie is cut only if it prevents removal.
steps.failure_condition: Forcing is required to free the sensor, or cutting is not performed when a wire tie blocks removal.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the sensor cannot be unplugged or removed without forcing (risk of damaging the PCA/CLINK controller wiring or the wire routing).

actions.label: Pull A-axis sensor
actions.exact_action: For A-axis sensors: pull the defective A-axis sensor away; if needed, cut the wire tie to free the sensor.

title: Route a replacement sensor through the frame, connect M8, reinstall M3 screw, and re-start the operator station
summary: Route a replacement sensor through the frame, connect the M8 connection, reinstall the M3 button-head screw, reinstall any removed grommets, and re-start the operator station.
when_to_use: Use when a replacement sensor must be installed by routing it through the frame, securing it with the M8 connection and M3 button-head screw, and then re-starting the operator station.

steps.title: Tape the replacement sensor to the M8 connector to route it through the frame
steps.instruction: Tape the replacement sensor to the M8 connector so the old sensor can be used to route the new sensor through the frame.
steps.purpose: Use the old sensor as a pull-through method so the replacement sensor can be routed through the frame without excessive force.
steps.expected_result: The replacement sensor is taped to the M8 connector in a way that allows the old sensor to be used to pull/route the new sensor through the frame.
steps.healthy_condition: The replacement sensor can be routed without excessive force (no binding during pull-through).
steps.failure_condition: The sensor cannot be routed through the frame without excessive force.
stop_or_escalate_if: Sensor cannot be routed through the frame without excessive force.

actions.label: Tape replacement sensor to M8 connector
actions.exact_action: Tape the replacement sensor to the M8 connector so the old sensor can be used to route the new sensor through the frame.

steps.title: Pull the sensor out
steps.instruction: Pull the sensor out.
steps.purpose: Remove the old sensor after it has been used to route the replacement sensor through the frame.
steps.expected_result: The old sensor is pulled out after routing the replacement sensor through the frame.
steps.healthy_condition: Replacement sensor remains routed through the frame after the old sensor is removed.
steps.failure_condition: Replacement sensor does not remain routed correctly (binding, misrouting, or inability to proceed to connection).

actions.label: Pull sensor out
actions.exact_action: Pull the sensor out.

steps.title: Route the sensor through the frame
steps.instruction: Route the sensor through the frame.
steps.purpose: Ensure the replacement sensor is positioned correctly through the frame for proper connection and operation.
steps.expected_result: The sensor is routed through the frame.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor routing is complete and does not require excessive force to position.
steps.failure_condition: Sensor cannot be routed through the frame without excessive force.
stop_or_escalate_if: Sensor cannot be routed through the frame without excessive force.

actions.label: Route sensor through frame

steps.title: Connect the M8 connection and re-install the M3 button-head screw
steps.instruction: Connect the M8 connection and re-install the M3 button-head screw.
steps.purpose: Secure the sensor electrically/mechanically using the specified M8 connection and M3 button-head screw.
steps.expected_result: The M8 connection is connected and the M3 button-head screw is reinstalled.
steps.healthy_condition: M3 button-head screw is installed at the specified location and the M8 connection is fully connected (no loose connection).
steps.failure_condition: M8 connection cannot be connected properly or M3 button-head screw cannot be reinstalled.

actions.label: Connect M8 and reinstall M3 screw
actions.exact_action: Connect the M8 connection and re-install the M3 button-head screw.

steps.title: Re-install any removed grommets
steps.instruction: Re-install any removed grommets.
steps.purpose: Restore wire strain relief/sealing by reinstalling grommets that were removed to route the sensor.

steps.failure_condition: Grommets cannot be reinstalled.
stop_or_escalate_if: Grommets cannot be reinstalled.

actions.label: Reinstall grommets
actions.exact_action: Re-install any removed grommets.

steps.title: Re-start the operator station
steps.instruction: Re-start the operator station (referenced as 'Starting The Operator Station' on page 66).
steps.purpose: Bring the operator station back online so the system can recognize the newly installed sensor.
steps.expected_result: The operator station is restarted using the manual’s referenced procedure.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator station restart completes successfully and the system proceeds past the restart state (no restart failure).
steps.failure_condition: Operator station cannot be re-started using the referenced procedure.
stop_or_escalate_if: Operator station cannot be re-started using the referenced procedure.

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

title: Stop the Automatic Tipping Cycle From Operator Station HMI (Visu_Dual_MCP → CYCLE STOP)

steps.title: Navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) on the operator station HMI
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3).

steps.expected_result: The operator station HMI is displaying the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen.
steps.healthy_condition: The "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen is active and ready for operator controls (including CYCLE STOP).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot reach the "Visu_Dual_MCP" screen (F3) or the screen shown is not the "Visu_Dual_MCP" interface.

steps.title: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the automatic tipping cycle
steps.instruction: Press CYCLE STOP to stop the automatic tipping cycle.
steps.purpose: Halt the automatic tipping cycle so maintenance procedures and/or manual end-effector positioning can proceed.
steps.expected_result: The automatic tipping cycle is stopped after pressing CYCLE STOP.
steps.healthy_condition: After pressing CYCLE STOP, the automatic tipping cycle is no longer running.
steps.failure_condition: The automatic cycle does not stop after pressing CYCLE STOP.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the automatic cycle does not stop after pressing CYCLE STOP, stop attempting and escalate for support.

actions.label: Stop automatic cycle

title: Stop the OptiSweep System Using the System HMI API Screen (SYSTEM SHUTDOWN)
summary: Use the system HMI API screen to initiate SYSTEM SHUTDOWN and confirm the AGVs transition to a shutdown queue between sorts.
when_to_use: When you need to stop the OptiSweep system between sorts so AGVs move to a shutdown queue.

steps.title: Navigate to the system API screen on the system HMI
steps.instruction: On the system HMI, navigate to the system API screen.
steps.purpose: Open the correct system control screen to initiate SYSTEM SHUTDOWN.
steps.expected_result: The system API screen is open and ready for the SYSTEM SHUTDOWN action.
steps.healthy_condition: The system API screen is displayed with the System API controls available.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot locate the system API screen or the SYSTEM SHUTDOWN control is not accessible.

actions.label: Open system API screen
actions.exact_action: On the system HMI, navigate to the system API screen.

steps.title: Press SYSTEM SHUTDOWN
steps.instruction: Press SYSTEM SHUTDOWN on the system API screen.
steps.purpose: Initiate the system shutdown sequence that routes AGVs to the shutdown queue.
steps.expected_result: SYSTEM SHUTDOWN is initiated.
steps.healthy_condition: The SYSTEM SHUTDOWN action is accepted by the system (shutdown sequence begins).
steps.failure_condition: SYSTEM SHUTDOWN does not initiate (no shutdown behavior follows).

actions.label: Initiate system shutdown
actions.exact_action: Press SYSTEM SHUTDOWN.

steps.title: Confirm AGVs transition to the shutdown queue
steps.instruction: Observe that the AGVs go to a shutdown queue after SYSTEM SHUTDOWN.
steps.purpose: Verify the shutdown outcome required for between-sorts operation.
steps.expected_result: AGVs are in a shutdown queue state.
steps.healthy_condition: AGVs transition into the shutdown queue after SYSTEM SHUTDOWN.
steps.failure_condition: AGVs do not transition to the shutdown queue after SYSTEM SHUTDOWN.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if AGVs do not transition to the shutdown queue after SYSTEM SHUTDOWN.

actions.label: Verify shutdown queue transition
actions.exact_action: Observe that the AGVs go to a shutdown queue.

title: Install and tension a replacement timing belt (counter-balance leg) to 471 N
summary: Hands-on installation procedure for replacing an OptiSweep timing belt and setting counter-balance leg belt tension to the specified target (471 N) using equal tensioning of two screws and (optionally) a Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter, followed by torque/fastener steps and operator-station restart.
when_to_use: Use when replacing the OptiSweep timing belt and you must set the counter-balance leg belt tension to 471 N (acceptable range 448–494 N) before reassembly and restarting the operator station.

steps.title: Place the new timing belt on the pulleys
steps.instruction: Place the new timing belt on the pulleys.
steps.purpose: Install the replacement belt onto the pulley path before tensioning and securing.
steps.expected_result: The replacement timing belt is seated on the pulleys in the intended routing path, ready for counter-balance positioning and tensioning.
steps.healthy_condition: Belt is correctly positioned on the pulleys with no obvious misrouting before tensioning.
steps.failure_condition: Belt is not seated on the pulleys or is visibly misrouted such that tensioning would be incorrect.

actions.label: Seat belt on pulleys
actions.exact_action: Place the new timing belt on the pulleys.

steps.title: Position counter-balance carriage on lower hard stop
steps.instruction: Slightly lift the counter-balance carriage, remove the M6 fastener supporting it, and lower the counter-balance carriage to rest on the lower hard stop.
steps.purpose: Set the counter-balance carriage to the correct resting position so the belt can be tensioned properly.
steps.expected_result: Counter-balance carriage is resting on the lower hard stop after the M6 fastener is removed.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriage rests on the lower hard stop (not suspended) with the supporting M6 fastener removed.
steps.failure_condition: Carriage remains lifted/suspended or does not rest on the lower hard stop after removing the M6 fastener.

actions.label: Lift, remove M6, lower to hard stop
actions.exact_action: Slightly lift the counter-balance carriage, remove the M6 fastener supporting it, and lower the counter-balance carriage to rest on the lower hard stop.

steps.title: Very lightly tighten M8x25 idler assembly screws
steps.instruction: Very lightly tighten the M8x25 screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place so the assembly is not loose, but it can slide under the fasteners.
steps.purpose: Hold the idler pulley assembly in place while still allowing it to slide under the fasteners during tensioning.
steps.expected_result: Idler pulley assembly is held snugly (not loose) but can still slide under the M8x25 fasteners during tension adjustment.
steps.healthy_condition: Assembly does not rattle/shift freely, yet tensioning can move it as tension increases.
steps.failure_condition: Assembly is too loose (moves excessively) or too tight (does not allow sliding during tensioning).

actions.label: Lightly snug idler assembly
actions.exact_action: Very lightly tighten the M8x25 screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place so the assembly is not loose, but it can slide under the fasteners.

steps.title: Insert M6x35 tension screws to firm contact
steps.instruction: Insert the two M6x35 tension screws until they make firm contact with the actuator base.
steps.purpose: Establish initial contact points for tensioning the belt via the actuator base.
steps.expected_result: Both M6x35 tension screws are inserted and each makes firm contact with the actuator base.
steps.healthy_condition: No gap between each screw tip and the actuator base at the contact point.
steps.failure_condition: One or both screws are not contacting the actuator base (insufficient insertion).

actions.label: Seat tension screws
actions.exact_action: Insert the two M6x35 tension screws until they make firm contact with the actuator base.

steps.title: Equally tighten tension screws
steps.instruction: Equally tighten the tension screws to add tension to the belt, ensuring both screws are turned the exact same amount (same applied force).
steps.purpose: Apply belt tension evenly by turning both tension screws the same amount/force.
steps.expected_result: Both tension screws have been advanced equally, producing balanced belt tension increase.
steps.healthy_condition: No visible imbalance between the two tension screw positions/advancement; tension increases evenly.
steps.failure_condition: One screw is advanced more than the other (unequal applied force), leading to uneven tension.

actions.label: Equal turns on both screws
actions.exact_action: Equally tighten the tension screws… ensuring both screws are turned the exact same amount (same applied force).

steps.title: Increase tension to 471 N (448–494 N acceptable range)
steps.instruction: Gradually increase tension until 471 N is reached (acceptable range 448 N to 494 N).
steps.purpose: Bring belt tension to the specified target before locking the idler assembly.
steps.expected_result: Measured belt tension reaches 471 N within the acceptable range of 448–494 N.
steps.healthy_condition: Tension reading is within 448–494 N and as close to 471 N as practical.
steps.failure_condition: Tension cannot be brought into the 448–494 N range.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if tension cannot be brought into the 448–494 N range.

actions.label: Adjust until target tension
actions.exact_action: Gradually increase tension until 471 N is reached (acceptable range 448 N to 494 N).

steps.title: Check tension only on the counter-balance leg
steps.instruction: Check tension only on the counter-balance leg of the belt (counter-balance is not in the way and will not interfere with belt vibration).
steps.purpose: Ensure the tension measurement corresponds to the correct belt segment.
steps.expected_result: Tension measurement is taken on the counter-balance leg only.
steps.healthy_condition: Measurement location is on the counter-balance leg and counter-balance does not interfere with belt vibration.
steps.failure_condition: Tension is checked on a different leg or counter-balance interferes with belt vibration during measurement.

actions.label: Measure correct belt leg
actions.exact_action: Check tension only on the counter-balance leg of the belt…

steps.title: Set Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter parameters (if used)
steps.instruction: If using a Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter, set: Mass = 4.86 g/m, Width = 20 mm, Span = 1200 mm.
steps.purpose: Configure the sonic tension meter to the correct belt parameters for accurate readings.
steps.expected_result: Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter is configured with Mass 4.86 g/m, Width 20 mm, Span 1200 mm.
steps.healthy_condition: Meter settings match the specified values before taking tension readings.
steps.failure_condition: Meter settings are not set to the specified values, leading to incorrect tension readings.

actions.label: Configure sonic meter
actions.exact_action: If using a Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter, set: Mass = 4.86 g/m, Width = 20 mm, Span = 1200 mm.

steps.title: Obtain three acceptable sonic readings in a row
steps.instruction: Adjust/check until three acceptable readings in a row are received. Note: excessive noise (e.g., forklifts beeping, conveyors running) can interfere with sonic meter readings.
steps.purpose: Verify stable tension measurement before locking the idler assembly.
steps.expected_result: Three consecutive sonic tension readings are acceptable.
steps.healthy_condition: Readings remain stable and acceptable across three consecutive checks.
steps.failure_condition: Three consecutive acceptable readings cannot be obtained, or readings are unstable due to excessive noise.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if three consecutive acceptable sonic meter readings cannot be obtained.
If excessive noise prevents stable sonic readings, reduce noise sources and re-check tension.

actions.label: Stabilize and re-check
actions.exact_action: Adjust/check until three acceptable readings in a row are received.

steps.title: Torque M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs)
steps.instruction: Tighten the M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs) to lock the idler assembly in place.
steps.purpose: Lock the idler pulley assembly in place after achieving correct belt tension.
steps.expected_result: M8x25 fasteners are torqued to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs), locking the idler assembly.
steps.healthy_condition: Fasteners are tightened to the specified torque value using the torque tool.
steps.failure_condition: Idler assembly is not locked (e.g., fasteners not torqued to spec) or tension shifts after tightening.

actions.label: Torque idler fasteners
actions.exact_action: Tighten the M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs) to lock the idler assembly in place.

steps.title: Raise counter-balance carriage and insert M6 socket-head screws
steps.instruction: Raise the counter-balance carriage back to mid-travel and insert the M6 socket-head screws for the carriage to rest against.
steps.purpose: Set the counter-balance carriage to mid-travel and secure it with the specified screws before clamp reattachment.
steps.expected_result: Counter-balance carriage is at mid-travel and supported/resting against the inserted M6 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriage is positioned at mid-travel with screws installed as the rest support.
steps.failure_condition: Carriage is not at mid-travel or screws are not inserted to provide the rest support.

actions.label: Set mid-travel rest
actions.exact_action: Raise the counter-balance carriage back to mid-travel and insert the M6 socket-head screws for the carriage to rest against.

steps.title: Re-attach A-axis belt clamp with M6x20 screws and Loctite®
steps.instruction: Re-attach the A-axis belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring the belt clamp aligns with belt teeth and does not pinch the belt (belt may need slight movement to line up).
steps.purpose: Secure the A-axis belt clamp while ensuring the belt is not pinched and clamp aligns with belt teeth.
steps.expected_result: A-axis belt clamp is reattached with six M6x20 screws using Loctite®, aligned with belt teeth, and belt is not pinched.
steps.healthy_condition: Clamp teeth alignment matches belt teeth; belt can move/seat without being pinched by the clamp.
steps.failure_condition: Belt clamp is misaligned with belt teeth or pinches the belt.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check clamp alignment if the belt appears pinched or the belt clamp does not align with belt teeth.

actions.label: Attach A-axis belt clamp
actions.exact_action: Re-attach the A-axis belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring the belt clamp aligns with belt teeth and does not pinch the belt (belt may need slight movement to line up).

steps.title: Re-attach counter-balance belt clamp with M6x20 screws and Loctite®
steps.instruction: Re-attach the counter-balance belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring alignment with belt teeth and no belt pinch (counter-balance may need to be lifted slightly for alignment).
steps.purpose: Secure the counter-balance belt clamp while ensuring alignment with belt teeth and no belt pinch.
steps.expected_result: Counter-balance belt clamp is reattached with six M6x20 screws using Loctite®, aligned with belt teeth, and belt is not pinched.
steps.healthy_condition: Clamp alignment matches belt teeth; belt is free of pinch points.
steps.failure_condition: Counter-balance belt clamp is misaligned or pinches the belt.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check clamp alignment if the belt appears pinched or the belt clamp does not align with belt teeth.

actions.label: Attach counter-balance belt clamp
actions.exact_action: Re-attach the counter-balance belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring alignment with belt teeth and no belt pinch (counter-balance may need to be lifted slightly for alignment).

steps.title: Remove M6 socket-head screws supporting A-axis and counter-balance
steps.instruction: Remove the M6 socket-head screws supporting the A-axis and counter-balance.
steps.purpose: Remove temporary supports once clamps are installed.
steps.expected_result: The M6 socket-head screws that supported the A-axis and counter-balance are removed.
steps.healthy_condition: No remaining support screws; A-axis and counter-balance are held by the installed belt/clamps as intended.
steps.failure_condition: Support screws remain installed when they should be removed, or removal destabilizes the assembly.

actions.label: Remove support screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the M6 socket-head screws supporting the A-axis and counter-balance.

steps.title: Reinstall side panels
steps.instruction: Reinstall the side panels.
steps.purpose: Restore station enclosure after belt/clamp installation.
steps.expected_result: Side panels are reinstalled.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panels are back in place, covering the belt/tensioning area.
steps.failure_condition: Side panels not fully reinstalled or left open after completion.

actions.label: Reinstall side panels
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the side panels.

steps.title: Restart the operator station
steps.instruction: Re-start the operator station (referenced as “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
steps.purpose: Return the station to service after mechanical work is complete.
steps.expected_result: Operator station is restarted per the manual’s referenced restart procedure.
steps.healthy_condition: Station restart completes successfully (no immediate mechanical issues attributable to belt/clamp pinch or incorrect tension).
steps.failure_condition: Restart fails or immediate issues indicate belt/clamp problems (e.g., belt pinch, tension not within target).

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (referenced as “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).

title: Remove Timing Belt on Tipper Station (A-axis/counterbalance positioning, LOTO, side panel removal, belt access)
summary: Safely prepare the OptiSweep tipper station for timing belt replacement by manually positioning the A-axis/counterbalance between the actuator-base threaded holes, performing site “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” on the tipper, removing the nine (9) self-tapping side-panel fasteners to access the timing belt, and threading M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
when_to_use: Use this procedure when preparing the tipper station for timing belt replacement and you must (1) position the A-axis/counterbalance correctly, (2) lock out/tag out the tipper using the site Operator Station LOTO process, (3) remove the station side panels to access the timing belt, and (4) install M6 socket-head screws below both carriages before releasing belt tension.
not_for: Do not proceed to belt tension release unless the M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping.

steps.title: Manually position the A-axis and counterbalance between actuator-base threaded holes
steps.instruction: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.purpose: Place the A-axis/counterbalance in the correct safe position so the station side panels can be removed and the belt access/prevent-drop screws can be installed.
steps.expected_result: The A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the threaded holes on their respective rails (two holes adjacent to each rail).
steps.healthy_condition: Both carriages are visibly located between the threaded holes adjacent to each rail (not outside the hole pair).
steps.failure_condition: One or both carriages are not between the threaded holes on their respective rails.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check positioning if the carriages are not between the threaded holes on their respective rails.

actions.label: Position A-axis/counterbalance
actions.exact_action: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the site Operator Station Lockout/Tagout process
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the site’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” process.
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely de-energized/locked out before removing side panels and accessing the timing belt area.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is in a locked-out/tagged-out state per the site Operator Station Lockout/Tagout process.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed and verified for the tipper before proceeding to side panel removal.
steps.failure_condition: LOTO cannot be completed/verified for the tipper.
stop_or_escalate_if: Do not proceed if LOTO cannot be completed/verified for the tipper.

actions.label: Execute site LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the nine (9) self-tapping side-panel fasteners and remove side panels to access the timing belt
steps.instruction: Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the station side panels, then remove the station side panels to access the timing belt.
steps.purpose: Expose the timing belt so the belt replacement preparation can continue.
steps.expected_result: The nine (9) self-tapping side-panel fasteners are removed and the station side panels are off, exposing the timing belt access area.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panels are removed and the timing belt area is accessible without obstruction.
steps.failure_condition: Side panels remain secured (fasteners not fully removed) or timing belt access is obstructed.

actions.label: Remove side-panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panels then remove the station side panels to access the timing belt.

steps.title: Thread M6 socket-head screws into holes below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.instruction: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.
steps.purpose: Mechanically prevent the A-axis and counterbalance from dropping when belt tension is released.
steps.expected_result: M6 socket-head screws are installed in the holes below both carriages.
steps.healthy_condition: Both sets of holes below the carriages have M6 socket-head screws threaded in place (prevent-drop condition established).
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screws are not installed below one or both carriages.
stop_or_escalate_if: Do not release belt tension unless the M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping.

actions.label: Install M6 prevent-drop screws
actions.exact_action: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

title: LOTO the tipper and remove the station side panel to access the motor for Timing Pulley Replacement
summary: Perform lockout/tagout (LOTO) for the specific tipper being serviced, then remove the station side panel (by removing nine self-tapping fasteners if needed) to access the motor area prior to Timing Pulley Replacement.
when_to_use: Use when you must service the tipper’s motor area for Timing Pulley Replacement and need safe physical access by applying LOTO and removing the station side panel.
not_for: Do not proceed with side panel removal if you cannot confirm LOTO is correctly applied to the tipper.

steps.title: Identify the specific tipper and perform LOTO
steps.instruction: Identify the specific tipper to be serviced. Perform LOTO for that tipper using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure on page 2.
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct tipper is isolated and safe before any physical access work.
steps.expected_result: The tipper being serviced is locked out/tagged out.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is correctly applied to the specific tipper prior to proceeding to side panel removal.
steps.failure_condition: LOTO cannot be confirmed as correctly applied to the tipper.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-verify LOTO is correctly applied before proceeding if lockout/tagout cannot be confirmed.

actions.label: Apply LOTO to the tipper
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel (remove nine self-tapping fasteners if necessary)
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing fasteners on the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Gain physical access to the motor area by removing the station side panel.
steps.expected_result: The nine self-tapping fasteners are removed (if needed) and the station side panel is removed, exposing the motor area.
steps.healthy_condition: Station side panel is removed and the motor area is accessible after fasteners are removed.
steps.failure_condition: The side panel cannot be removed after removing the nine self-tapping fasteners.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the side panel cannot be removed after removing the nine self-tapping fasteners, stop and escalate for assistance rather than forcing the panel.

actions.label: Remove side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

title: Remove Tip (or A-Axis) Cable From Tipper/A-Axis Carriage
summary: Safely remove the Tip (A-Axis) cable from the OptiSweep tipper station by performing LOTO, removing the station side panel and valve cover, disconnecting the four M8 connectors, routing the cable through the grommet, opening the snap-open cable carrier, cutting cable ties, and unplugging the cable from the A-axis PCA.
when_to_use: Use when the Tip (or A-Axis) cable must be physically disconnected/removed from the tipper station (e.g., for maintenance/replacement), following the manual’s removal steps.

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the tipper
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the tipper (manual references "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is locked out/tagged out before any panel/cover removal or electrical connector disconnection.
steps.expected_result: Tipper is under LOTO prior to proceeding to side panel/valve cover removal and cable disconnection.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is in place and you can proceed with safe access to the station components.
steps.failure_condition: LOTO is not completed or cannot be verified before proceeding.
stop_or_escalate_if: If LOTO cannot be completed, stop and escalate to FORTNA support.

actions.label: Apply LOTO to tipper
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel to access the motor (if necessary)
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping screws securing the side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the valve cover and cable routing area inside the tipper station.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed, exposing the motor access area for subsequent valve cover removal.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel removal is complete and the motor/access area is reachable for the next step.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel cannot be removed as described (e.g., screws not accessible or not removable).
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to FORTNA support if access to the motor/valve cover cannot be achieved as described.

actions.label: Remove side panel screws
actions.exact_action: use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Remove the valve cover
steps.instruction: Remove the valve cover by removing the four (4) M4x50 socket-head screws.
steps.purpose: Expose the valve cover area so the Tip (A-Axis) cable connections can be accessed/disconnected.
steps.expected_result: Valve cover is removed after taking out the four (4) M4x50 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Valve cover is fully removed and the cable connection area is accessible.
steps.failure_condition: Valve cover cannot be removed because screws are not removed or cover remains secured.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to FORTNA support if the valve cover cannot be removed as described.

actions.label: Remove valve cover screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the valve cover by removing the four (4) M4x50 socket-head screws.

steps.title: Disconnect all four (4) M8 connectors
steps.instruction: Disconnect all four (4) M8 connectors.
steps.purpose: Unplug the Tip (A-Axis) cable electrical connections from the A-axis carriage.
steps.expected_result: All four M8 connectors are disconnected from the A-axis carriage.
steps.healthy_condition: No M8 connectors remain physically connected.
steps.failure_condition: One or more M8 connectors remain connected.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if any M8 connectors remain connected.

actions.label: Disconnect M8 connectors
actions.exact_action: Disconnect all four (4) M8 connectors.

steps.title: Route the cable through the grommet and feed M8 connectors one at a time
steps.instruction: Pull the jacketed part of the cable out of the grommet, then feed all the M8 connectors through the grommet one at a time.
steps.purpose: Remove the cable from the station while ensuring the connectors pass through the grommet correctly.
steps.expected_result: Cable jacket is pulled out of the grommet and all four M8 connectors have been fed through the grommet.
steps.healthy_condition: Cable and connectors are free of the grommet path and can be moved toward the cable carrier.
steps.failure_condition: Cable cannot be pulled free after opening the cable carrier cross bars (or connectors cannot pass through the grommet).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if the cable cannot be pulled free after opening the cable carrier cross bars.

actions.label: Pull jacket and feed connectors through grommet
actions.exact_action: Pull the jacketed part of the cable out of the grommet, then feed all the M8 connectors through the grommet one at a time.

steps.title: Open the snap-open cable carrier cross bars
steps.instruction: Open all of the cross bars on the outside of the cable carrier (snap-open type).
steps.purpose: Allow the cable to be removed from the cable carrier.
steps.expected_result: All cable carrier cross bars are opened (carrier is unlatched for cable removal).
steps.healthy_condition: Carrier cross bars are fully opened so the cable can be lifted/removed.
steps.failure_condition: Cross bars are not fully opened, preventing cable removal.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if the cable cannot be pulled free after opening the cable carrier cross bars.

actions.label: Snap-open carrier cross bars
actions.exact_action: Open all of the cross bars on the cable carrier.

steps.title: Mark the cable on both ends where it enters the cable carrier
steps.instruction: Use tape or a marker to mark the cable on both ends where the cable enters the cable carrier.
steps.purpose: Preserve cable orientation/positioning for later reinstallation (or transfer to the new cable).
steps.expected_result: Two cable entry marks are applied (one at each end where the cable enters the cable carrier).
steps.healthy_condition: Marks are visible and correspond to the cable entry points into the carrier.
steps.failure_condition: Marks are missing, unclear, or not placed at the cable entry points.

actions.label: Apply tape/marker marks
actions.exact_action: Use tape or a marker to mark the cable on both ends where the cable enters the cable carrier.

steps.title: Cut cable ties at both carrier ends and the A-axis carriage tie point
steps.instruction: Note how the cable ties are situated at both ends of the carrier (take a picture) and cut the cable ties holding the cable to the cable carrier at both ends and the tie point on the A-axis carriage.
steps.purpose: Free the cable from the carrier and carriage tie-down points so it can be unplugged from the A-axis PCA.
steps.expected_result: Cable ties at both carrier ends and the A-axis carriage tie point are cut, freeing the cable from those restraints.
steps.healthy_condition: No cable ties remain holding the cable at the carrier ends or the A-axis carriage tie point.
steps.failure_condition: A cable tie remains uncut at either carrier end or the A-axis carriage tie point.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if the cable is still attached by an uncut cable tie near the A-axis PCA (the procedure notes there may be one more cable tie to cut near the PCA).

actions.label: Cut cable ties
actions.exact_action: cut the cable ties holding the cable to the cable carrier at both ends and the tie point on the A-axis carriage.

steps.title: Unplug from the A-axis PCA and remove from the cable carrier
steps.instruction: Unplug the cable from the A-axis PCA and remove it from the cable carrier. There may be one more cable tie to cut near the PCA.
steps.purpose: Complete removal by disconnecting the cable from the A-axis PCA and extracting it from the carrier.
steps.expected_result: Cable is unplugged from the A-axis PCA and removed from the cable carrier.
steps.healthy_condition: No cable remains connected to the A-axis PCA; cable is fully extracted from the carrier.
steps.failure_condition: Cable remains attached near the PCA due to an uncut tie or incomplete unplugging.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check if the cable is still attached by an uncut cable tie near the A-axis PCA (the procedure notes there may be one more cable tie to cut near the PCA).

actions.label: Unplug from A-axis PCA
actions.exact_action: Unplug the cable from the A-axis PCA and remove it from the cable carrier.

steps.title: Transfer the markings to the new cable
steps.instruction: Transfer the markings from Step 5 to the new cable.
steps.purpose: Preserve the cable entry/orientation reference for correct reinstallation on the replacement cable.
steps.expected_result: Marks from the original cable are applied to the new cable at the corresponding entry points.
steps.healthy_condition: New cable has the same tape/marker markings at both ends where it enters the cable carrier.
steps.failure_condition: Markings are missing or not transferred to the new cable.

actions.label: Transfer markings
actions.exact_action: Transfer the markings from Step 5 to the new cable.

title: Apply Power to Tipper Station (Electrical Panel Power Switch)
summary: Turn on electrical power to the tipper station by moving the electrical panel power switch to the "On" position as the first step of tipper commissioning.
when_to_use: Use as the first step when starting tipper commissioning to energize the tipper station before subsequent commissioning steps.

steps.title: Locate the electrical panel power switch at the tipper station
steps.instruction: Go to the tipper station electrical panel and locate the power switch.
steps.purpose: Identify the correct electrical panel switch used to energize the tipper station for commissioning.
steps.expected_result: You have identified the electrical panel power switch that will be moved to the "On" position.
steps.healthy_condition: The correct power switch is found and is ready to be moved to the "On" position.
steps.failure_condition: The power switch cannot be located or cannot be moved to the "On" position.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the power switch cannot be moved to "On".

actions.label: Find panel power switch
actions.exact_action: Go to the tipper station electrical panel and locate the power switch.

steps.title: Turn the electrical panel power switch to "On"
steps.instruction: Turn the power switch to the "On" position.
steps.purpose: Energize the tipper station so commissioning can proceed.
steps.expected_result: The electrical panel power switch is in the "On" position and the station is powered for subsequent commissioning steps.
steps.healthy_condition: The power switch is visibly set to the "On" position.
steps.failure_condition: The power switch cannot be moved to "On" or the panel indicates an abnormal condition that prevents commissioning from proceeding (e.g., no power indication/visible fault).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the power switch cannot be moved to "On".
Stop and escalate if the panel indicates an abnormal condition (e.g., no power indication/visible fault) that prevents commissioning from proceeding.

actions.label: Set switch to On
actions.exact_action: Turn the power switch to the "On" position.

title: Set Tipper Controller Parameters on Operator Station HMI (Visu_MDs F2)
summary: Use the operator station HMI to open the “Visu_MDs” screen (F2) and set the initial controller parameters for each tipper axis. Maintenance or admin login is required to change the settings.
when_to_use: When a tipper component has been replaced and the tipper needs to be re-commissioned by setting the initial controller parameters for each tipper axis.

steps.title: Navigate to the Visu_MDs screen (F2) on the operator station HMI
steps.instruction: On the operator station HMI, navigate to the “Visu_MDs” screen using F2.
steps.purpose: Open the correct HMI screen used to set initial controller parameters for each tipper axis.
steps.expected_result: The “Visu_MDs” screen is open on the operator station HMI.
steps.healthy_condition: The “Visu_MDs” screen is accessible and displayed (not blocked/absent).
steps.failure_condition: The “Visu_MDs” screen cannot be accessed (screen does not open) or the navigation does not reach the “Visu_MDs” screen.
stop_or_escalate_if: Visu_MDs screen cannot be accessed

actions.label: Open Visu_MDs (F2)
actions.exact_action: navigate to the "Visu_MDs" screen (F2)

steps.title: Confirm maintenance or admin login before changing settings
steps.instruction: Confirm you are logged in as maintenance or admin (required to be able to change the settings).
steps.purpose: Ensure the HMI allows parameter edits; the manual states maintenance/admin login is required to change settings.
steps.expected_result: The current login level is maintenance or admin, enabling the controller parameter fields/settings to be changed.
steps.healthy_condition: Controller parameter settings on the Visu_MDs screen are editable after login.
steps.failure_condition: Settings are missing/locked such that initial controller parameters cannot be changed.
stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot edit the settings
Axis parameter fields are missing/locked in a way that prevents setting initial parameters

actions.label: Verify login level
actions.exact_action: You must be logged in as maintenance or admin to be able to change the settings.

steps.title: Set initial controller parameters for each tipper axis on Visu_MDs
steps.instruction: On the Visu_MDs screen, set the initial parameters for each axis of the tippers.
steps.purpose: Complete the commissioning step by updating the initial controller parameters for each tipper axis.
steps.expected_result: The initial controller parameters for each tipper axis are updated on the Visu_MDs screen (i.e., the settings were editable and changes were applied).
steps.healthy_condition: After editing, the Visu_MDs screen reflects updated initial parameter values for each axis.
steps.failure_condition: Edits do not apply (values do not change) or axis parameter fields are not available/editable.
stop_or_escalate_if: Axis parameter fields are missing/locked in a way that prevents setting initial parameters

actions.label: Edit axis controller parameters
