actions.exact_action: Set the initial parameters for each axis of the tippers.

title: Perform Daily Maintenance Checklist for Tipper (Operator Station, Chute, Stacklights, Guards, QR Codes)
summary: Complete the daily inspection items for the OptiSweep tipper system to confirm key operator-station and physical components are in acceptable condition.
when_to_use: Use this daily checklist procedure to perform routine operator-station and physical inspections of the tipper system components: Operator Station controller, Operator Station chute, stacklights, guards/attaching hardware, and QR codes on the floor and racks.

steps.title: Record inspection metadata on the Daily Maintenance Checklist form
steps.instruction: On the Daily Maintenance Checklist form, record the Inspection Date, Inspected By, and Unit Inspected.
steps.purpose: Ensure the inspection is traceable and tied to the correct unit and inspector.
steps.expected_result: The form has entries for Inspection Date, Inspected By, and Unit Inspected.
steps.healthy_condition: All three fields are completed (no blanks).
steps.failure_condition: Any of the three fields are missing or incomplete.

actions.label: Fill checklist header fields
actions.exact_action: Record Inspection Date, Inspected By, and Unit Inspected on the Daily Maintenance Checklist form.

steps.title: Inspect the Operator Station controller for damage
steps.instruction: Visually inspect the Operator Station controller for damage.
steps.purpose: Detect physical damage to the controller referenced by the daily checklist.
steps.expected_result: You can mark the checklist item as passing because no damage is found on the Operator Station controller.
steps.healthy_condition: No visible damage is present on the Operator Station controller.
steps.failure_condition: Damage is found on the Operator Station controller.
stop_or_escalate_if: If controller damage is found, stop the checklist and escalate per site maintenance process.

actions.label: Check controller condition
actions.exact_action: Inspect the Operator Station controller for damage.

steps.title: Ensure the Operator Station chute is free of debris
steps.instruction: Inspect the Operator Station chute and ensure it is free of debris.
steps.purpose: Confirm the chute is clear so operation is not impeded by debris.
steps.expected_result: You can mark the checklist item as passing because no debris is present in the Operator Station chute.
steps.healthy_condition: The Operator Station chute is clear of debris.
steps.failure_condition: Debris is present in the Operator Station chute.
stop_or_escalate_if: If debris is found, stop the checklist and escalate per site maintenance process.

actions.label: Check chute cleanliness
actions.exact_action: Ensure Operator Station chute is free of debris.

steps.title: Verify stacklights are operational
steps.instruction: Verify the stacklights are operational.
steps.purpose: Confirm stacklights function as expected for operator signaling.
steps.expected_result: You can mark the checklist item as passing because the stacklights are operational.
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklights are operational (functional as observed during the inspection).
steps.failure_condition: Stacklights are not operational.
stop_or_escalate_if: If stacklights are non-operational, stop the checklist and escalate per site maintenance process.

actions.label: Check stacklight operation
actions.exact_action: Verify stacklights are operational.

steps.title: Inspect guards and verify attaching hardware is secure
steps.instruction: Inspect the guards and verify attaching hardware is secure.
steps.purpose: Ensure guards are secure and attaching hardware is not loose.
steps.expected_result: You can mark the checklist item as passing because guards are secure and attaching hardware is secure.
steps.healthy_condition: Guards are secure and attaching hardware is secure.
steps.failure_condition: Guards are loose or attaching hardware is not secure.
stop_or_escalate_if: If guards are loose/unsafe or attaching hardware is not secure, stop the checklist and escalate per site maintenance process.

actions.label: Check guard security
actions.exact_action: Inspect the guards and verify attaching hardware is secure.

steps.title: Inspect all QR codes on the floor for damage or peeling
steps.instruction: Inspect all QR codes on the floor for damage or peeling.
steps.purpose: Ensure floor QR codes are readable and intact.
steps.expected_result: You can mark the checklist item as passing because all floor QR codes show no damage or peeling.
steps.healthy_condition: All floor QR codes show no damage or peeling.
steps.failure_condition: Any floor QR code shows damage or peeling.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any floor QR code is damaged or peeling, stop the checklist and escalate per site maintenance process.

actions.label: Check floor QR codes
actions.exact_action: Inspect all QR codes on the floor for damage or peeling.

steps.title: Inspect all QR codes on the racks for damage or peeling
steps.instruction: Inspect all QR codes on the racks for damage or peeling.
steps.purpose: Ensure rack QR codes are readable and intact.
steps.expected_result: You can mark the checklist item as passing because all rack QR codes show no damage or peeling.
steps.healthy_condition: All rack QR codes show no damage or peeling.
steps.failure_condition: Any rack QR code shows damage or peeling.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any rack QR code is damaged or peeling, stop the checklist and escalate per site maintenance process.

actions.label: Check rack QR codes
actions.exact_action: Inspect all QR codes on the racks for damage or peeling.

title: Replace an OptiSweep Operator Station Tipper (LOTO, disconnect power/Ethernet/air, remove and reinstall)
summary: Safely replace a failed/replaced OptiSweep operator station tipper by performing LOTO, disconnecting the tipper’s power (6-pin Molex), Ethernet (ClearLink controller), and air line (quick disconnect), removing the old tipper from the sub-plate, installing the new tipper onto the existing sub-plate, reconnecting conduit/power/air/Ethernet, and restarting the operator station.
when_to_use: Use when an OptiSweep operator station tipper must be removed and replaced, requiring LOTO and physical disconnection/reconnection of the tipper’s power (6-pin Molex), Ethernet (ClearLink controller), and air line (quick disconnect), followed by reinstall and operator station restart.

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the tipper
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the method referenced as "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout".
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely locked out before any disconnection of power, Ethernet, or air.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is in a locked-out state prior to disconnecting the control box and tipper connections.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed and verified before proceeding to disconnect power (6-pin Molex), Ethernet, and air line.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to disconnect power/air/Ethernet without completing LOTO.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot complete LOTO for the tipper before disconnecting power/air/Ethernet.

actions.label: Apply LOTO to tipper
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel (if necessary) to access the motor
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor/control box area for disconnecting power and Ethernet and for removing the tipper.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (when needed) and the motor area is accessible.
steps.healthy_condition: Nine (9) self-tapping securing screws are removed and the side panel is removed without damaging fasteners or surrounding components.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel cannot be removed due to inability to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.

actions.label: Check if side panel removal is needed
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Disconnect tipper power (6-pin Molex) at the control box and route cable into the column
steps.instruction: Remove the control box and disconnect the power cable from the tipper (6-pin Molex connector), then push the cable into the column.
steps.purpose: Remove electrical power connection to the tipper safely before further disassembly.
steps.expected_result: 6-pin Molex power cable is disconnected from the tipper and the cable is pushed into the column.
steps.healthy_condition: Power cable is fully unplugged from the tipper’s 6-pin Molex connector and is routed into the column (not left hanging at the tipper).
steps.failure_condition: Power cable cannot be disconnected from the 6-pin Molex connector or cannot be routed into the column.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot complete LOTO for the tipper before disconnecting power/air/Ethernet.

actions.label: Disconnect 6-pin Molex power
actions.exact_action: Remove the control box and disconnect the power cable from the tipper (6-pin Molex connector), then push the cable into the column.

steps.title: Unplug Ethernet from the ClearLink controller and route into the column
steps.instruction: Unplug the Ethernet cable from the ClearLink controller and push the Ethernet cable into the column.
steps.purpose: Remove network connection to the tipper safely before removing the tipper from the sub-plate.
steps.expected_result: Ethernet cable is unplugged from the ClearLink controller and routed into the column.
steps.healthy_condition: Ethernet connector is fully unplugged and cable is routed into the column (not left connected to the tipper).
steps.failure_condition: Ethernet cable cannot be unplugged from the ClearLink controller or cannot be routed into the column.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if you cannot complete LOTO for the tipper before disconnecting power/air/Ethernet.

actions.label: Unplug Ethernet from ClearLink controller
actions.exact_action: Unplug the Ethernet cable from the ClearLink controller and push the Ethernet cable into the column.

steps.title: Disconnect air line at the quick disconnect (leave quick disconnect on tipper side)
steps.instruction: Disconnect the air line at the quick disconnect at the bottom of the column, leaving the quick disconnect with the tipper side of the air line.
steps.purpose: Safely disconnect pneumatic supply to the tipper while preserving the specified quick disconnect side for reassembly.
steps.expected_result: Air line is disconnected at the quick disconnect, with the quick disconnect remaining on the tipper side of the air line.
steps.healthy_condition: Quick disconnect is left on the tipper side as specified; air line is separated without damage to fittings.
steps.failure_condition: Quick disconnect cannot be left on the tipper side as specified.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the air line quick disconnect cannot be left on the tipper side as specified.

actions.label: Disconnect air line at quick disconnect
actions.exact_action: Disconnect the air line at the quick disconnect at the bottom of the column, leaving the quick disconnect with the Tipper side of the air line.

steps.title: Tape air line and quick disconnect to prevent debris entry
steps.instruction: Add tape over the air line and quick disconnect to prevent debris from entering either side of the air line.
steps.purpose: Prevent debris from entering either side of the air line during disconnection.
steps.expected_result: Tape is applied over the air line and quick disconnect on both sides to block debris entry.
steps.healthy_condition: Both exposed air-line/quick-disconnect openings are covered with tape.
steps.failure_condition: Debris protection (tape) cannot be applied to both sides.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the air line quick disconnect cannot be left on the tipper side as specified or if debris protection (tape) cannot be applied to both sides.

actions.label: Apply tape for debris protection
actions.exact_action: Add tape over the air line and quick disconnect to prevent debris from entering either side of the air line.

steps.title: Fully disconnect conduit bringing power, air, and Ethernet to the column and free cables from the tipper
steps.instruction: Fully disconnect the conduit bringing power, air, and Ethernet to the column and pull these cables free from the tipper.
steps.purpose: Remove all remaining connections so the tipper can be lifted off the sub-plate.
steps.expected_result: Conduit is disconnected and power/air/Ethernet cables are free from the tipper.
steps.healthy_condition: No remaining electrical or pneumatic connections hold the tipper to the column/conduit.
steps.failure_condition: Cables/conduit cannot be fully disconnected or remain attached to the tipper.

actions.label: Disconnect conduit and free cables
actions.exact_action: Fully disconnect the conduit bringing power, air, and Ethernet to the column and pull these cables free from the Tipper.

steps.title: Optional: remove gripper and counter-balance weights
steps.instruction: Optional but recommended: remove the gripper (see "Gripper Replacement" on page 97) and the counter-balance weights (see "Counter-balance weights" on page 95).
steps.purpose: Reduce mechanical complexity/imbalance during tipper removal (optional but recommended).
steps.expected_result: Gripper and counter-balance weights are removed if you choose to follow the optional recommendation.
steps.healthy_condition: Mechanical components are removed without leaving the system in an unsafe or unstable state for the subsequent tipper removal.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot remove the gripper and/or counter-balance weights as needed to proceed safely.

actions.label: Remove gripper and counter-balance weights (optional)
actions.exact_action: Optional but recommended: Remove the gripper (see "Gripper Replacement" on page 97) and the counter-balance weights (see "Counter-balance weights" on page 95).

steps.title: Remove the old tipper from the sub-plate
steps.instruction: With the tipper supported, remove the four (4) hex head screws holding the tipper to the sub-plate.
steps.purpose: Detach the failed/old tipper from the sub-plate so the new tipper can be installed.
steps.expected_result: Four (4) hex head screws are removed and the old tipper is free from the sub-plate.
steps.healthy_condition: Tipper remains properly supported while screws are removed; tipper can be lifted off without binding.
steps.failure_condition: Four hex head screws cannot be removed/installed while the tipper is properly supported.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the four hex head screws cannot be removed/installed while the tipper is properly supported.

actions.label: Remove tipper mounting screws
actions.exact_action: With the tipper supported, remove the four (4) hex head screws holding the tipper to the sub-plate.

steps.title: Install the new tipper onto the existing sub-plate
steps.instruction: Install the new tipper onto the existing sub-plate.
steps.purpose: Reinstall the replacement tipper on the same sub-plate mounting interface.
steps.expected_result: New tipper is positioned on the existing sub-plate mounting interface.
steps.healthy_condition: Tipper sits correctly on the sub-plate such that mounting screws can be installed.
steps.failure_condition: New tipper cannot be installed onto the sub-plate or mounting screws cannot be installed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the four hex head screws cannot be removed/installed while the tipper is properly supported.

actions.label: Mount new tipper
actions.exact_action: Install the new tipper onto the existing sub-plate.

steps.title: Reconnect conduit, power, air, and Ethernet to the column and control box
steps.instruction: Connect the conduit, power, air, and Ethernet to the column and control box.
steps.purpose: Restore electrical, network, and pneumatic connections required for tipper operation.
steps.expected_result: Conduit/power/air/Ethernet are reconnected to the column and control box.
steps.healthy_condition: All reconnections are made to the specified interfaces (column and control box) so the station can be restarted.
steps.failure_condition: Any required reconnection cannot be completed (power/air/Ethernet/conduit).

actions.label: Reconnect conduit/power/air/Ethernet
actions.exact_action: Connect the conduit, power, air, and Ethernet to the column and control Box.

steps.title: Mount the gripper if necessary
steps.instruction: Mount the gripper, if necessary (see "Gripper Replacement" on page 97).
steps.purpose: Restore the end effector/gripper assembly if it was removed.
steps.expected_result: Gripper is mounted if it was removed.
steps.healthy_condition: Gripper is installed and secured per the referenced gripper replacement procedure.
steps.failure_condition: Gripper cannot be mounted/secured as required.

actions.label: Mount gripper (if necessary)
actions.exact_action: Mount the gripper, if necessary (see "Gripper Replacement" on page 97).

steps.title: Reinstall top and/or bottom side panels if necessary
steps.instruction: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.
steps.purpose: Restore station guarding/side panels after access work.
steps.expected_result: Side panels are reinstalled if they were removed.
steps.healthy_condition: Panels are reinstalled and secured (no open access to internal components).
steps.failure_condition: Panels cannot be reinstalled or remain unsecured.

actions.label: Reinstall side panels
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.

steps.title: Re-start the operator station
steps.instruction: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 1).
steps.purpose: Bring the operator station back online after reconnection and reassembly.
steps.expected_result: Operator station is restarted after the tipper replacement and reconnections.
steps.healthy_condition: Station restart completes and the station is ready for normal operation/commissioning steps as applicable.
steps.failure_condition: Operator station cannot be restarted or does not come back online after replacement.

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 1).

title: Inspect and Lubricate Tipper Z-Axis Linear Bearings (Grease Wetness on Z-Axis Linear Rails)
summary: Preventive maintenance for an OptiSweep tipper: visually inspect the Z-axis linear rails for grease wetness or dried grease. If the rails are dry, lubricate the bearing blocks through the grease nipples using automotive bearing grease, applying 1.0 to 3.0 cc per bearing block. Do not rely on wiping grease on the rails as a substitute for lubrication.
when_to_use: Use during tipper preventive maintenance to check Z-axis linear rail lubrication condition (wet grease vs dried grease) and to apply grease to the Z-axis bearing blocks when the rails are dry.

steps.title: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for grease wetness or dried grease
steps.instruction: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails and look for wet grease and/or signs of dried grease.
steps.purpose: Determine whether lubrication is present (wet grease) or absent (dry/dried grease) to decide whether lubrication is required.
steps.expected_result: You can classify the condition of the Z-axis linear rails as either wet with grease or dry (not wet with grease) / showing dried grease.
steps.healthy_condition: Rails show grease wetness and/or signs of dried grease (indicating grease presence).
steps.failure_condition: Rails are dry (not wet with grease), indicating lubrication is needed.

actions.label: Inspect Z-axis rails
actions.exact_action: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease and/or signs of dried grease.

steps.title: If rails are dry, lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease
steps.instruction: If the rails are dry (not wet with grease), lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).
steps.purpose: Restore lubrication to the Z-axis bearing blocks when the rails are dry.
steps.expected_result: Grease is applied to the bearing blocks via the grease nipples using the specified quantity per block (1.0 to 3.0 cc per block).
steps.healthy_condition: Grease is applied to each bearing block through its grease nipples with 1.0 to 3.0 cc per block.
steps.failure_condition: Grease is not applied to the bearing blocks (or lubrication is attempted by wiping rails instead of greasing the bearing blocks).
stop_or_escalate_if: If rails show signs of dried grease but lubrication cannot be performed as specified (e.g., inability to access nipples), stop and escalate to maintenance support.

actions.label: Lubricate bearing blocks
actions.exact_action: If the rails are dry (not wet with grease) then lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).

steps.title: Locate the grease nipples on the two bearing blocks
steps.instruction: Locate the grease nipples: there are two (2) bearing blocks, each with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end (four (4) nipples total).
steps.purpose: Ensure grease is applied to the correct lubrication points (the bearing blocks via the nipples).
steps.expected_result: You identify four (4) grease nipples total: two bearing blocks, one 1/4-in nipple on each end of each block.
steps.healthy_condition: All four nipples are located and accessible for greasing the bearing blocks.
steps.failure_condition: Nipples cannot be located or accessed, preventing lubrication as specified.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access the nipples to apply grease to the bearing blocks, stop and escalate to maintenance support.

actions.label: Find grease nipples
actions.exact_action: Locate the grease nipples: there are two (2) bearing blocks, each with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end (four (4) nipples total).

steps.title: Apply 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each bearing block
steps.instruction: Using a grease applicator, add 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each bearing block (via its grease nipples).
steps.purpose: Apply the specified grease quantity to ensure adequate lubrication of each bearing block.
steps.expected_result: Total grease applied per bearing block is within 1.0 to 3.0 cc, and grease has been delivered through the bearing block nipples.
steps.healthy_condition: Each bearing block receives 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease (four nipples total used to deliver grease to the two blocks).
steps.failure_condition: Grease quantity per block is outside 1.0 to 3.0 cc, or grease is not delivered to the bearing blocks through the nipples.

actions.label: Grease bearing blocks
actions.exact_action: Adding 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each block should be adequate.

steps.title: Do not substitute wiping grease on the rails for lubrication
steps.instruction: Do not rely on wiping grease on the rails as a substitute for lubrication.
steps.purpose: Ensure lubrication is performed correctly at the bearing blocks rather than only cosmetically on the rails.
steps.expected_result: Lubrication is performed by greasing the bearing blocks via the grease nipples (not by wiping rails).
steps.healthy_condition: Grease is applied to bearing blocks through nipples; rail wiping is not used as the lubrication method.
steps.failure_condition: Only wiping grease on the rails is performed without greasing the bearing blocks via nipples.

actions.label: Confirm correct lubrication method
actions.exact_action: Wiping grease on the rails is not adequate.

title: Replace and Install Tote Detect Sensor (M3 screws + M8 connector) and Restart Operator Station
summary: Remove and replace the tote detect sensor by disconnecting the M8 connector and M3 socket-head screw, routing the replacement sensor through the frame (using the M8 connector/tape method), reinstalling grommets, mounting with M3 socket-head screws, reconnecting the M8 connector, and restarting the operator station so the sensor is ready for tote detection.
when_to_use: Use when a tote detect sensor must be replaced and reinstalled with the correct M3 socket-head screws and M8 connector, including routing through the frame and reinstalling grommets, followed by restarting the operator station.

steps.title: Perform LOTO on the tipper
steps.instruction: Apply LOTO to the tipper using the manual procedure referenced as "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout".
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely locked out before disconnecting and removing the tote detect sensor.
steps.expected_result: Tipper is under LOTO prior to disconnecting the M8 connector and M3 socket-head screw.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is in place before any sensor disconnection/removal actions are performed.
steps.failure_condition: Attempting to disconnect/remove the sensor without LOTO applied.
stop_or_escalate_if: If LOTO cannot be applied/verified, stop and do not proceed with sensor disconnection/removal.

actions.label: Apply tipper LOTO
actions.exact_action: Perform LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Disconnect the M8 connector and M3 socket-head screw from the tote detect sensor
steps.instruction: Disconnect the M8 connector and the M3 socket-head screw from the tote detect sensor.
steps.purpose: Free the tote detect sensor for removal by disconnecting its electrical connector and mechanical fastener.
steps.expected_result: M8 connector is disconnected and the M3 socket-head screw is removed/loosened such that the sensor can be pulled out.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor is mechanically and electrically disconnected (M8 connector disconnected; M3 socket-head screw disconnected).
steps.failure_condition: Sensor cannot be pulled out because the M8 connector or M3 socket-head screw is still connected/secured.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the sensor cannot be disconnected cleanly, stop and re-check wiring/routing before continuing.

actions.label: Disconnect M8 connector
actions.exact_action: Disconnect the M8 connector ... from the tote detect sensor.

actions.label: Disconnect M3 socket-head screw
actions.exact_action: Disconnect the ... M3 socket-head screw ... from the tote detect sensor.

steps.title: Pull the sensor out
steps.instruction: Pull the tote detect sensor out after disconnecting the M8 connector and M3 socket-head screw.
steps.purpose: Remove the old tote detect sensor from the frame for replacement.
steps.expected_result: Old tote detect sensor is removed from the frame.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor is fully removed with no remaining mechanical/electrical attachment.
steps.failure_condition: Sensor resists removal due to remaining attachment or routing obstruction.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the sensor cannot be pulled out, stop and re-check that the M8 connector and M3 socket-head screw are fully disconnected.

actions.label: Remove sensor
actions.exact_action: Pull the sensor out.

steps.title: Route the replacement sensor through the frame using the M8 connector/tape method
steps.instruction: Route the replacement sensor through the frame by taping the replacement sensor to the M8 connector so the old sensor can be used to route the new sensor through the frame.
steps.purpose: Ensure the replacement sensor wire is routed correctly through the frame to reach the M8 connector location.
steps.expected_result: Replacement sensor is routed through the frame to the correct termination point for the M8 connector.
steps.healthy_condition: Replacement sensor wire reaches the M8 connector area without being pinched or misrouted.
steps.failure_condition: Replacement sensor cannot be routed to the termination point or routing is incorrect such that the sensor cannot be mounted/connected.
stop_or_escalate_if: If routing is difficult or incorrect, stop and use the grommet-removal approach in the next step.

actions.label: Tape replacement sensor to M8 connector
actions.exact_action: Tape the replacement sensor to the M8 connector so the old sensor can be used to route the new sensor through the frame.

steps.title: If routing is difficult, pull grommets from the frame and re-install later
steps.instruction: If routing is difficult, pull the grommets from the frame to make routing easier, then re-install them later.
steps.purpose: Provide additional access to route the sensor wire when the frame routing is difficult.
steps.expected_result: Sensor routing is completed successfully; grommets are available to be re-installed after routing.
steps.healthy_condition: Grommets are removed only as needed to enable routing and are ready to be reinstalled after the sensor is routed.
steps.failure_condition: Grommets are not reinstalled later or routing is completed with grommets missing.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot route the sensor even after pulling grommets, stop and re-check wiring/routing before proceeding to mounting.

actions.label: Assess routing difficulty
actions.exact_action: If routing is difficult, pull the grommets from the frame to make routing easier, then re-install them later.

steps.title: Mount the sensor using the M3 socket-head screws
steps.instruction: Mount the replacement sensor using the M3 socket-head screws.
steps.purpose: Secure the replacement tote detect sensor mechanically to the correct mounting location.
steps.expected_result: Sensor is physically mounted using the M3 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Sensor is securely mounted with M3 socket-head screws (no looseness).
steps.failure_condition: Sensor cannot be mounted securely with the M3 socket-head screws.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check wiring/routing if the sensor cannot be mounted securely with the M3 socket-head screws.

actions.label: Install M3 screws
actions.exact_action: Mount the sensor using the M3 socket-head screws.

steps.title: Connect the M8 connector
steps.instruction: Connect the M8 connector to the tote detect sensor.
steps.purpose: Restore electrical connection for the tote detect sensor.
steps.expected_result: M8 connector is connected to the tote detect sensor.
steps.healthy_condition: M8 connector is fully seated/connected (no loose connection).
steps.failure_condition: M8 connector cannot be connected or remains loose.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the M8 connector cannot be connected, stop and re-check wiring/routing before proceeding.

actions.label: Connect M8
actions.exact_action: Connect the M8 connector.

steps.title: Seat the small grommet around the wire back into the valve cover slot
steps.instruction: Put the small grommet around the wire back into the slot in the valve cover.
steps.purpose: Restore wire strain relief and sealing by correctly seating the grommet in the valve cover.
steps.expected_result: Small grommet is seated in the valve cover slot with the wire passing through it.
steps.healthy_condition: Grommet is seated in the valve cover slot (wire is properly supported).
steps.failure_condition: Grommet cannot be seated back into the valve cover slot.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check wiring/routing if the grommet cannot be seated back into the valve cover slot.

actions.label: Re-seat small grommet
actions.exact_action: Put the small grommet around the wire back into the slot in the valve cover.

steps.title: Re-install any removed grommets
steps.instruction: Re-install any removed grommets.
steps.purpose: Ensure all grommets removed to aid routing are restored to maintain proper wire management.
steps.expected_result: All grommets that were removed for routing are re-installed.
steps.healthy_condition: No grommets remain missing from the frame where they were removed.
steps.failure_condition: Any removed grommets are left uninstalled.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any grommets cannot be reinstalled, stop and re-check routing before restarting the operator station.

actions.label: Re-install grommets
actions.exact_action: Re-install any removed grommets.

steps.title: Re-start the operator station
steps.instruction: Re-start the operator station using the manual procedure "Starting The Operator Station".
steps.purpose: Bring the operator station back online after sensor replacement so the tote detect sensor is ready for detection.
steps.expected_result: Operator station is restarted after the sensor is installed and connected.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator station restart completes successfully using the documented restart procedure.
steps.failure_condition: Operator station cannot be restarted using the documented "Starting The Operator Station" procedure.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the operator station cannot be restarted using the documented "Starting The Operator Station" procedure.

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

title: Replace Tote Detect Sensor (LOTO tipper, disconnect M8, remove and remount sensor)
summary: Safely lock out the OptiSweep tipper, remove the Tote Detect sensor by disconnecting the M8 connector and M3 socket-head screw, pull the sensor out, mount the replacement sensor using the M3 socket-head screws, and restart the operator station.
when_to_use: Use when the Tote Detect sensor must be physically removed and replaced on the OptiSweep tipper (sensor replacement task).

steps.title: Identify the Tote Detect sensor location
steps.instruction: Use the manual’s “Sensors” section to identify the Tote sensor locations, then locate the Tote Detect sensor on the tipper/frame.
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct sensor is accessed for removal and replacement.
steps.expected_result: You have identified the correct Tote Detect sensor location on the tipper for the subsequent M8 disconnect and M3 screw removal.
steps.healthy_condition: The sensor you are about to service matches the Tote sensor location referenced by the manual’s “Sensors” section.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confidently match the sensor location to the manual’s Tote sensor locations (risk of disconnecting/removing the wrong component).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if you cannot identify the correct Tote Detect sensor location without guessing.

actions.label: Locate Tote Detect sensor
actions.exact_action: Identify the Tote Detect sensor location using the manual’s “Sensors” section (sensor locations referenced by this section).

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO of the tipper using the manual’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” procedure (page 2).
steps.purpose: Prevent hazardous motion/energy while disconnecting and removing the sensor.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is in a locked out/tagged out state before any sensor disconnection/removal.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed per the manual’s Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure before proceeding.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to disconnect the M8 connector or remove the M3 screw without completing LOTO.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if LOTO cannot be completed before proceeding.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” on page 2).

steps.title: Disconnect the M8 connector and M3 socket-head screw
steps.instruction: Disconnect the M8 connector and remove the M3 socket-head screw securing the Tote Detect sensor.
steps.purpose: Free the Tote Detect sensor from electrical connection and mechanical mounting.
steps.expected_result: The M8 connector is disconnected and the M3 socket-head screw is removed, allowing the sensor to be pulled out.
steps.healthy_condition: The sensor is no longer electrically connected (M8 disconnected) and is no longer mechanically secured by the M3 socket-head screw.
steps.failure_condition: The M8 connector or M3 screw cannot be disconnected/removed without forcing (risk of damage).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the sensor cannot be disconnected/reinstalled without forcing connectors or screws (risk of damage).

actions.label: Disconnect M8 and remove M3 screw
actions.exact_action: Disconnect the M8 connector and M3 socket-head screw.

steps.title: Pull the sensor out
steps.instruction: Pull the Tote Detect sensor out of the frame/mount.
steps.purpose: Remove the sensor from the frame/mount after disconnection.
steps.expected_result: The Tote Detect sensor is removed from the frame/mount.
steps.healthy_condition: The sensor comes out without damage to the sensor body or surrounding grommets/cable routing.
steps.failure_condition: The sensor cannot be pulled out without forcing or appears stuck due to routing/grommets.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if pulling requires forcing that could damage the sensor or wiring.

actions.label: Pull sensor out
actions.exact_action: Pull the sensor out.

steps.title: Mount the replacement sensor with the M3 socket-head screws
steps.instruction: Mount the replacement Tote Detect sensor using the M3 socket-head screws.
steps.purpose: Re-secure the replacement sensor mechanically and prepare for reconnection and restart.
steps.expected_result: The replacement sensor is mounted and secured with the M3 socket-head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: The replacement sensor is firmly mounted using the M3 socket-head screws (no loose mounting).
steps.failure_condition: The sensor cannot be mounted securely with the M3 socket-head screws without forcing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the sensor cannot be mounted without forcing connectors/screws (risk of damage).

actions.label: Mount replacement sensor
actions.exact_action: Mount the sensor with the M3 socket-head screws.

steps.title: Restart the operator station
steps.instruction: Restart the operator station using the manual’s “Starting The Operator Station” procedure (page 66).
steps.purpose: Bring the station back online after sensor replacement.
steps.expected_result: The operator station is restarted after the sensor replacement.
steps.healthy_condition: The operator station startup sequence completes successfully per the manual’s Starting The Operator Station procedure.
steps.failure_condition: The operator station cannot be restarted after installation.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the operator station cannot be restarted after installation, stop and escalate to the appropriate support procedure for operator station startup.

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).

title: Recover From AGV Motionless on Floor Fault (Locate AGV, E-stop Zone, Remove, Reset)
summary: For an AGV that is motionless on the floor due to a fault, locate the faulted AGV (optionally using RMS for AGV error), stop the appropriate E-stop zone, remove the faulted AGV, pull E-STOP, and press the blue RESET button to resume operation.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV is motionless on the floor due to a fault and the system needs to be recovered so operation can resume.

steps.title: Locate the faulted AGV
steps.instruction: Locate the faulted AGV on the floor. If needed to identify the faulted AGV error, use the RMS / fleet status UI to determine which AGV is faulted.
steps.purpose: Identify which AGV is faulted and motionless so the correct E-stop zone can be stopped and the correct unit removed.
steps.expected_result: You have identified the specific faulted AGV that is motionless on the floor.
steps.healthy_condition: The faulted AGV is correctly identified (not a different AGV) so the correct E-stop zone can be stopped.
steps.failure_condition: The wrong AGV is identified (leading to stopping the wrong E-stop zone or removing the wrong unit).

actions.label: Identify faulted AGV
actions.exact_action: Locate the faulted AGV (may need to reference RMS for AGV error).

steps.title: Stop the appropriate E-stop zone
steps.instruction: Reference the E-stop zone map and press E-STOP to stop the appropriate E-stop zone for the faulted AGV.
steps.purpose: Stop motion in the correct zone to make the faulted AGV safe to remove and to prevent further system movement in that area.
steps.expected_result: The appropriate E-stop zone is stopped (E-STOP action applied to the correct zone).
steps.healthy_condition: E-STOP is applied to the correct zone corresponding to the faulted AGV location.
steps.failure_condition: E-STOP is applied to the wrong zone or the zone does not stop as intended.

actions.label: Stop E-stop zone
actions.exact_action: Reference E-stop zone map. Press E-STOP to stop the appropriate E-stop zone.

steps.title: Remove the faulted AGV
steps.instruction: Remove the faulted AGV from the floor/system area.
steps.purpose: Physically remove the faulted AGV from the system so it can be handled/recovered and the system can be reset.
steps.expected_result: The faulted AGV has been removed.
steps.healthy_condition: The faulted AGV is no longer present in the zone where it was motionless.
steps.failure_condition: The faulted AGV remains in place or cannot be safely removed.

actions.label: Remove AGV
actions.exact_action: Remove the faulted AGV.

steps.title: Pull E-STOP and press blue RESET
steps.instruction: Pull E-STOP, then press the blue RESET button.
steps.purpose: Clear the fault state and bring the system back to a state where operation can resume.
steps.expected_result: The blue RESET button is pressed after pulling E-STOP.
steps.healthy_condition: RESET is applied as the final recovery action in the sequence.
steps.failure_condition: RESET is not pressed (or is pressed without pulling E-STOP as required by the sequence).

actions.label: Pull E-STOP
actions.exact_action: Pull E-STOP.

actions.label: Press blue RESET
actions.exact_action: Press the blue RESET button.

steps.title: Verify the system resumes operation
steps.instruction: Observe the system after pressing blue RESET to confirm it resumes operation.
steps.purpose: Confirm recovery succeeded and the system is back in operation.
steps.expected_result: The system resumes operation.
steps.healthy_condition: Operation continues after RESET (system is no longer in the faulted motionless condition).
steps.failure_condition: The system does not resume operation after RESET.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the system does not resume operation after RESET, stop and escalate to a supervisor/support for further troubleshooting.

actions.label: Confirm resume
actions.exact_action: Observe that the system resumes operation.

title: Open CELLIO STATUS Sub-Screen From VISU_MANCONTROL to View Cell Control I/O Values
summary: From the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen VISU_MANCONTROL, use the CELLIO STATUS button to open the CELLIO STATUS sub-screen and view cell control input/output values per tipper for troubleshooting/verification.
when_to_use: Use when you need to verify cell control input/output values per tipper from the Operator Station HMI by opening the CELLIO STATUS sub-screen via VISU_MANCONTROL.

steps.title: Open the VISU_MANCONTROL maintenance manual control screen
steps.instruction: On the Operator Station HMI (VISU / WebVisu), open the maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.
steps.purpose: Get to the screen that contains the CELLIO STATUS navigation button.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen is displayed and includes the CELLIO STATUS button (Item 9).
steps.healthy_condition: VISU_MANCONTROL is visible with the CELLIO STATUS button present.
steps.failure_condition: VISU_MANCONTROL is not displayed, or the CELLIO STATUS button is not present/accessible.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot reach VISU_MANCONTROL or cannot locate the CELLIO STATUS button, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Navigate to VISU_MANCONTROL
actions.exact_action: Open the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.

steps.title: Press CELLIO STATUS to open the cell control I/O values screen per tipper
steps.instruction: On VISU_MANCONTROL, press the CELLIO STATUS button (Item 9).
steps.purpose: Open the CELLIO STATUS sub-screen that displays cell control input/output values per tipper.
steps.expected_result: The CELLIO STATUS sub-screen opens.
steps.healthy_condition: CELLIO STATUS screen opens successfully.
steps.failure_condition: The CELLIO STATUS screen does not open.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the CELLIO STATUS screen fails to open, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Open CELLIO STATUS sub-screen
actions.exact_action: Press the CELLIO STATUS button (Item 9) to open the cell control input/output values screen per tipper.

steps.title: Verify cell control input/output values are displayed for each tipper
steps.instruction: On the CELLIO STATUS screen, verify that cell control input and output values are displayed for each tipper.
steps.purpose: Confirm the CELLIO STATUS screen is populated with the expected cell control I/O values per tipper.
steps.expected_result: Cell control input and output values are displayed for each tipper on the CELLIO STATUS screen.
steps.healthy_condition: For each tipper, the CELLIO STATUS screen shows non-blank cell control input/output values.
steps.failure_condition: The CELLIO STATUS screen shows missing/blank input/output values for one or more tippers.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the expected input/output values are missing/blank, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Check displayed I/O values per tipper
actions.exact_action: On the CELLIO screen, verify that cell control input and output values are displayed for each tipper.

title: Reset a LEFT/RIGHT Tipper Fault From the VISU_MANCONTROL Screen
summary: On the Operator Station HMI VISU_MANCONTROL screen, use the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET button to clear the corresponding left or right tipper fault. Then verify the VISU_MANCONTROL informational banner/message area updates to reflect the reset (fault-related message cleared or replaced with a normal informational state).
when_to_use: Use when a LEFT or RIGHT tipper fault is indicated on the Operator Station HMI VISU_MANCONTROL screen and you need to reset the corresponding tipper fault using the screen’s manual control.

steps.title: Open the VISU_MANCONTROL manual control screen
steps.instruction: Open the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.
steps.purpose: Get to the Operator Station HMI screen that contains the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET buttons and the informational banner used to confirm the fault state.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen is displayed with the informational banner (alarms/informational messages) and the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET buttons visible.
steps.healthy_condition: The informational banner area is visible and the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET buttons are present on the screen.
steps.failure_condition: VISU_MANCONTROL does not load or the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET buttons and informational banner are not visible.

actions.label: Navigate to VISU_MANCONTROL
actions.exact_action: Open the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.

steps.title: Review the current banner message(s) for the active fault
steps.instruction: Use the informational banner arrows on the right side of the banner to review the current alarm/informational messages so you can confirm what fault is present.
steps.purpose: Confirm which LEFT/RIGHT tipper fault is currently indicated before pressing the corresponding reset button.
steps.expected_result: The informational banner message(s) corresponding to the current tipper fault are visible/identifiable via the banner navigation arrows.
steps.healthy_condition: Banner navigation arrows allow you to view the relevant current message(s) in the banner.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot navigate the banner messages (arrows do not change the displayed message) or the fault message cannot be identified.

actions.label: Navigate banner messages
actions.exact_action: Use the arrows on the right side of the banner to navigate through messages in the banner.

steps.title: Press the LEFT or RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET button for the indicated side
steps.instruction: Select the correct side (LEFT or RIGHT) and press the corresponding LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET button.
steps.purpose: Clear the corresponding tipper fault using the manual reset control for the correct side.
steps.expected_result: The corresponding tipper fault reset action is triggered for the selected side (LEFT or RIGHT).
steps.healthy_condition: You press the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET button that matches the side indicated by the current banner message(s).
steps.failure_condition: The wrong side’s reset button is pressed (LEFT vs RIGHT mismatch) or the reset button cannot be pressed/does not respond.

actions.label: Reset indicated tipper fault
actions.exact_action: Select the correct side (LEFT or RIGHT) and press the corresponding LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET button.

steps.title: Verify the banner message updates after reset
steps.instruction: After pressing reset, re-check the informational banner messages (use the arrows again if needed) to confirm the fault-related message is cleared/updated.
steps.purpose: Confirm the reset cleared/updated the fault indication as reflected in the VISU_MANCONTROL informational banner.
steps.expected_result: The informational banner messages update to reflect that the corresponding LEFT or RIGHT tipper fault has been reset (fault-related message cleared or replaced with a new/normal informational state).
steps.healthy_condition: The banner no longer shows the same active fault message for the reset side; it is cleared or replaced with a normal informational state.
steps.failure_condition: The same fault message remains unchanged after the reset.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the fault message does not change/clears within the expected operator observation window.
Do not proceed with additional manual actions if the banner continues to show an active fault condition.

actions.label: Re-check banner messages
actions.exact_action: Re-check the informational banner messages (use the arrows again if needed) to confirm the fault-related message is cleared/updated.

title: Run Lamp Test From VISU_MANCONTROL and Verify Red Flash + Audible Alarm
summary: On the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen VISU_MANCONTROL, use the LAMP TEST button to verify the audible alarm sounds and the stacklight flashes red.
when_to_use: Use to confirm the VISU_MANCONTROL LAMP TEST function triggers both the audible alarm and the stacklight red flashing behavior.

steps.title: Open the VISU_MANCONTROL screen
steps.instruction: Open the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.
steps.purpose: Access the maintenance manual control screen that contains the LAMP TEST button.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen is displayed with the LAMP TEST button visible.
steps.healthy_condition: VISU_MANCONTROL is loaded and the LAMP TEST button is present on the screen.
steps.failure_condition: VISU_MANCONTROL does not load or the LAMP TEST button is not visible.
stop_or_escalate_if: If VISU_MANCONTROL cannot be opened or the LAMP TEST button is not available, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Open VISU_MANCONTROL
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the "Visu_ManControl" screen.

steps.title: Press LAMP TEST
steps.instruction: On the VISU_MANCONTROL screen, press the LAMP TEST button.
steps.purpose: Trigger the lamp test behavior defined for VISU_MANCONTROL.
steps.expected_result: After pressing LAMP TEST, the audible alarm sounds and the stacklight flashes red.
steps.healthy_condition: Audible alarm is heard and the stacklight flashes red.
steps.failure_condition: Audible alarm does not sound and/or the stacklight does not flash red.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the audible alarm does not sound.
Stop and escalate if the stacklight does not flash red.
