actions.exact_action: Press the "LAMP TEST" button.

title: Manually Open/Close Tipper Grippers Using VISU_MANCONTROL
summary: On the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen VISU_MANCONTROL, use the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE button for the corresponding tipper (LEFT or RIGHT) to manually command the gripper to open or close, then verify the physical gripper state changes accordingly.
when_to_use: Use when you need to manually actuate a specific tipper gripper (LEFT or RIGHT) via the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen VISU_MANCONTROL.

steps.title: Open the VISU_MANCONTROL manual control screen
steps.instruction: On the Operator Station HMI, navigate to the maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.
steps.purpose: Access the HMI screen that contains the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE manual gripper controls.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen is displayed with the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE button for the corresponding tipper.
steps.healthy_condition: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen is visible and the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE control(s) are present for manual gripper actuation.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access VISU_MANCONTROL or the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE controls are not available on the displayed screen.

actions.label: Navigate to VISU_MANCONTROL
actions.exact_action: Open the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.

steps.title: Command the LEFT or RIGHT tipper gripper to open or close
steps.instruction: On VISU_MANCONTROL, select the corresponding tipper side (LEFT or RIGHT) and press the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE button to command the gripper to open or close.
steps.purpose: Send the manual open/close command to the selected tipper gripper.
steps.expected_result: A manual open/close command is issued for the selected tipper gripper via the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE button.
steps.healthy_condition: You have selected the correct tipper side (LEFT or RIGHT) and pressed the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE button for that side.
steps.failure_condition: You press the control for the wrong side, or the command cannot be issued from the screen.

actions.label: Press GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE for selected tipper
actions.exact_action: Select the corresponding tipper side (LEFT or RIGHT) and press the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE button to command the gripper to open or close.

steps.title: Verify physical gripper state matches the command
steps.instruction: Physically observe the corresponding tipper and confirm the gripper changes state to match the command (open vs closed).
steps.purpose: Confirm the manual command resulted in the expected physical gripper movement.
steps.expected_result: The corresponding tipper gripper opens or closes in response to the GRIPPERS OPEN/CLOSE button command.
steps.healthy_condition: The physical gripper position changes to the commanded state (open when commanded open; closed when commanded close).
steps.failure_condition: The physical gripper does not move to the commanded open/closed state.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the gripper does not move to the commanded open/closed state.

actions.label: Visually confirm gripper position
actions.exact_action: Verify the corresponding tipper gripper changes state to match the command (open vs closed) using physical observation at the tipper.

steps.title: Escalate if the gripper does not respond
steps.instruction: If the gripper does not move to the commanded open/closed state, stop the attempt and escalate.
steps.purpose: Ensure unresolved manual actuation is handled through escalation.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is initiated due to lack of physical response to the open/close command.
steps.healthy_condition: Not applicable (this step triggers only on failure).
steps.failure_condition: Continuing without escalation despite no physical response.

actions.label: Stop and escalate
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the gripper does not move to the commanded open/closed state.

title: Disable a LEFT/RIGHT Tipper and Verify Solid Blue Stacklight on VISU_MANCONTROL
summary: On the Operator Station HMI screen VISU_MANCONTROL, disable the corresponding LEFT or RIGHT tipper using the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE button and verify the corresponding stacklight illuminates solid blue.
when_to_use: Use when you need to disable a specific LEFT or RIGHT tipper from the Operator Station HMI and confirm the expected stacklight indication (solid blue) on VISU_MANCONTROL.

steps.title: Open VISU_MANCONTROL (Operator Station HMI manual control screen)
steps.instruction: Open the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.
steps.purpose: Access the manual control screen that contains the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE buttons and the associated stacklight indication.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen is displayed with the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE controls visible.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE button(s) on VISU_MANCONTROL.
steps.failure_condition: VISU_MANCONTROL is not accessible or the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE controls are not visible.

actions.label: Open VISU_MANCONTROL
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the "Visu_ManControl" screen.

steps.title: Disable the correct LEFT or RIGHT tipper using the DISABLE button
steps.instruction: Select the correct side (LEFT or RIGHT) and press the corresponding LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE button on VISU_MANCONTROL.
steps.purpose: Disable the selected tipper so the corresponding stacklight indicates the disabled state.
steps.expected_result: The corresponding tipper is disabled as indicated by the stacklight behavior described for the DISABLE button.
steps.healthy_condition: After pressing the correct LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE button, the corresponding tipper stacklight transitions to the expected solid blue state (verified in the next step).
steps.failure_condition: You press the wrong side or the stacklight does not transition to solid blue after the disable action.

actions.label: Press LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE
actions.exact_action: Press the LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE button.

steps.title: Verify the corresponding tipper stacklight illuminates solid blue
steps.instruction: Observe the corresponding tipper stacklight and confirm it illuminates solid blue.
steps.purpose: Confirm the disable action produced the expected physical indication.
steps.expected_result: The corresponding tipper stacklight illuminates solid blue.
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight is solid blue for the tipper whose DISABLE button was pressed.
steps.failure_condition: Stacklight does not illuminate solid blue after pressing the DISABLE button.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the stacklight does not illuminate solid blue after pressing the DISABLE button.

actions.label: Observe stacklight color
actions.exact_action: Observe the corresponding tipper stacklight.

title: Open WCOMMAND Screen and Check Input/Output Command Word Values for Left/Right Tipper
summary: On the Tipper HMI / WebVisu (VISU_MANCONTROL), open the WCOMMAND sub-screen to view the WCS input/output Command Word values for the selected tipper, and use NEXT SIDE to switch between left and right tipper communication.
when_to_use: Use when you need to verify the WCS communication as shown on the operator station tipper HMI by checking the input/output Command Word values for the left vs right tipper on the WCOMMAND screen.

steps.title: Open VISU_MANCONTROL (Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen)
steps.instruction: On the Tipper HMI / WebVisu (VISU), open the Operator Station maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.
steps.purpose: Get to the maintenance manual control screen that contains the WCOMMAND navigation button.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen is displayed with the WCOMMAND button available (Item 10).
steps.healthy_condition: VISU_MANCONTROL is visible and the WCOMMAND button is present for navigation to the WCOMMAND sub-screen.
steps.failure_condition: VISU_MANCONTROL does not open, or the WCOMMAND button is not available.
stop_or_escalate_if: VISU_MANCONTROL does not open.

actions.label: Open VISU_MANCONTROL
actions.exact_action: Open the Operator Station HMI maintenance manual control screen named VISU_MANCONTROL.

steps.title: Press WCOMMAND button to open WCOMMAND sub-screen
steps.instruction: On VISU_MANCONTROL, press the WCOMMAND button (Item 10).
steps.purpose: Open the screen that displays the WCS input/output Command Word values for the respective tipper.
steps.expected_result: The WCOMMAND sub-screen opens and displays input and output Command Word values for the respective tipper to WCS.
steps.healthy_condition: The WCOMMAND screen is open and shows both input and output Command Word values (not missing/blank).
steps.failure_condition: The WCOMMAND screen does not open, or the Command Word input/output values are missing/blank.
stop_or_escalate_if: WCOMMAND screen does not open.
Command Word input/output values are missing/blank.

actions.label: Open WCOMMAND sub-screen
actions.exact_action: Press the WCOMMAND button (Item 10) to open a screen with the input and output Command Word values for the respective tipper to WCS.

steps.title: Confirm input/output Command Word values are displayed on WCOMMAND screen
steps.instruction: On the WCOMMAND screen, confirm that the input and output Command Word values are displayed.
steps.purpose: Verify the WCOMMAND screen is functioning and the required values are visible for the selected tipper.
steps.expected_result: Input and output Command Word values are visible on the WCOMMAND screen.
steps.healthy_condition: Both input and output Command Word values are present (not blank/missing).
steps.failure_condition: Input and/or output Command Word values are missing or blank.
stop_or_escalate_if: Command Word input/output values are missing/blank.

actions.label: Verify Command Word values
actions.exact_action: On the WCOMMAND screen, confirm that input and output Command Word values are displayed.

steps.title: Use NEXT SIDE to switch between left and right tipper views and verify communication changes
steps.instruction: Press the NEXT SIDE button to navigate between the left and right tipper views, and confirm the displayed communication changes accordingly.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the WCOMMAND screen updates to show current WCS-to-operator-station communication for the left vs right tipper.
steps.expected_result: When NEXT SIDE is pressed, the displayed communication between the WCS and the operator station updates for the other tipper (left vs right).
steps.healthy_condition: The WCOMMAND screen view changes between left and right tipper communication (i.e., the displayed values/communication context updates).
steps.failure_condition: Pressing NEXT SIDE does not change the displayed communication/view, or the communication does not update when switching sides.
stop_or_escalate_if: Displayed communication does not change accordingly when switching left/right.

actions.label: Switch tipper side
actions.exact_action: To navigate between the left and right tipper, press the NEXT SIDE button.

title: Remove Z-Axis Gearbox for OptiSweep Z-Axis Gearbox Replacement (A-axis jog + LOTO + side panel removal)
summary: Prepare the OptiSweep Z-axis for gearbox replacement by manually positioning the A-axis/counter-balance to the specified threaded-hole location using the tipper HMI, performing tipper lockout/tagout (LOTO), removing the station side panel (nine self-tapping fasteners), and exposing the motor/gearbox area. Install an M6 socket-head screw below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
when_to_use: Use when preparing an OptiSweep Z-axis gearbox replacement and you must (1) position the A-axis/counter-balance between the actuator-base threaded holes, (2) lockout/tagout the tipper, and (3) remove the station side panel to access the motor/gearbox area.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a complete gearbox replacement workflow (it only covers the removal preparation steps evidenced in the provided manual section/page excerpt).

steps.title: Jog A-axis and counter-balance to the threaded-hole position
steps.instruction: On the tipper HMI (WebVisu/VISU), manually position (jog) the A-axis and counter-balance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.purpose: Position the A-axis/counter-balance so the gearbox removal preparation can proceed safely and so the carriages can be secured to prevent dropping after belt tension is released.
steps.expected_result: A-axis/counter-balance are positioned between the threaded holes with carriages between the holes on their respective rails.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are visibly located between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail (as shown in the gearbox figure).
steps.failure_condition: A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described, or carriages cannot be placed between the holes on their respective rails.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described.

actions.label: Manual jog A-axis/counter-balance
actions.exact_action: Use the HMI to manually position (jog) the A-axis and counter-balance between the threaded holes in the actuator base.

steps.title: Perform tipper LOTO using the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO for the tipper using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is locked out/tagged out before removing the station side panel and accessing the motor/gearbox area.
steps.expected_result: Tipper is locked out/tagged out.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed for the tipper per the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure (page 2).
steps.failure_condition: LOTO cannot be completed safely using the referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if LOTO cannot be completed safely using the referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure.

actions.label: Execute tipper lockout/tagout
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove the station side panel fasteners and the station side panel
steps.instruction: Using a 3/8-in. wrench or socket, remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Expose the motor/gearbox access area by removing the station side panel secured with nine self-tapping fasteners.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed and the motor/gearbox access area is exposed.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine self-tapping fasteners are removed and the station side panel is removed without remaining fasteners attached.
steps.failure_condition: Fasteners cannot be removed with the 3/8-in. wrench/socket, or the side panel cannot be removed to access the motor.

actions.label: Remove side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Install M6 socket-head screw below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.instruction: Insert an M6 socket-head screw into the holes below both carriages. These fasteners prevent the A-axis and counter-balance from dropping once belt tension is released.
steps.purpose: Prevent the A-axis and counter-balance from dropping once belt tension is released during subsequent gearbox removal steps.
steps.expected_result: An M6 socket-head screw is installed into the holes below both carriages.
steps.healthy_condition: M6 socket-head screw(s) are seated in the holes below both carriages, providing mechanical retention as described.
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screw cannot be inserted into the holes below both carriages, or the carriages cannot be held in place.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the carriages cannot be held in place with the M6 socket-head screw.

actions.label: Insert M6 screw below carriages
actions.exact_action: Insert an M6 socket-head screw into the holes below both carriages.

title: Quick Replacement of Z-Axis Cable Carrier (Snap Apart/Ends Snap-In)
summary: Performs a quick Z-axis cable carrier replacement by LOTO the tipper, snapping the carrier apart at both ends, removing the old carrier, installing the new carrier, snapping cross bars closed, and snapping both ends into the end pieces that remain mounted.
when_to_use: Use when both ends of the existing Z-axis cable carrier are in good condition and you need a quick replacement by snapping the carrier apart at both ends, leaving the end pieces mounted on the tipper.
not_for: Do not use this quick replacement method if either end of the existing carrier is not in good condition (the procedure is explicitly a quick replacement only when both ends are good).
Do not proceed if LOTO cannot be completed safely or if access to the motor/side panel is unclear.

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the manual’s referenced “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” location.
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is locked out/tagged out before any disassembly or access to the motor/side panel.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is in a locked-out/tagged-out state prior to side panel removal or carrier disassembly.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed before proceeding to remove the station side panel or snap apart the cable carrier.
steps.failure_condition: Proceeding without completing LOTO, or inability to complete LOTO safely.
stop_or_escalate_if: If LOTO cannot be completed safely, escalate to site/maintenance support before proceeding.

actions.label: Apply LOTO to tipper
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove station side panel (if necessary) to access the motor
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor area so the cable carrier can be snapped apart and replaced.
steps.expected_result: The station side panel is removed and the motor access area is available.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine (9) self-tapping securing screws are removed and the side panel is removed cleanly to expose the motor area.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel cannot be removed due to unclear access, missing/incorrect fasteners, or unsafe conditions.
stop_or_escalate_if: If access to the motor/side panel is unclear, escalate to site/maintenance support before proceeding.

actions.label: Remove nine side panel screws
actions.exact_action: use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Snap apart the old cable carrier at both ends (leave end pieces attached)
steps.instruction: Disassemble or “snap apart” the cable carrier at both ends, leaving only the end pieces attached to the tipper.
steps.purpose: Remove the old carrier while keeping the end pieces mounted on the tipper.
steps.expected_result: The old cable carrier is separated at both ends, with only the end pieces remaining attached to the tipper.
steps.healthy_condition: End pieces remain attached to the tipper while the carrier is fully separated at both ends.
steps.failure_condition: Carrier ends cannot be snapped apart cleanly, or end pieces detach unintentionally.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check alignment if the new carrier cannot be snapped fully into the end pieces or if cross bars do not fully close.

actions.label: Snap apart carrier at both ends
actions.exact_action: Disassemble or “snap apart” the cable carrier at both ends, leaving only the end pieces attached to the tipper.

steps.title: Snap ends off the new carrier and open cross bars on the outside of the new carrier
steps.instruction: “Snap” the ends off the new cable carrier and open all the cross bars on the outside of the new cable carrier.
steps.purpose: Prepare the new carrier so it can be installed and then snapped into the existing end pieces.
steps.expected_result: The new carrier’s ends are snapped off, and all outside cross bars are open.
steps.healthy_condition: All outside cross bars are open on the new carrier and the ends are separated from the new carrier.
steps.failure_condition: Cross bars do not open fully or ends cannot be snapped off.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check alignment if the new carrier cannot be snapped fully into the end pieces or if cross bars do not fully close.

actions.label: Prepare new carrier
actions.exact_action: “Snap” the ends off the new cable carrier and open all the cross bars on the outside of the new cable carrier.

steps.title: Open cross bars on the old carrier and remove it from the system
steps.instruction: Open all the cross bars on the outside of the old cable carrier and remove it from the system.
steps.purpose: Clear the old carrier from the system after it has been snapped apart.
steps.expected_result: The old cable carrier is removed from the system.
steps.healthy_condition: All outside cross bars on the old carrier are open and the carrier is fully removed.
steps.failure_condition: Old carrier cannot be removed or cross bars remain closed.

actions.label: Remove old carrier
actions.exact_action: Open all the cross bars on the outside of the old cable carrier and remove it from the system.

steps.title: Position the new carrier roughly in place with internal dividers against the air line
steps.instruction: Put the new cable carrier roughly in place while positioning the internal dividers all the way to one side, against the air line.
steps.purpose: Ensure correct internal divider placement before snapping cross bars closed and snapping ends into end pieces.
steps.expected_result: New carrier is positioned roughly in place and internal dividers are all the way to one side against the air line.
steps.healthy_condition: Internal dividers are positioned against the air line (all the way to one side).
steps.failure_condition: Internal dividers are not against the air line or carrier alignment prevents later snapping.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check alignment if the new carrier cannot be snapped fully into the end pieces or if cross bars do not fully close.

actions.label: Roughly position new carrier
actions.exact_action: Put the new cable carrier roughly in place while positioning the internal dividers all the way to one side, against the air line.

steps.title: Snap all outside cross bars closed
steps.instruction: “Snap” all the cross bars closed.
steps.purpose: Secure the new carrier structure by closing all outside cross bars.
steps.expected_result: All outside cross bars on the new carrier are snapped closed.
steps.healthy_condition: Every outside cross bar is fully closed (snapped in).
steps.failure_condition: One or more cross bars do not fully close.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check alignment if the new carrier cannot be snapped fully into the end pieces or if cross bars do not fully close.

actions.label: Close cross bars
actions.exact_action: “Snap” all the cross bars closed.

steps.title: Snap both ends into the end pieces still mounted on the tipper
steps.instruction: “Snap” both ends into the end pieces that are still mounted.
steps.purpose: Complete installation by snapping the carrier ends into the existing end pieces.
steps.expected_result: Both ends of the new carrier are snapped into the end pieces that remain mounted on the tipper.
steps.healthy_condition: Both ends are fully seated in the end pieces (snapped in).
steps.failure_condition: New carrier ends cannot be snapped fully into the end pieces.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and re-check alignment if the new carrier cannot be snapped fully into the end pieces or if cross bars do not fully close.
If LOTO cannot be completed safely or access to the motor/side panel is unclear, escalate to site/maintenance support before proceeding.

actions.label: Snap ends into end pieces
actions.exact_action: “Snap” both ends into the end pieces that are still mounted.

title: Configure Barcode Interface scanner settings (password, prefixes, HTTP/OPC URLs) for AGV and Hospital control IPs
summary: On the Windows laptop used for scanner setup, update the replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner’s Barcode Interface settings so tote/location label prefixes match and the HTTP/OPC URLs point to the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses, then save the settings.
when_to_use: Use when a scanner is replaced and the new scanner must be set up so Barcode Interface settings use the correct tote/location prefixes and the correct AGV/Hospital control IP addresses in the HTTP and OPC URL fields.

steps.title: Launch Barcode Interface on the scanner setup laptop
steps.instruction: On the Windows laptop used for scanner setup, launch the Barcode Interface application (Barcode Interface.exe).
steps.purpose: Open the application used to configure the replacement scanner settings.
steps.expected_result: Barcode Interface is open and ready for interaction (scanner setup workflow visible).
steps.healthy_condition: The application is running and you can proceed to the settings area.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode Interface does not launch or is not accessible on the desktop.

actions.label: Open Barcode Interface
actions.exact_action: Launch the Barcode Interface application. This should be on the desktop.

steps.title: Open Settings and enter the default password
steps.instruction: In Barcode Interface, click the "settings" button and supply the default password "Opti".
steps.purpose: Access the protected settings panel to edit prefixes and HTTP/OPC URLs.
steps.expected_result: The settings panel accepts the password and the settings fields are available for editing.
steps.healthy_condition: You can view/edit the prefix configuration fields and the HTTP/OPC URL fields.
steps.failure_condition: Password is rejected or settings fields do not become available.

actions.label: Open settings
actions.exact_action: Check the settings by clicking the settings button, supply the password. By default, the pass- word is “Opti”.

steps.title: Verify tote/location label prefixes match
steps.instruction: Verify the configured prefixes match the labels on the totes and locations.
steps.purpose: Ensure the scanner will interpret labels correctly for totes and locations.
steps.expected_result: Prefix values shown in the settings match the tote/location label prefixes you physically verify.
steps.healthy_condition: Prefixes match the tote/location labels (no mismatch observed).
steps.failure_condition: Prefixes do not match the tote/location labels.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the prefixes do not match the tote/location labels.

actions.label: Compare prefixes
actions.exact_action: Verify prefixes match the labels on the totes and locations.

steps.title: Update HTTP and OPC URLs to correct AGV/Hospital control IPs
steps.instruction: Change the URL for both the HTTP and OPC settings so the HTTP URL contains the AGV control IP address and the OPC URL contains the Hospital control IP address.
steps.purpose: Point the scanner interface to the correct AGV control and Hospital control endpoints.
steps.expected_result: HTTP URL field includes the AGV control IP address; OPC URL field includes the Hospital control IP address.
steps.healthy_condition: Both URL fields contain the correct IP addresses in the expected HTTP vs OPC fields.
steps.failure_condition: HTTP/OPC URLs cannot be updated to include the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the HTTP/OPC URLs cannot be updated to include the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses.

actions.label: Edit HTTP/OPC URLs
actions.exact_action: Change the URL for both the HTTP and OPC setting to contain the AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses respectively.

steps.title: Save the scanner settings
steps.instruction: Save the settings using the "Save Settings" button.
steps.purpose: Commit the updated prefixes and URLs so the scanner uses them.
steps.expected_result: Settings are saved (the updated prefix/URL values are committed after clicking "Save Settings").
steps.healthy_condition: After saving, the settings reflect the updated prefixes and the HTTP/OPC URLs with the correct IP addresses.
steps.failure_condition: Settings do not save or the displayed values revert/are not updated after saving.

actions.label: Save settings
actions.exact_action: Save the settings with the "Save Settings" button.

title: Set up a replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner using Barcode Interface (hardware connect + connectivity + calibration)
summary: Set up a replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner so the Barcode Interface application shows healthy connectivity and the scanner is calibrated when the app connectivity indicator is red.
when_to_use: Use when a Zebra DS3608-SR scanner has been replaced and needs setup so Barcode Interface connectivity is healthy; if the Barcode Interface connectivity indicator is red, calibration is required.

steps.title: Verify laptop and Barcode Interface availability; log in with a FORTNA account
steps.instruction: On the Windows 10/11 laptop, confirm Barcode Interface.exe is installed (on the desktop with a FORTNA logo), then log into the laptop with a FORTNA account.
steps.purpose: Ensure the setup laptop can run Barcode Interface and is authenticated before connecting and configuring the scanner.
steps.expected_result: You are logged into the Windows laptop with a FORTNA account and Barcode Interface.exe is available to launch.
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode Interface.exe is present on the desktop and you can proceed to launch it.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode Interface.exe is not available or you cannot log in with a FORTNA account.

actions.label: Confirm Barcode Interface.exe and login
actions.exact_action: Log into the laptop with a FORTNA account.

steps.title: Connect scanner dock cabling and power; confirm dock lights up
steps.instruction: Connect the RJ45 side of the USB cable to the back of the scanner dock, connect the USB to the laptop, and connect the auxiliary cable to the power adapter. Plug the power adapter into a 120 VAC outlet (x2). Confirm the dock lights up.
steps.purpose: Provide power and connectivity path from the scanner dock to the laptop so the scanner can charge and Barcode Interface can detect connectivity.
steps.expected_result: The scanner dock powers on and its lights are on.
steps.healthy_condition: Dock lights up after the power adapter is plugged into a 120 VAC outlet.
steps.failure_condition: Dock does not light up after connecting power.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the dock does not light up after connecting power.

actions.label: Connect RJ45/USB/aux power
actions.exact_action: Connect the RJ45 side of the USB cable to the back of the scanner dock, the USB to the laptop, and the auxiliary to the power adapter. Be sure to plug the adapter into a 120 VAC outlet. The dock should light up.

steps.title: Charge the scanner on the dock until the battery indicator turns green
steps.instruction: If the scanner is uncharged, place it on the dock until the red battery symbol shown on top turns green.
steps.purpose: Ensure the replacement scanner has sufficient charge before proceeding to Barcode Interface connectivity checks and calibration.
steps.expected_result: Scanner battery indicator changes from red to green.
steps.healthy_condition: Battery indicator on top of the scanner is green.
steps.failure_condition: Battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the scanner battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock.

actions.label: Check battery indicator color
actions.exact_action: If the scanner is uncharged it will need to rest on the dock until the red battery symbol shown on top turns green.

steps.title: Launch Barcode Interface application
steps.instruction: Launch the Barcode Interface application (should be on the desktop).
steps.purpose: Open the application that displays connectivity status and provides the calibration action when connectivity is red.
steps.expected_result: Barcode Interface is open and the screen is ready for connectivity status verification.
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode Interface window is visible and you can view the connectivity indicator at the bottom right of the screen.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode Interface does not launch or the connectivity indicator is not visible.

actions.label: Open Barcode Interface
actions.exact_action: Launch the Barcode Interface application. This should be on the desktop.

steps.title: Check Barcode Interface connectivity indicator (bottom right)
steps.instruction: Check the connectivity indicator at the bottom right of the Barcode Interface screen.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the scanner needs calibration based on the app connectivity status.
steps.expected_result: Connectivity indicator is either green or red.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectivity indicator is green.
steps.failure_condition: Connectivity indicator remains red.

actions.label: Observe connectivity indicator
actions.exact_action: Check connectivity on the bottom right of the screen.

steps.title: Calibrate scanner only if connectivity indicator is red
steps.instruction: If the connectivity indicator is red, click "Calibrate Scanner" and follow the onscreen instructions until calibration completes.
steps.purpose: Restore healthy scanner connectivity by running calibration when the app reports red connectivity.
steps.expected_result: After calibration, the operator observes the connectivity indicator change to green.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectivity indicator becomes green after calibration.
steps.failure_condition: Connectivity indicator remains red after clicking "Calibrate Scanner" and following the onscreen instructions.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the Barcode Interface connectivity indicator remains red after clicking "Calibrate Scanner" and following the onscreen instructions.

actions.label: Run calibration
actions.exact_action: If red, click "Calibrate Scanner" and follow the onscreen instructions.

steps.title: Skip calibration if connectivity indicator is green
steps.instruction: If the connectivity indicator is green, skip calibration and proceed to the next step of the overall scanner setup procedure.
steps.purpose: Avoid unnecessary calibration when the scanner already reports healthy connectivity.
steps.expected_result: Connectivity indicator is green and calibration is not performed.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectivity indicator is green.
steps.failure_condition: Connectivity indicator is not green (red) but calibration is skipped.

actions.label: Confirm green status
actions.exact_action: If green, skip this step.

title: Check SMALLS System Health Using the Smalls Overview HMI Screen (Color-Coded Layout)
summary: Use the SMALLS overview screen on the System HMI to quickly identify which parts of the SMALLS system are in a normal vs abnormal (color-coded) status based on the system layout.
when_to_use: When you need a fast, at-a-glance health check of the SMALLS system parts using the color-coded SMALLS system layout.

steps.title: Open the "Smalls" overview screen from the System HMI
steps.instruction: On the System HMI, press the SMALLS button to open the "Smalls" overview screen.
steps.purpose: Get to the SMALLS overview layout that shows color-coded status for each part.
steps.expected_result: The "Smalls" overview screen is displayed.
steps.healthy_condition: The "Smalls" overview screen loads successfully and shows the SMALLS system layout.
steps.failure_condition: The "Smalls" overview screen does not open or the SMALLS layout is not visible.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access the "Smalls" overview screen, stop and escalate for support.

actions.label: Press SMALLS
actions.exact_action: Press SMALLS to access the "Smalls" overview screen.

steps.title: Review the SMALLS system layout on the "Smalls" overview screen
steps.instruction: On the "Smalls" overview screen, review the SMALLS system layout.
steps.purpose: Identify each SMALLS part shown on the layout so you can check its color-coded status.
steps.expected_result: You can see the SMALLS system layout with parts displayed for status checking.
steps.healthy_condition: The layout is fully visible and each part is present on the screen for color inspection.
steps.failure_condition: Parts are missing/unreadable on the layout, or the screen does not provide a clear view of the layout.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot clearly determine which parts are shown on the layout, stop and escalate.

actions.label: Review layout
actions.exact_action: Review the "Smalls" system layout.

steps.title: Check each SMALLS part’s color-coded status indicator
steps.instruction: For each part shown on the layout, observe the color-coded status indicator.
steps.purpose: Determine which parts are abnormal by observing the color-coded status indicators on the layout.
steps.expected_result: You have identified which parts (if any) show abnormal color-coded status (i.e., not the normal/expected color for that part).
steps.healthy_condition: All parts show the normal/expected color-coded status indicators for their respective parts.
steps.failure_condition: One or more parts show abnormal color-coded status indicators.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if multiple system parts show abnormal color-coded status.

actions.label: Observe color-coded indicators
actions.exact_action: Observe the color-coded status of each part of the system.

steps.title: Identify abnormal parts and decide whether to stop/escalate
steps.instruction: Identify any parts whose color-coded status indicates an abnormal condition (i.e., not the normal/expected color for that part). If the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, treat it as abnormal.
steps.purpose: Ensure abnormal indications are handled appropriately and escalate when abnormality is widespread or unclear.
steps.expected_result: You have a clear list of abnormal parts (if any) and a decision to escalate when abnormality is widespread or unclear.
steps.healthy_condition: No parts indicate abnormal color-coded status; no offline/blocked section is indicated.
steps.failure_condition: Multiple parts show abnormal color-coded status, or the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, or you cannot determine which parts are abnormal.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if multiple system parts show abnormal color-coded status.
Stop and escalate if the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action.
Stop and escalate if you cannot determine which parts are abnormal from the screen.

actions.label: Identify abnormal parts
actions.exact_action: Identify any parts whose color-coded status indicates an abnormal condition.

title: Check Operator Station HMI I/O Diagnostics (VISU_IO_DIAG) for CPU/MB Temps, 24V, and Input/ Switch States
summary: Use the read-only Operator Station HMI screen VISU_IO_DIAG to troubleshoot operator-station I/O by verifying the displayed Control Temps (CPU and MB), internal controller Voltage Levels (expected 24 V), and the on/off status of the station switch and inputs. Use the input sections to open input detail information and use the screen drop-down to navigate to other screens if needed.
when_to_use: When troubleshooting operator-station I/O on the Operator Station HMI and you need to confirm that the HMI hardware diagnostics are reporting expected values for CPU/MB temperatures, internal controller voltage (should be 24 V), and the station switch/input on/off indications.

steps.title: Open the read-only VISU_IO_DIAG diagnostics screen on the Operator Station HMI
steps.instruction: On the Operator Station HMI, navigate to the read-only screen named VISU_IO_DIAG (Operator Station IO Diagnostics Screen).
steps.purpose: Access the diagnostic sections needed to verify CPU/MB temperatures, internal controller voltage (expected 24 V), and switch/input on/off states.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_IO_DIAG screen is open and displays the informational banner, the “Control Temps” section, the “Voltage Levels” section, the switch status section (inputs on/off), the input sections, and the drop-down menu.
steps.healthy_condition: VISU_IO_DIAG loads successfully and shows all diagnostic sections (banner, Control Temps, Voltage Levels, switch status, inputs, and drop-down menu).
steps.failure_condition: The VISU_IO_DIAG screen cannot be opened, or it does not display the Control Temps / Voltage Levels / input sections as described.
stop_or_escalate_if: VISU_IO_DIAG cannot be opened or does not display the Control Temps / Voltage Levels / input sections.

actions.label: Navigate to VISU_IO_DIAG
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the read-only screen named VISU_IO_DIAG (Operator Station IO Diagnostics Screen).

steps.title: Check the informational banner for active alarms/messages
steps.instruction: Review the informational banner at the top of the VISU_IO_DIAG screen. If messages are present, use the right-side arrows to cycle through messages.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the screen is reporting any current alarms or informational messages that may explain I/O behavior.
steps.expected_result: The informational banner shows any current alarms or informational messages; if multiple messages exist, you can navigate through them using the right-side arrows.
steps.healthy_condition: The banner displays the current status/messages and the right-side arrows allow cycling through them.
steps.failure_condition: The banner does not show any messages when expected for the troubleshooting context, or the banner navigation arrows are not present/usable.

actions.label: Review banner and cycle messages
actions.exact_action: Use the right-side arrows to navigate through messages in the banner.

steps.title: Verify CPU and motherboard (MB) temperature readings in Control Temps
steps.instruction: In the “Control Temps” section, verify the CPU temperature and the motherboard (MB) temperature values displayed on the screen.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the HMI’s internal temperature diagnostics are reporting values for CPU and MB.
steps.expected_result: The “Control Temps” section shows temperature readings for both CPU and MB.
steps.healthy_condition: CPU and MB temperature readings are present and displayed in the “Control Temps” section.
steps.failure_condition: CPU/MB temperature readings are missing, not displayed, or the Control Temps section is not present on the screen.

actions.label: Check Control Temps values
actions.exact_action: In the “Control Temps” section, record/verify the CPU temperature and the motherboard (MB) temperature values shown on the screen.

steps.title: Verify internal controller voltage readings in Voltage Levels (expected 24 V)
steps.instruction: In the “Voltage Levels” section, verify the internal controller voltage reading(s). These should be 24 V.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the HMI internal controller voltage diagnostic reports the expected 24 V level.
steps.expected_result: The “Voltage Levels” section shows internal controller voltage readings with a value of 24 V.
steps.healthy_condition: Voltage Levels indicates the internal controller voltage is 24 V.
steps.failure_condition: Voltage Levels is not 24 V.
stop_or_escalate_if: “Voltage Levels” are not 24 V.

actions.label: Check Voltage Levels
actions.exact_action: Verify the internal controller voltage reading(s; these should be 24 V.

steps.title: Verify station switch/input on/off indications in the switch status section
steps.instruction: In the switch status section (corresponding to the switch mounted on the station), verify which inputs are shown as ON vs OFF.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the station switch and input on/off states shown by the HMI match the expected station behavior being investigated.
steps.expected_result: The switch status section displays which station inputs are ON and which are OFF.
steps.healthy_condition: The ON/OFF indications in the switch status section match the expected station behavior being investigated.
steps.failure_condition: The switch/input ON/OFF indications do not match the expected station behavior being investigated.
stop_or_escalate_if: Switch/input ON/OFF indications do not match the expected station behavior being investigated.

actions.label: Check switch/input ON/OFF
actions.exact_action: Verify which inputs are shown as ON vs OFF in the switch status section.

steps.title: Open input detail window by selecting an input section
steps.instruction: In the inputs section, select one of the input sections to open the window with more information about what the selected input is.
steps.purpose: Get more information about a specific input whose ON/OFF state you are investigating.
steps.expected_result: Selecting an input section opens a window providing more information about that input.
steps.healthy_condition: The input detail window opens successfully for the selected input.
steps.failure_condition: Selecting an input section does not open the detail window, or the detail window does not provide input information.

actions.label: Select an input section
actions.exact_action: Select one of the input sections to open the window with more information about what the selected input is.

steps.title: Use the VISU_IO_DIAG drop-down menu to navigate to other screens if needed
steps.instruction: Use the drop-down menu on the VISU_IO_DIAG screen to directly select/view other screens if needed for additional troubleshooting context.
steps.purpose: Jump to other Operator Station HMI screens for additional troubleshooting context when required.
steps.expected_result: The drop-down menu allows direct selection of another screen to view.
steps.healthy_condition: You can use the drop-down menu to navigate to the selected screen.
steps.failure_condition: The drop-down menu is not present/usable or navigation does not occur.

actions.label: Select another screen from drop-down
actions.exact_action: Use the drop-down menu that can be used to directly select the screen to view.

title: Load New Tipper Firmware via Tipper HMI (VISU) USB Install
summary: Update the tipper controller firmware using the Tipper HMI (VISU) USB install flow, then power-cycle the controller and confirm the HMI returns to the expected default screen state ("Visu_Default" with IP and subnet mask settings) and that F3 navigates to "Visu_MCP_Dual".
when_to_use: Use when you need to load new firmware onto a tipper controller using the HMI USB install flow and then verify the HMI returns to the expected default screen state.

steps.title: Turn off power to the tipper using the disconnect
steps.instruction: Turn off power to the tipper using the disconnect.
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper controller is powered down before initiating the firmware-load button/power-on sequence.
steps.expected_result: The tipper controller is powered off (HMI is not in normal operation).
steps.healthy_condition: Power is fully off prior to the next step’s power-on sequence.
steps.failure_condition: Power remains on (HMI does not behave as expected for a power-on sequence).

actions.label: Power off tipper via disconnect
actions.exact_action: Turn off power to the tipper using the disconnect.

steps.title: Hold the top three buttons on the tipper HMI
steps.instruction: On the tipper HMI, press and hold the top three buttons.
steps.purpose: Enter the firmware-load mode during the subsequent power-on.
steps.expected_result: The top three buttons are held continuously in preparation for powering on.
steps.healthy_condition: Buttons remain held through the power-on in the next step.
steps.failure_condition: You release the buttons before or during power-on.

actions.label: Hold top three buttons
actions.exact_action: On the tipper HMI, press and hold the top three buttons.

steps.title: Power on the tipper while continuing to hold the top three buttons
steps.instruction: While continuing to hold the top three buttons, power on the tipper.
steps.purpose: Trigger the controller into the firmware-load mode.
steps.expected_result: The controller begins booting into the firmware-load mode.
steps.healthy_condition: The gray screen appears in the next step while the buttons are still held.
steps.failure_condition: The gray screen does not appear (indicating the firmware-load mode was not entered).
stop_or_escalate_if: If the gray screen does not appear after holding the top three buttons during power-on, stop and re-check that the correct buttons are held through power-on before proceeding.

actions.label: Power on tipper
actions.exact_action: While continuing to hold the top three buttons, power on the tipper.

steps.title: Wait for the gray screen
steps.instruction: Keep holding the buttons until a gray screen appears.
steps.purpose: Confirm the controller is in the firmware-load mode before starting the USB install.
steps.expected_result: A gray screen appears on the tipper HMI.
steps.healthy_condition: Gray screen is visible while buttons are still held.
steps.failure_condition: No gray screen appears.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the gray screen does not appear, stop and re-check that the correct buttons are held through power-on before proceeding.

actions.label: Confirm gray screen
actions.exact_action: Keep holding the buttons until a gray screen appears.

steps.title: Insert the USB drive into the HMI USB dongle
steps.instruction: Plug the USB drive containing the new firmware version into the USB dongle on the HMI.
steps.purpose: Provide the firmware file to the controller for installation.
steps.expected_result: The USB drive is physically connected to the HMI USB dongle.
steps.healthy_condition: USB is inserted and ready for the install action.
steps.failure_condition: USB is not inserted correctly (install option cannot proceed).

actions.label: Insert firmware USB
actions.exact_action: Plug the USB drive containing the new firmware version into the USB dongle on the HMI.

steps.title: Press INSTALL FROM FILE
steps.instruction: Press the "INSTALL FROM FILE" button.
steps.purpose: Start the firmware installation from the USB drive.
steps.expected_result: The HMI begins the firmware install flow from the USB.
steps.healthy_condition: The install flow proceeds to loading/progress or completion.
steps.failure_condition: The install flow does not start or does not progress.

actions.label: Start install from USB
actions.exact_action: Press the "INSTALL FROM FILE" button.

steps.title: Load the firmware from the USB until the install completes
steps.instruction: Load the firmware from the USB (continue the on-screen install flow until it completes).
steps.purpose: Complete the firmware update process.
steps.expected_result: The on-screen install flow reaches completion.
steps.healthy_condition: Install/load progress completes successfully and the flow ends.
steps.failure_condition: Install does not complete or appears stuck/failed.

actions.label: Run install flow to completion
actions.exact_action: Load the firmware from the USB (continue the on-screen install flow until it completes).

steps.title: Power-cycle the controller and boot normally
steps.instruction: Power the controller off and back on, then allow it to boot normally without pressing any buttons.
steps.purpose: Ensure the new firmware is applied and the controller returns to normal operation.
steps.expected_result: Controller reboots normally without entering the firmware-load mode.
steps.healthy_condition: No button-hold sequence is active during boot.
steps.failure_condition: Controller re-enters firmware-load mode due to button presses during boot.

actions.label: Power-cycle controller
actions.exact_action: Power the controller off and back on, then allow it to boot normally without pressing any buttons.

steps.title: Verify Visu_Default screen appears with IP and subnet mask settings
steps.instruction: Verify the "Visu_Default" screen appears on the HMI displaying the IP and subnet mask settings.
steps.purpose: Confirm the controller is in the expected post-install default screen state.
steps.expected_result: The HMI shows the "Visu_Default" screen and displays IP and subnet mask fields.
steps.healthy_condition: "Visu_Default" is visible with IP and subnet mask settings shown.
steps.failure_condition: "Visu_Default" does not appear or IP/subnet mask fields are not shown after reboot.
stop_or_escalate_if: If "Visu_Default" does not appear or IP/subnet mask fields are not shown after reboot, stop and escalate for support rather than continuing with further HMI navigation.

actions.label: Check default screen state
actions.exact_action: Verify the "Visu_Default" screen appears on the HMI displaying the IP and subnet mask settings.

steps.title: Press F3 to navigate to Visu_MCP_Dual
steps.instruction: Press F3 to go to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.
steps.purpose: Confirm the HMI navigation works after firmware load and reboot.
steps.expected_result: The HMI displays the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen after pressing F3.
steps.healthy_condition: "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen is visible.
steps.failure_condition: Pressing F3 does not navigate to "Visu_MCP_Dual".

actions.label: Navigate to Visu_MCP_Dual
actions.exact_action: Press F3 to go to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.

title: Open and Use the Tipping Station Screen on the Tipper HMI
summary: Navigate the Tipper HMI to the “Tipping Station” screen to view bag completion counts, error information, and task duration metrics for the tipping station.
when_to_use: Use when you need to monitor tipping station performance by checking bag completion counts, error information, and how long tasks take on the Tipper HMI.

steps.title: Press the SMALLS button on the Tipper HMI
steps.instruction: On the Tipper HMI, press the SMALLS button.
steps.purpose: Start navigation to the ACB-related screens on the Tipper HMI.
steps.expected_result: The SMALLS drop-down menu is displayed.
steps.healthy_condition: The SMALLS drop-down menu appears and is selectable.
steps.failure_condition: The SMALLS drop-down menu does not appear or cannot be selected.

actions.label: Open SMALLS menu
actions.exact_action: press SMALLS

steps.title: Select ACB from the SMALLS drop-down menu
steps.instruction: In the drop-down menu, select "ACB".
steps.purpose: Choose the ACB category to reach the correct ACB instance.
steps.expected_result: The options list updates to show ACB options.
steps.healthy_condition: “ACB” is selected and the next options list is available.
steps.failure_condition: “ACB” is not selectable or selecting it does not advance to the ACB options list.

actions.label: Select ACB
actions.exact_action: select "ACB" from the drop-down menu

steps.title: Select ACB1 - AMT TT from the options list
steps.instruction: From the options list, select "ACB1 - AMT TT".
steps.purpose: Select the specific ACB instance required to open the Tipping Station screen.
steps.expected_result: The system is set to the “ACB1 - AMT TT” context so the tipper button can open the Tipping Station screen.
steps.healthy_condition: “ACB1 - AMT TT” is selected and the screen is ready for the next action (pressing the tipper button).
steps.failure_condition: “ACB1 - AMT TT” is not present/selectable or selection does not prepare the screen for the tipper button action.

actions.label: Select ACB1 - AMT TT
actions.exact_action: select "ACB1 - AMT TT" from the options

steps.title: Press the tipper button on the right side of the screen
steps.instruction: Press the tipper button on the right side of the screen.
steps.purpose: Open the “Tipping Station” screen for the selected ACB instance.
steps.expected_result: The “Tipping Station” screen opens.
steps.healthy_condition: The “Tipping Station” screen is displayed.
steps.failure_condition: The “Tipping Station” screen does not appear after selecting “ACB1 - AMT TT” and pressing the tipper button.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the “Tipping Station” screen does not appear after selecting "ACB1 - AMT TT" and pressing the tipper button, stop and escalate to support/site IT to restore HMI navigation or access.

actions.label: Open Tipping Station screen
actions.exact_action: press the tipper button on the right side of the screen

steps.title: Verify bag completion, errors, and task duration metrics on the Tipping Station screen
steps.instruction: Verify the “Tipping Station” screen is displayed and check that it shows: (1) how many bags are completed, (2) errors, and (3) how long tasks take.
steps.purpose: Confirm the screen is functioning and capture the key operational metrics it provides.
steps.expected_result: The “Tipping Station” screen displays bag completion information, error information, and task duration/timers.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see values/indicators for: bag completion count, error information, and task duration metrics on the “Tipping Station” screen.
steps.failure_condition: The “Tipping Station” screen is missing one or more of the expected metric areas (bag completion, errors, task duration) or the screen does not display the expected information.

actions.label: Check metrics
actions.exact_action: check that it shows how many bags are completed, errors, and how long tasks take

title: Check Tipper Process Status and Send/Pause Controls on the VISU_DATA Screen
summary: On the Operator Station HMI (VISU_DATA screen), verify the tipper Process Status indicators (green states) and use the VISU_DATA controls to send a tote to the hospital (SEND LEFT TO HOSPITAL / SEND RIGHT TO HOSPITAL) or pause both tippers (PAUSE TIPPER).
when_to_use: Use when you need to (1) confirm the current tipper process state indicators on the VISU_DATA screen and (2) send the tote at the left or right tipper to the hospital, or pause both tippers.

steps.title: Open the Operator Station HMI and navigate to the VISU_DATA screen
steps.instruction: On the Operator Station HMI, open the VISU_DATA screen (Operator Station HMI Data Screen).
steps.purpose: Access the Process Status indicators and the manual controls for sending totes to the hospital or pausing both tippers.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_DATA screen is displayed, including the Process Status section and the buttons SEND LEFT TO HOSPITAL, SEND RIGHT TO HOSPITAL, and PAUSE TIPPER.
steps.healthy_condition: VISU_DATA screen elements are visible and readable, including the Process Status indicators and the three controls.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot see the Process Status section or the SEND LEFT/RIGHT TO HOSPITAL and PAUSE TIPPER buttons on the screen.

actions.label: Navigate to VISU_DATA
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the "VISU_DATA" screen (Operator Station HMI Data Screen).

steps.title: Verify green Process Status indicators in the Process Status section
steps.instruction: In the Process Status section, observe the green status indicators for: In Cycle (Auto mode), Tipper Ready, AGV Present, Tip in Process, Tipper Clear, and Tipper Faulted.
steps.purpose: Confirm the tipper’s current operational state before using send/pause controls.
steps.expected_result: The Process Status indicators show green states corresponding to the current tipper process state (as defined by the VISU_DATA Process Status indicators).
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant indicators you intend to rely on for the action are green (e.g., In Cycle is green when operating in Auto mode; Tipper Ready is green when ready to receive a tote; Tip in Process is green when the gripper has a tote; Tipper Clear is green when the gripper is open; Tipper Faulted is green if the tipper currently has a fault).
steps.failure_condition: The Process Status indicators do not match the intended action state (e.g., the tipper is not in the expected ready/clear/in-process state, or the tipper faulted state is not consistent with what you are attempting).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and do not continue using send/pause controls if the Process Status indicators do not match the expected green states for the intended action (e.g., tipper not ready / not in the expected state).

actions.label: Check Process Status indicators
actions.exact_action: Observe the Process Status indicators (In Cycle, Tipper Ready, AGV Present, Tip in Process, Tipper Clear, Tipper Faulted).

steps.title: Send the tote at the left tipper to the hospital
steps.instruction: If a tote is currently at the left tipper and needs to be sent to the hospital, press SEND LEFT TO HOSPITAL.
steps.purpose: Divert the tote currently at the left tipper to the hospital using the VISU_DATA control.
steps.expected_result: Pressing SEND LEFT TO HOSPITAL initiates sending the tote at the left tipper to the hospital.
steps.healthy_condition: The Process Status indicators are consistent with the action (e.g., the left side is in the appropriate state such that a tote is present/in process and the tipper is ready/appropriate per the Process Status indicator meanings).
steps.failure_condition: The Process Status indicators do not match the expected green states for sending (e.g., tipper not ready / not in the expected state), or you observe a mismatch after pressing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and do not continue using send/pause controls if the Process Status indicators do not match the expected green states for the intended action.

actions.label: Send left tote to hospital
actions.exact_action: Press the SEND LEFT TO HOSPITAL button.

steps.title: Send the tote at the right tipper to the hospital
steps.instruction: If a tote is currently at the right tipper and needs to be sent to the hospital, press SEND RIGHT TO HOSPITAL.
steps.purpose: Divert the tote currently at the right tipper to the hospital using the VISU_DATA control.
steps.expected_result: Pressing SEND RIGHT TO HOSPITAL initiates sending the tote at the right tipper to the hospital.
steps.healthy_condition: The Process Status indicators are consistent with the action (e.g., the right side is in the appropriate state such that a tote is present/in process and the tipper is ready/appropriate per the Process Status indicator meanings).
steps.failure_condition: The Process Status indicators do not match the expected green states for sending (e.g., tipper not ready / not in the expected state), or you observe a mismatch after pressing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and do not continue using send/pause controls if the Process Status indicators do not match the expected green states for the intended action.

actions.label: Send right tote to hospital
actions.exact_action: Press the SEND RIGHT TO HOSPITAL button.

steps.title: Pause both tippers
steps.instruction: If you need to pause both tippers, press PAUSE TIPPER.
steps.purpose: Temporarily stop tipper activity when needed.
steps.expected_result: Pressing PAUSE TIPPER pauses both tippers.
steps.healthy_condition: You have verified Process Status indicators are in a state consistent with pausing (and you are not attempting send actions when indicators do not match expected states).
steps.failure_condition: Process Status indicators do not match the expected green states for the intended action, or pausing does not occur as expected.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and do not continue using send/pause controls if the Process Status indicators do not match the expected green states for the intended action.

actions.label: Pause both tippers
actions.exact_action: Press the PAUSE TIPPER button.

title: Reset Heartbeat Stats Data to Zero on the VISU_DATA Screen
summary: Use the Heartbeat section RESET button on the Operator Station HMI VISU_DATA screen to clear the heartbeat timing statistics (Last/Max/Min in milliseconds) back to zero.
when_to_use: When the Operator Station HMI VISU_DATA screen Heartbeat section shows Last/Max/Min heartbeat timing values that you need to reset to zero using the on-screen RESET button.

steps.title: Open the Operator Station HMI and navigate to the VISU_DATA screen
steps.instruction: On the Operator Station HMI, navigate to the VISU_DATA screen (Operator Station HMI Data Screen).
steps.purpose: Get to the screen that contains the Heartbeat section and its RESET button.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_DATA screen is displayed and the Heartbeat section is accessible on the screen.
steps.healthy_condition: The VISU_DATA screen shows the Heartbeat section with Last/Max/Min heartbeat timing values (milliseconds) and a RESET button.
steps.failure_condition: The VISU_DATA screen is not displayed, or the Heartbeat section/RESET button is not visible.

actions.label: Navigate to VISU_DATA
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the "VISU_DATA" screen (Operator Station HMI Data Screen).

steps.title: Locate the Heartbeat section and the RESET button
steps.instruction: On the VISU_DATA screen, locate the "Heartbeat" section and the "RESET" button within that section.
steps.purpose: Identify the correct control used to reset heartbeat timing statistics.
steps.expected_result: You can see the Heartbeat section fields: Last, Max, Min (milliseconds) and the RESET button.
steps.healthy_condition: Heartbeat section shows Last/Max/Min values in milliseconds and a RESET button labeled for resetting the data to zero.
steps.failure_condition: The Heartbeat section fields (Last/Max/Min) or the RESET button are missing or not readable.

actions.label: Find Heartbeat RESET
actions.exact_action: Locate the "Heartbeat" section and the "RESET" button.

steps.title: Press the Heartbeat RESET button to reset the data to zero
steps.instruction: Press the RESET button in the Heartbeat section on the VISU_DATA screen.
steps.purpose: Clear the displayed heartbeat timing statistics back to zero.
steps.expected_result: The Heartbeat Stats values displayed for Last, Max, and Min reset to zero.
steps.healthy_condition: Last, Max, and Min (milliseconds) show reset-to-zero values after pressing RESET.
steps.failure_condition: Last/Max/Min do not reset to zero after pressing RESET.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the Heartbeat Stats values do not reset to zero, stop and escalate for support rather than repeatedly pressing RESET.

actions.label: Reset heartbeat stats
actions.exact_action: Press this button to reset the data to zero.

steps.title: Verify Heartbeat Last/Max/Min values show reset-to-zero
steps.instruction: Verify that the Heartbeat fields (Last, Max, Min in milliseconds) now display zero values.
steps.purpose: Confirm the reset action succeeded on the live HMI display.
steps.expected_result: Last, Max, and Min show zero (reset-to-zero values) on the VISU_DATA screen.
steps.healthy_condition: All three displayed heartbeat timing metrics (Last, Max, Min) are at zero after the reset.
steps.failure_condition: One or more of Last/Max/Min remain non-zero after the reset.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the Heartbeat Stats values do not reset to zero, stop and escalate for support rather than repeatedly pressing RESET.

actions.label: Check Last/Max/Min
actions.exact_action: Verify the Heartbeat fields (Last, Max, Min in milliseconds) show reset-to-zero values as displayed.

title: Reset Operator Stats Data to Zero on the VISU_DATA Screen

steps.title: Open the VISU_DATA screen on the Operator Station HMI

steps.purpose: Get to the screen that contains the Operator Stats section and its DATA RESET button.

steps.healthy_condition: Operator Stats section is visible on VISU_DATA with response-time fields for left and right tippers.

actions.label: Navigate to VISU_DATA

steps.title: Locate the Operator Stats section and DATA RESET button

steps.purpose: Identify the exact control used to reset the operator response-time metrics.

steps.healthy_condition: Operator Stats section shows Resp Time Max (ms), Resp Time Min (ms), and Resp Time Avg (ms) for both left and right tippers, and the DATA RESET button is present.
steps.failure_condition: DATA RESET button is not present/visible in the Operator Stats section.

actions.label: Identify Operator Stats controls
actions.exact_action: Locate the "Operator Stats" section and its "DATA RESET" button

steps.title: Press DATA RESET to reset operator stats to zero

actions.exact_action: Verify the Operator Stats response-time fields (Resp Time Max (ms), Resp Time Min (ms), Resp Time Avg (ms) for left and right) show reset-to-zero values

title: Reset Tipper Stats Data to Zero on the VISU_DATA Screen
summary: The Operator Station HMI VISU_DATA screen includes a Tipper Stats section with a DATA RESET button. Pressing DATA RESET clears the displayed tipper statistics data to zero.
when_to_use: Use when you need to clear the displayed Tipper Stats counters on the Operator Station HMI VISU_DATA screen (e.g., to start a fresh measurement window for Totes Processed, Faults, Avg Cycle Time, Avg Totes/Hour, and Time Starved).

steps.title: Open the Operator Station HMI and navigate to the VISU_DATA screen
steps.instruction: On the Operator Station HMI, navigate to the VISU_DATA screen (Operator Station HMI Data Screen).
steps.purpose: Get to the screen that contains the Tipper Stats section and its DATA RESET button.
steps.expected_result: The VISU_DATA screen is displayed with the Tipper Stats section visible.
steps.healthy_condition: The Tipper Stats section is visible on VISU_DATA, including the displayed tipper statistics fields (e.g., Totes Processed, Faults, Avg Cycle Time, Avg Totes/Hour, Time Starved).
steps.failure_condition: The VISU_DATA screen is not accessible or the Tipper Stats section is not visible.

actions.label: Navigate to VISU_DATA
actions.exact_action: Navigate to the "VISU_DATA" screen (Operator Station HMI Data Screen).

steps.title: Locate the DATA RESET button for the Tipper Stats section
steps.instruction: On the VISU_DATA screen, locate the DATA RESET button within the Tipper Stats section.
steps.purpose: Ensure you press the correct reset control associated with the Tipper Stats counters.
steps.expected_result: You can identify the DATA RESET button associated with the Tipper Stats section.
steps.healthy_condition: The DATA RESET button is visible in the Tipper Stats area on VISU_DATA.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find a DATA RESET button in the Tipper Stats section (or you are unsure which reset button applies to Tipper Stats).
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot clearly identify the DATA RESET button for the Tipper Stats section, stop and escalate for support rather than pressing an incorrect reset control.

actions.label: Find DATA RESET (Tipper Stats)
actions.exact_action: Locate the "DATA RESET" button within the "Tipper Stats" section.

steps.title: Press DATA RESET to reset Tipper Stats to zero

steps.failure_condition: The displayed Tipper Stats values do not reset to zero.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the displayed Tipper Stats values do not reset to zero, stop and escalate for support rather than repeatedly pressing the reset.

steps.title: Verify Tipper Stats values reset to zero

steps.healthy_condition: Totes Processed (left/right), Faults (left/right), Avg Cycle Time, Avg Totes/Hour, and Time Starved display zero values on VISU_DATA.
steps.failure_condition: One or more Tipper Stats fields remain non-zero after pressing DATA RESET.
stop_or_escalate_if: If any Tipper Stats values do not reset to zero, stop and escalate for support.
